title: Cairns Marine Precinct - Common User Facility (CMP-CUF) Co-Investment
description:
The Opportunity:

Ports North is pleased to advise that Request for Proposal (RFP) Phase 1 for the Cairns Marine Precinct - Common User Facility (CMP-CUF) Co-Investment Opportunity has now commenced.

Ports North is proposing the development of the Cairns Marine Precinct – Common User Facility, a major maritime infrastructure project, to expand the marine vessel maintenance capability and capacity in Far North Queensland to support the continued growth of the region’s maritime industry. The proposed facility responds to increasing demand for maritime maintenance, repair, and overhaul services as global vessel fleets expand and age, alongside sustained investment in Australia’s maritime defence capability driving long-term sustainment demand.

Ports North has identified a Finance (co-funded), Design, Build, Operate and Maintain (FDBOM) commercial delivery model as the most efficient means of Project delivery to successfully facilitate achievement of the Project Objectives. As the Project will benefit from a significant contribution of funds from the Queensland and Commonwealth Governments, the physical facilities coming into existence as a result of the Project will be a common user facility available for use by the operator and customers including vessel owners and ship maintenance and repair service providers.

Ports North is seeking a private sector proponent to co-fund, develop, operate and maintain the facility under a long-term arrangement on Ports North-owned land at the Port of Cairns.

This RFP follows the successful completion of an Expression of Interest (EOI) process. Participation in the EOI process was not a prerequisite for participation in RFP Phase 1. Ports North welcomes registrations and proposals from organisations that did not participate in the EOI and may be engaging with the opportunity for the first time.

Purpose of this Request for Proposal:

The purpose of this RFP is to elicit proposals from the market that address the Project Objectives and develop the CMP-CUF, including the following:

•	the co-funding of the Project;

•	the design, construction and commissioning of the CMP-CUF; and

•	the operation and maintenance of the CMP-CUF on a common user basis.

How to Participate in RFP Phase 1:

Proposals are being accepted only via the Ansarada CMP-CUF RFP Phase 1 Data Room. Submissions via this Queensland Procurement Solution may not be eligible.

To participate:

- register online via https://www.portsnorth.com.au/ports-north-projects/cairns-marine-precinct

- Shortly after, Ports North will provide access to the Ansarada CMP-CUF RFP Phase 1 Data Room

- Access the RFP documentation within the CMP-CUF RFP Phase 1 Data Room

- Submit your RFP via the CMP-CUF RFP Phase 1 Data Room prior to 1200 AEST on Friday 18 December 2026.

Enquiries regarding the procurement process may be directed to cmpenquiry@portsnorth.com.au.

Ballina Shire Council is located on the New South Wales Far North Coast, 770 kilometres north of Sydney and 190 kilometres south of Brisbane. The Shire, an area of 484 square kilometres, is set amongst a picturesque rural-coastal landscape and enjoys a temperate to mild subtropical climate.

The Shires resident population is approximately 45,000 with major service centre Ballina servicing the major townships of Alstonville, Lennox Head, Wollongbar, and Wardell. As well as a number of smaller villages and localities including Cumbalum, Teven, Tintenbar and Knockrow.

Ballina Shire Council acknowledges that we are here on the land of the Bundjalung people. The Bundjalung are the traditional owners of this land and are part of the oldest surviving continuous culture in the world.

publicQuestions.question:
1. Drawing E004 states, "Existing communications cable to be preserved and reconnected to the new data rack". Can we assume this cable is the "4 core OS1 Fibre from existing Rack" as shown on Drawing E005. Or does a new Fibre need to be installed?

2. In regards to the Addendum & the Supernatant pump. They state the "Control Panel" needs to be relocated.

 3.Can we confirm they are referring to the circuit breaker only, and not the actual control panel located at the actual pump well (Please see photo attached).
publicQuestions.answer:

title: RFQ for Client-Side ERP Project Manager
description: Barcoo Shire Council invites quotations from suitably qualified and experienced consultants to act as the Client-Side ERP Project Manager and Owner's Representative for the implementation of the Civica Authority Altitude SaaS ERP platform. The successful consultant will provide strategic project leadership, contract management, governance, change management, business process improvement, data migration assurance, testing oversight, and go-live support to ensure a successful ERP implementation and transition. The engagement will run from project mobilisation through implementation, stabilisation, and project closure.

publicQuestions.question:
Council has indicated that the engagement is intended to use a blended delivery model, with purposeful onsite attendance aligned to key project stages rather than a routine weekly attendance commitment.

Would Council be open to a proposed lead consultant being substantially or continuously based in Jundah during the implementation, where the consultant considers this would provide greater accessibility to Council staff and improve delivery?

If so, could Council please advise whether suitable workspace would be available for the consultant at Council premises and whether Council has access to, or could assist with identifying, suitable medium- or long-term accommodation in Jundah?
publicQuestions.answer:
Council is open to a lead consultant being substantially or continuously based in Jundah during the implementation phase where this is considered beneficial to project delivery, stakeholder engagement, and accessibility to Council staff.

Council also has access to accommodation within Jundah and would be willing to make accommodation available to the successful consultant at a subsidised rate, subject to availability and agreement of terms. Further details can be discussed during contract negotiations.

Consultants are encouraged to outline their proposed delivery model, including any onsite presence they consider necessary to achieve the project's objectives.

publicQuestions.question:
1.	Is Council seeking responses from individual consultants, consulting firms, or both?

2.	Is Council seeking a single lead resource, or would a lead consultant supported by specialist resources across change, governance and ERP assurance be viewed favourably?

3.	How would Council balance direct local government ERP implementation experience against broader ERP governance, assurance and client-side delivery experience?

4.	Can Council provide any further guidance regarding the anticipated level of effort or engagement profile for the Client-Side ERP Project Manager and Owner's Representative role across the implementation lifecycle?
publicQuestions.answer:
1.Council welcomes submissions from both individual consultants and consulting firms. Regardless of the delivery model proposed, respondents must demonstrate that they have the capability, capacity, and experience to successfully perform the Client-Side ERP Project Manager and Owner's Representative role throughout the implementation lifecycle. Any proposed support personnel, specialist resources, or subcontractors should be clearly identified in the submission.

2.Council expects a clearly nominated lead consultant who will provide the primary client-side leadership, coordination, governance, and assurance functions for the engagement. However, Council recognises that ERP implementations often require specialist expertise and would welcome a delivery model where the lead consultant is supported by appropriately qualified resources in areas such as change management, governance, business process improvement, reporting, data migration, testing, and ERP assurance. The lead consultant is expected to remain accountable for overall integration, coordination, and delivery outcomes.

3.Council will assess submissions against the evaluation criteria outlined in the RFQ and will consider the overall capability of the proposed team. Direct experience with local government ERP implementations is highly valued due to the importance of statutory compliance, financial management, payroll, rating, asset management, governance, and reporting obligations. However, Council also recognises the value of broader ERP governance, assurance, contract management, change leadership, and client-side delivery experience where respondents can demonstrate successful outcomes in comparable complex enterprise system implementations. Council will evaluate the overall relevance, risk profile, and demonstrated ability to deliver the required outcomes within a small and remote local government environment.

4.Council has deliberately not prescribed a fixed level of effort, attendance pattern, or number of days for this engagement. Respondents are expected to propose a delivery model and resource profile that is aligned with the project objectives, implementation stages, and Council's operational context. Council anticipates that effort levels will vary throughout the project lifecycle, with higher involvement typically required during mobilisation, governance establishment, business process design, data migration activities, testing, organisational readiness, cutover, go-live, and stabilisation periods. Council expects a blended onsite and remote delivery model, with onsite attendance being purposeful and linked to project outcomes rather than a fixed recurring schedule. Respondents should provide a phase-by-phase effort estimate and clearly identify the roles, responsibilities, availability, and anticipated contribution of all proposed resources.

publicQuestions.question: Section 6 of the RFQ is headed "Mandatory capability and experience" and lists ten items. Section 8 sets out five weighted evaluation criteria. Could Council please confirm whether the section 6 items are threshold requirements that a respondent must meet in full for the quotation to be evaluated, or whether they are assessed within the weighted criteria in section 8 so that a response is scored on the strength of its evidence against each item?
publicQuestions.answer:
The capability and experience requirements listed in Section 6 – Mandatory Capability and Experience are intended to establish the minimum capability expected of respondents for this engagement.

Council will initially review submissions to determine whether respondents have adequately demonstrated the required capabilities and relevant experience. Submissions that do not provide sufficient evidence of the mandatory requirements may be excluded from further consideration at Council's discretion.

For submissions that satisfy the mandatory requirements, the strength, relevance, and quality of the respondent's demonstrated experience and proposed approach will then be assessed under the weighted evaluation criteria outlined in Section 8 – Evaluation Criteria.

Accordingly, Section 6 should be viewed as establishing the minimum capability threshold for participation, while Section 8 provides the framework through which Council will comparatively evaluate and score conforming submissions.

Council encourages respondents to provide clear and comprehensive evidence against all mandatory capability and experience requirements, as the quality and relevance of this information will also support assessment under the weighted evaluation criteria.

publicQuestions.question: The first item in section 6 refers to "demonstrated leadership of client-side ERP or major enterprise system implementations of comparable risk and organisational impact". Could Council please confirm whether experience leading the delivery of a major enterprise system from the delivery side, rather than as the client's representative, will be considered against this item, and whether client side leadership of major infrastructure contracts of comparable risk and organisational impact will also be considered?
publicQuestions.answer:
Council's primary objective under this requirement is to assess a respondent's ability to provide effective leadership, governance, risk management, stakeholder coordination, and delivery assurance for a major organisational transformation project.

While direct client-side ERP implementation leadership experience is highly desirable, Council will also consider experience gained from leading the delivery of major enterprise system implementations from the vendor, systems integrator, or delivery side where the respondent can clearly demonstrate responsibility for project leadership, governance, stakeholder management, risk management, and successful implementation outcomes.

Similarly, Council will consider client-side leadership experience on major infrastructure, capital works, or organisational transformation projects of comparable complexity, risk profile, stakeholder environment, and organisational impact. However, respondents should clearly demonstrate how their experience is transferable to an ERP implementation environment, particularly in relation to governance, change management, business transformation, assurance, and executive stakeholder engagement.

Council will assess the relevance, complexity, and demonstrated outcomes of the respondent's experience, with greater weighting generally afforded to experience that most closely aligns with the scope, responsibilities, and objectives of the Client-Side ERP Project Manager and Owner's Representative role.

publicQuestions.question: The RFQ cover states a closing date and time of 9 October 2026 at 5:00 pm. The VendorPanel listing for this request shows a close of 6:00 PM on the same day. Could Council please confirm which closing time applies?
publicQuestions.answer:
Council confirms that the official closing time for submissions is 6:00 PM on 9 October 2026 as displayed in VendorPanel.

The RFQ documentation references 5:00 PM; however, the additional one-hour period has been intentionally allowed to provide respondents with sufficient time to address any unforeseen technical or system issues that may arise during the submission process.

Accordingly, respondents may submit their quotations up until 6:00 PM on 9 October 2026 through VendorPanel. Council strongly encourages respondents not to leave submissions until the final hour and to allow adequate time for uploading and lodgement.

publicQuestions.question: Section 7.1 asks for an estimated number of days or hours and a professional fee for each work package. Could Council please confirm (a) whether a schedule of hourly rates by role, applied to the estimated hours for each work package, is an acceptable basis for the pricing schedule, and (b) how the "Optional specialist services" line should be priced where the need for those services is not known at quotation stage, for example as an indicative rate only or as a provisional sum?
publicQuestions.answer:
(a) Council confirms that respondents may use a pricing schedule based on hourly or daily rates by role, together with the estimated hours or days proposed for each work package. Respondents should clearly identify the proposed resources, applicable rates, estimated effort, and total professional fee for each work package. This approach will assist Council in understanding the proposed resourcing methodology and evaluating value for money.

(b) With respect to Optional Specialist Services, Council acknowledges that the requirement for such services may not be fully known at the quotation stage. Accordingly, respondents may provide indicative hourly or daily rates for specialist resources and, where appropriate, an estimated level of effort based on reasonable assumptions. If respondents consider it appropriate, Optional Specialist Services may also be presented as a provisional allowance, provided the pricing methodology and assumptions are clearly explained.

Council's preference is that respondents provide sufficient pricing transparency to enable evaluation while recognising that the scope and timing of any optional specialist services will ultimately be subject to Council's approval and agreement at the time such services are required.

publicQuestions.question:
Could Council please clarify the scope of data migration services already included within Civica's implementation engagement?

In particular, does Civica's contracted implementation scope include the technical migration activities required to move data from Practical Plus to Authority Altitude, including extraction/transformation/loading and execution of the migration?

If so, could Council please indicate the principal data migration activities that remain Council's responsibility, for example data cleansing, validation, reconciliation and acceptance?

This clarification would assist respondents in estimating the appropriate client-side effort and avoiding duplication of services already being provided by Civica.
publicQuestions.answer:
Council confirms that the implementation contract with Civica includes delivery of the system implementation services, including migration activities required to transition data from Practical Plus to Authority Altitude. As outlined in the RFQ, Civica is responsible for delivering the contracted migration activities and technical reconciliation associated with the implementation.

The Client-Side ERP Project Manager and Owner's Representative sought through this RFQ is not expected to undertake Civica's technical migration responsibilities. Rather, the role is to provide client-side leadership, coordination, oversight and assurance across the migration workstream.

Consistent with Sections 2.7 and 5 of the RFQ, Council will retain ownership of its data, including data cleansing, validation, reconciliation and business sign-off activities. The successful consultant will be expected to coordinate planning and accountability, review migration evidence, support data governance arrangements, monitor migration progress and risks, and provide assurance that migration activities are being appropriately managed by the responsible parties.

Respondents should therefore allow for a client-side governance, coordination and assurance role in relation to data migration rather than hands-on delivery of technical extraction, transformation, loading (ETL) or migration execution services. Any need for specialist technical migration services beyond Civica's contracted scope would be assessed separately by Council if required.

publicQuestions.question: Would the council consider a response by an organisation rather then an individual for this tender?
publicQuestions.answer: Yes, Council will consider responses from organisations as well as individual consultants, provided the respondent clearly identifies a nominated lead consultant who will be responsible for delivering the client-side leadership, integration, coordination and assurance functions outlined in the RFQ. Any supporting personnel, specialist resources, and their respective roles should also be clearly identified in the submission.

publicQuestions.question:
Q1. Can Council confirm the Functional Scope for the project and that the following modules are included in scope.

 - Finance and Supply Chain

 - HR and Payroll

 - Property, Rates, Development Applications, Licences and Compliance Management

 - CRM and On-line services

 - Assets, Maintenance Management and field mobility

 - Document Management

Q2. Can Council please provide the following information:

 - Total number of Rating Assessments

 - Number of indoor staff (FTE)

 - Number of outdoor staff (FTE)

 - Organisation structure
publicQuestions.answer:
Q1.

Council confirms that the ERP replacement project is intended to deliver an integrated enterprise platform across Council's core business functions. Based on Council's current understanding of the required solution, the following functional areas are expected to be within scope of the implementation program:

Finance and Supply Chain

Human Resources and Payroll

Property, Rates, Development Applications, Licences and Compliance Management

Customer Relationship Management (CRM) and Online Services

Asset Management, Maintenance Management and Field Mobility

Document and Records Management

The purpose of this RFQ is to engage a client-side Project Manager to support Council through the implementation of the selected ERP solution and associated business transformation activities. Respondents should therefore assume that the above functional areas form part of the broader ERP program and scope their services accordingly.

Q2.

Council can provide the following indicative information for the purpose of this procurement:

Total Rating Assessments: Approximately 500

Indoor Staff (FTE): Approximately 20

Outdoor Staff (FTE): Approximately 33

Organisation Structure: Refer council web site.

publicQuestions.question:
Onsite vs. Remote Requirements: Can this engagement be delivered fully remotely, or is a specific on-site presence expected in Jundah, Stonehenge, and Windorah?

Team Structure & Resourcing: Is the council looking for a single dedicated Project Manager, or is a core lead supported by specialist team members (e.g., change management or testing support) acceptable?

Civica Experience Weighting: While our team brings extensive local government ERP project management and change management expertise, will direct experience with Civica Authority Altitude be evaluated as a strict requirement or a preferred capability?

Project Governance & Go-Live Timeline: What is the targeted start date for the Project Manager, and is there an established go-live deadline for the Altitude rollout?
publicQuestions.answer:
Q1.

The engagement is expected to be delivered through a blended onsite and remote model. However, Council places significant importance on onsite attendance in Jundah during critical project phases, including mobilisation, business process workshops, data migration activities, change readiness assessments, user acceptance testing, and go-live activities. Respondents should propose a purposeful onsite engagement plan linked to project outcomes rather than a generic attendance schedule. Onsite presence is expected during final cutover and go-live activities unless otherwise agreed by Council.

Q2.

Council's preference is for a clearly identified lead ERP Project Manager who will provide client-side leadership, integration, coordination and assurance throughout the engagement. Support from specialist resources may be proposed where beneficial, provided the lead consultant remains the primary point of accountability and continuity throughout the project.

Q3.

Direct experience managing Civica Authority Altitude implementations will be viewed favourably. However, Council's mandatory requirements focus on demonstrated experience leading ERP or major enterprise system implementations of similar complexity, together with contract management, change management, process improvement, data migration, testing and organisational readiness capabilities.

Q4.

Council's current planning position is to finalise contracts and commence mobilisation in late 2026. The current vendor contract identifies 1 December 2027 as the proposed contractual go-live milestone, with Council's objective being for the new Civica Authority Altitude platform to be fully operational and successfully implemented by 28 February 2028.

title: Drainage Improvements - Farnsworth and View Street - Castlemaine
description:
Mount Alexander Shire Council (MASC) is committed to upgrading, maintaining and rehabilitating infrastructure in an efficient and timely manner. The existing drainage network contains both overland and piped stormwater drainage.

In 2022 Mount Alexander Shire experienced heavy rainfall resulting in localised flash flooding throughout the shire, with many areas identified for improved drainage.

The storm water catchment in Farnsworth Street is initially captured by the underground drainage network before it then outfalls via an overland flow path towards View Street/Forest Street.

The objective of this construction project is to improve the underground storm water connection along a section of Farnsworth Street, View Street and Forest Street. Drainage designs have been completed for the drainage connection and kerb construction.

title: Whitsunday Regional Sports Precinct Stage 1 - Design and Construction
description:
The Whitsunday Regional Council (Principal) is delivering the Whitsunday Regional Sports Precinct (WRSP) to address the increasing demand for high-quality sporting, recreation and community infrastructure across the Whitsunday Region.

The WRSP is one of Council's most significant community infrastructure investments and will provide a contemporary regional sporting destination that supports organised sport, community participation, recreation, health and wellbeing, regional events and long-term population growth. The precinct has been planned to meet current community needs while providing a scalable framework for future expansion through subsequent stages of development.

Stage 1 represents the first phase of the Master Plan and will establish the core sporting facilities, supporting infrastructure and services required to enable the precinct to operate as a high-quality regional sports hub. The completed works are intended to provide durable, functional and maintainable infrastructure that delivers value for money over the life of the asset while supporting a broad range of community users.

This Principal's Project Requirements (PPR) defines the minimum functional, operational, technical and performance requirements for the Project. It establishes the outcomes that the Contractor is required to achieve and forms the basis upon which the Contractor will develop, coordinate, design, construct, commission and hand over the Works.

The Works will be delivered under an AS 4300–1995 Design and Construct Contract, under which the Contractor will assume full responsibility for the detailed design, design coordination, statutory approvals, construction, commissioning, testing and handover of the completed facility, except where expressly stated otherwise in the Contract.

This Project is funded under the Australian Government Growing Regions Program. In accordance with the Project Funding Agreement, the Head Contractor must hold and maintain current accreditation under the Australian Government Work Health and Safety Accreditation Scheme (the Scheme) for the entirety of the Contract.

Tenderers must:

a)	hold current accreditation under the Australian Government Work Health and Safety Accreditation Scheme at the Tender Closing Time;

b)	provide evidence of current accreditation with their Tender submission;

c)	maintain accreditation for the duration of the Contract, including any extensions of time or defects liability period where accreditation is required to remain in force; and

d)	immediately notify the Principal of any actual or proposed suspension, lapse, cancellation or variation to their accreditation status.

A non-mandatory Tender Site Briefing will be held on Tuesday, 6 October 2026, 1.30 pm (AEST). The location of the meeting will commence at Proserpine Administration Building, 83-85 Main Street, Proserpine Qld 4800 and will progress to the Site Visit at Shute Harbour Road and Brandy Creek Road. Access to the Site is adjacent to the bus stop pair refer to the Conditions of Tender clause 7 for a map for parking at the Site.

N.B. PPE is a requirement to attend this site, at a minimum Hi-Vis long-sleeved shirt, full length pants, steel cap boots and eye protection, it is also recommended to wear sun protection.

Please confirm your attendance at this meeting via contracts@whitsundayrc.qld.gov.au no later than midday, Thursday, 1 October 2026.

All communications must go through the VendorPanel communications forum.

publicQuestions.question:
1.	Pavement Types

Can EGSC please confirm or clarify the Pavement Types for the Taxiway;

Concrete Aprons = Pavement Type 1

Taxiway (Light Grey) = Pavement Type 2

Taxiway Shoulder (Double Diagonal Hatched) = Pavement Type 3
publicQuestions.answer:
On the part-complete drawings, Concrete Aprons = Pavement Type 1, Taxiway (Light Grey) = Pavement Type 2,

Taxiway Shoulder (Double Diagonal Hatched) = Pavement Type 3.

Part-complete drawings are provided for information only. Pavement type shown on these drawings are not the approved pavement type under contract CON2027 1790. Pavement design is part of the Contractor's scope of works under contract CON2027 1790.

publicQuestions.question:
Good afternoon,

1. Can Council confirm if the aircraft traffic mix nominated in section 6 of the PPR is to be adopted for the design of all pavements or if a reduced number of B360 and AT802 can be adopted for Code A section of Taxiway C/C3? Can Council also confirm if a loaded AT802 is to be considered in the design mix?

2. Can Council confirm if the preference is for a spray seal or asphalt wearing surface? Section 5 of the PPR nominates a two-coast spray seal however the previous design was asphalt?
publicQuestions.answer:
1. B360 will generally not use the code A section of Taxiway C/C3 unless the Air Ambulance Apron is at full capacity or closed for works. A reduced number of 100 annual departure can be adopted for B360 for the code A section of Taxiway C/C3. AT802 uses the code A section of Taxiway C/C3 so a reduced number of AT802 cannot be adopted for the code A section of Taxiway C/C3, numbers for this aircraft type remains the same for the full length of taxiway.

AT802 will generally use Taxiway C/C3 unloaded. However, to ensure that the pavement design caters for events such as Black Summer, a loaded AT802 is to be considered in the design mix.

2. Preference is for a two-coat spray seal wearing course.

publicQuestions.question:
PPR Section 7 – Operational Requirements

#1, states that Taxiway C/C3 and apron remain operational during the day throughout the works; operations may be suspended for intersection works as per the minimal outage window accepted pre-possession of site; Taxiway C/C3 and apron closed at night (7pm-7am) throughout the works; Air Ambulance operates out of Terminal Building apron during night hours.

Can EGSC please provide details of the minimal outage window referred to above and clarify the Taxiway Works are expected to be performed at night between 7pm to 7am as indicated and confirm acceptance that Taxiway will be reopened daily on the basis of an unsealed pavement and not a finished design level.
publicQuestions.answer:
The taxiway works are not expected to be performed at night. Taxiway works are expected to be performed during daylight hours. Council anticipates that the taxiway will be closed during night hours as it will not be monitored by an ARO/WSO.

The Contractor will minimise impact to emergency services through the methodology and staging of the works. Council has not nominated a minimal outage window. As part of the pre-possession of site requirements, the Contractor will submit for acceptance an outage window and demonstrate that this outage window has been minimised. Methodology, staging and proposed outage window also form part of the tender submission.

publicQuestions.question:
Scope of Works Contractor (Design and Construct) Ref: 12203_ Taxiway C/C3 Apron_PMF-T-DCSOW-001

Section 5.2 Project Specific Project Constraints, can EGSC confirm the seasonal weather windows for sprayed sealed and/or asphalt.
publicQuestions.answer: The Contractor is responsible for programming sealing and/or asphalting works in favourable weather conditions prior to the Practical Completion date set by the grant funding requirements.

publicQuestions.question:
PPR Section 5 – Performance/Output Requirements

#10 Perimeter Fencing, Can EGSC confirm Perimeter fencing is required for Taxiway Package of Works, and if so, provide a plan/layout of the general location.
publicQuestions.answer: Modification to airside fencing will be based on the requirement for the taxiway strip to be free of fixed objects.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi

Respectfully we would like to request an extension to the closing date.

Given the complexities of this project and the requirements for design we would like to request a 3-week extension.

Thanks
publicQuestions.answer: Thank you for your request. Unfortunately, we are unable to grant an extension to the closing date due to our project timelines. We appreciate your understanding and look forward to receiving your submission.

publicQuestions.question: For the Taxiway C/C3 and Apron Upgrade Package (SP2), please confirm whether the existing concrete apron adjacent to the northern hangar facilities forms part of the project scope.
publicQuestions.answer: No, the existing concrete apron adjacent to the northern hangar facilities does not form part of the project scope. However, localised works may be required in this area to achieve a compliant Taxiway C/C3.

publicQuestions.question:
The tender documentation has been reviewed for aircraft tie-down requirements within the upgraded apron area.

Please confirm whether new aircraft tie-down facilities are required as part of the project scope. If required, please provide the quantity, location, design criteria and any applicable standards or operational requirements to be adopted during design.
publicQuestions.answer: As part of the project, the existing tie-down facilities need to be removed, and new aircraft tie-down facilities need to be installed. All aircraft parking bays need to be equipped with three-point tiedowns capable of securing up to light twin-engine aircraft.

title: Landfill Gas Capture and Flaring System
description:
Livingstone Shire Council is seeking proposals from suitably qualified and experienced organisations to provide a commercial solution for the financing, design, approval, construction, commissioning, operation and maintenance of a Landfill Gas (LFG) Capture and Flaring System at the Yeppoon Landfill. The proposed solution must safely capture and control landfill gas, provide reliable flaring infrastructure, meet applicable environmental and regulatory requirements, and accommodate potential future landfill gas-to-energy or cogeneration opportunities.

Council is seeking a commercial partnership model under which the successful Respondent will be responsible for the delivery and ongoing operation of the system, including all labour, plant, equipment, approvals, monitoring, reporting, maintenance and associated services necessary to achieve the required performance outcomes. Respondents may also propose innovative approaches that improve environmental, operational or commercial outcomes for Council.

Location of Services

 The works and services will be undertaken at Yeppoon Landfill, Livingstone Shire, Queensland. Site inspections will be available during the procurement process. While some design, engineering, monitoring and reporting activities may be undertaken remotely, the successful Respondent must be capable of delivering and supporting on-site operations, maintenance and incident response services throughout the contract term.

Expected Timing

Council's anticipated procurement timetable is:

RFP issued: 27 August 2026

Optional site inspection: 16 September 2026

Questions close: 28 September 2026

RFP closes: 5 October 2026

Key Outcomes Sought

- Capture and control landfill gas in accordance with environmental, safety and regulatory requirements.

- Reliably flare landfill gas to achieve methane destruction and odour control.

- Establish infrastructure capable of supporting future landfill gas-to-energy, cogeneration or other beneficial gas utilisation opportunities.

- Deliver measurable and ongoing commercial returns to Council through a revenue-sharing arrangement.

- Maintain safe, compliant and continuous operation of the landfill gas capture and flaring system throughout the contract term

This Request for Proposal seeks responses from organisations with demonstrated experience in landfill gas capture, landfill gas flaring, landfill gas-to-energy projects and related environmental infrastructure services. Council welcomes innovative and commercially sustainable solutions that support environmental compliance, risk management and long-term value for the community.

publicQuestions.answer:
Question 1

Can Council provide any previous environmental monitoring reports, even if limited, that may indicate methane trends or historical gas behaviour?

Response

Council undertakes quarterly landfill gas monitoring using perimeter monitoring bores located outside the landfill footprint. Monitoring to date has not identified evidence of landfill gas migration beyond the landfill boundary.

Question 2

Are there any recent waste acceptance records, filling rates, or cell development plans that would help inform gas generation modelling?

Response

Waste disposal data for the previous five financial years has been provided in Attachment 1 to Addendum No. 1. Based on current operational assumptions and airspace consumption forecasts, Council estimates that the current operating landfill cell (Cell 2B) has approximately three years of remaining capacity before final capping. Construction of Cell 3A is currently underway and will provide the next stage of landfill development. No additional landfill gas generation modelling information is available.

Question 3

Can Council confirm whether any previous gas wells, passive vents, or trial flaring systems exist on site?

Response

Council confirms that no landfill gas wells, passive gas vents or trial flaring systems currently exist, or are known to have previously existed, at the site.

Landfill Operational Interface

Question 4

Will Council provide topographical surveys, cap thickness information, or geotechnical data for drilling and well installation planning?

Response

Available cell construction information and topographical survey data will be made available to the preferred tenderer.

Question 5

Can Council provide a current landfill operations plan, including active tipping areas, future cell development timelines, and rehabilitation schedules?

Response

A recent aerial photograph of the landfill site showing the current landfill operational area, active cell locations and future landfill development areas has been provided as Attachment 6 - Aerial Photograph of Current Landfill Site Operations. Council estimates that the current operating landfill cell (Cell 2B) has approximately three years of remaining capacity before final capping. Construction of Cell 3A is currently underway and will provide the next stage of landfill development. No additional landfill operations plans or rehabilitation schedules will be provided as part of this procurement process.

Question 6

What are the site access constraints, including operating hours, traffic management requirements and heavy vehicle movement restrictions?

Response

The landfill operates from 7:00 am to 5:00 pm daily, excluding Christmas Day and Good Friday.

Council is not currently aware of any site-specific traffic management or heavy vehicle movement restrictions that would be expected to materially affect the proposed works. All vehicles entering and leaving the site are required to pass through the weighbridge in accordance with normal landfill operating procedures.

Question 7

Will Council provide laydown areas for materials, flare compound construction and temporary works?

Response

Yes. Council will make suitable areas available for laydown, flare compound construction and temporary works associated with the delivery of the project. The location and extent of such areas will be agreed with the successful contractor.

Question 8

Are there any noise, dust or odour management requirements that may affect drilling or flare installation activities?

Response

The contractor will be required to undertake all works in accordance with applicable legislative requirements and the site's Environmental Authority, including requirements relating to dust and odour management.

The current Environmental Authority is available through the Queensland Government Environmental Authority Register (Environmental Authority No. EPPR01823814).

Approvals and Regulatory Requirements

Question 9

Can Council confirm whether the existing Environmental Authority includes landfill gas capture and flaring activities, or whether an amendment to the Environmental Authority will be required?

Response

Council is currently considering the approval pathway that may be required to support landfill gas capture and flaring activities. Tenderers should make their own enquiries regarding any approvals relevant to their proposed solution.

The current Environmental Authority (EPPR01823814) was referenced in Addendum No. 1 and is publicly available through the Queensland Government Environmental Authority Register. Tenderers should make their own enquiries regarding approval requirements relevant to their proposed solution.

Question 10

Will Council assist with local government planning approvals, or is the contractor expected to manage all submissions independently?

Response

Council will provide reasonable assistance throughout approval processes where required. However, approval applications and supporting documentation will need to be prepared and submitted through the applicable statutory processes.

Question 11

Are there any heritage, cultural or ecological constraints applicable to the proposed flare compound location?

Response

Council has not identified any known heritage, cultural or ecological constraints affecting the proposed flare compound location. However, tenderers remain responsible for satisfying themselves as to site conditions and constraints relevant to their proposed solution.

Tenderers remain responsible for undertaking their own investigations and satisfying themselves as to site conditions and constraints relevant to their proposed solution.

Future Gas-to-Energy Requirements

Question 12

Does Council have a preferred cogeneration technology (for example, reciprocating engine or microturbine)?

Response

No. Council does not have a preferred cogeneration technology.

Question 13

Has Council engaged with energy authorities regarding potential grid connection feasibility or constraints?

Response

No. Council has not undertaken discussions regarding grid connection feasibility or associated network constraints.

Question 14

Does Council expect tenderers to include preliminary gas-to-energy feasibility modelling within their proposal?

Response

No. Preliminary gas-to-energy feasibility modelling is not required as part of the proposal submission.

Performance Requirements and Reporting

Question 15

Can Council confirm the required methane destruction efficiency?

Response

Tenderers should nominate the methane destruction efficiency associated with their proposed solution and provide supporting information within their proposal.

Question 16

Does Council require real-time SCADA access, or will periodic data reporting be sufficient?

Response

Council does not require real-time SCADA access. Periodic reporting and data export functionality will be sufficient.

Question 17

Are there any specific KPIs Council intends to include in the contract?

Response

Performance measures and key performance indicators will be negotiated with the successful tenderer as part of contract finalisation.

Risk Allocation and Contractual Matters

Question 18

Will Council provide a draft contract before submission, or only after evaluation?

Response

Council intends to work collaboratively with shortlisted tenderers during the evaluation phase to negotiate and develop mutually acceptable contractual arrangements.

Question 19

Can Council clarify the proposed allocation of risk relating to force majeure events, landfill operational changes, gas generation variability and regulatory changes?

Response

Risk allocation and associated contractual mechanisms will form part of contract discussions and negotiations with shortlisted tenderers during the evaluation phase.

Question 20

Does Council require performance bonds, parent company guarantees or other financial securities?

Response

Financial security requirements, if applicable, will be determined having regard to the proposed solution, project delivery methodology and risk profile, and will be discussed with shortlisted tenderers during the evaluation phase.

Livingstone Shire Council is seeking proposals from suitably qualified and experienced organisations to provide a commercial solution for the financing, design, approval, construction, commissioning, operation and maintenance of a Landfill Gas (LFG) Capture and Flaring System at the Yeppoon Landfill. The proposed solution must safely capture and control landfill gas, provide reliable flaring infrastructure, meet applicable environmental and regulatory requirements, and accommodate potential future landfill gas-to-energy or cogeneration opportunities.

Council is seeking a commercial partnership model under which the successful Respondent will be responsible for the delivery and ongoing operation of the system, including all labour, plant, equipment, approvals, monitoring, reporting, maintenance and associated services necessary to achieve the required performance outcomes. Respondents may also propose innovative approaches that improve environmental, operational or commercial outcomes for Council.

Location of Services

 The works and services will be undertaken at Yeppoon Landfill, Livingstone Shire, Queensland. Site inspections will be available during the procurement process. While some design, engineering, monitoring and reporting activities may be undertaken remotely, the successful Respondent must be capable of delivering and supporting on-site operations, maintenance and incident response services throughout the contract term.

Expected Timing

Council's anticipated procurement timetable is:

RFP issued: 27 August 2026

Optional site inspection: 16 September 2026

Questions close: 28 September 2026

RFP closes: 5 October 2026

Key Outcomes Sought

- Capture and control landfill gas in accordance with environmental, safety and regulatory requirements.

- Reliably flare landfill gas to achieve methane destruction and odour control.

- Establish infrastructure capable of supporting future landfill gas-to-energy, cogeneration or other beneficial gas utilisation opportunities.

- Deliver measurable and ongoing commercial returns to Council through a revenue-sharing arrangement.

- Maintain safe, compliant and continuous operation of the landfill gas capture and flaring system throughout the contract term

This Request for Proposal seeks responses from organisations with demonstrated experience in landfill gas capture, landfill gas flaring, landfill gas-to-energy projects and related environmental infrastructure services. Council welcomes innovative and commercially sustainable solutions that support environmental compliance, risk management and long-term value for the community.

title: FAIR Support and Maintenance
description:
Queensland Treasury (Customer) is seeking submissions from suitably qualified suppliers to provide ongoing support, maintenance, managed services and development services for the Financial Assurance Information Registry (FAIR).

FAIR is a business-critical application built on the Appian low-code enterprise platform. The system supports the administration of the Queensland Government's Financial Provisioning Scheme and integrates with external agency systems and Treasury's SAP financial management system.

The required services include:

•	Tier 1 to Tier 4 application support and incident management.

•	Monitoring and resolution of system issues and errors.

•	Appian platform and environment support, including upgrades and liaison with Appian.

•	Ongoing application development and enhancements (approximately eight development days per month).

•	Management of code releases across environments and support for production deployments.

•	Testing and quality assurance activities associated with support and development services.

•	Support for system integrations and participation in inter-agency governance and operational meetings.

Suppliers must demonstrate significant experience providing support and development services for Appian-based solutions. Experience supporting government enterprise applications and complex system integrations will be highly regarded.

This procurement will establish a contract for the ongoing provision of FAIR support, maintenance and development services.

title: Expression of Interest (EOI) for Asbestos and hazardous materials management Services
description:
Energy Queensland is seeking Expressions of Interest (EOI) from suitably qualified and experienced Occupational Hygienist service providers to support the management of asbestos and hazardous materials across its portfolio of sites and assets. The successful provider will undertake asbestos surveys, inspections, assessments, risk evaluations, air monitoring, removal clearances and desktop reviews where appropriate and agreed. Providers will be responsible for delivering professional advice, exercising independent technical judgement, and maintaining accountability for all findings, risk ratings and recommendations associated with asbestos management activities.

The appointed Hygienist will be required to undertake all activities necessary to complete assigned work packages, including sampling, air monitoring, engagement of NATA accredited laboratory analysis services, report preparation, delivery and publication. The provider must maintain all necessary licences, competencies, accreditations, insurances and relevant asbestos assessment qualifications. In addition, the successful respondent will be expected to provide guidance and recommendations to Energy Queensland regarding the safe and effective management of asbestos risks, while ensuring compliance with applicable legislation, codes of practice, workplace health and safety requirements and Energy Queensland procedures.

A key requirement of this engagement is the ability to work within an established digital asbestos management environment provided by Energy Queensland's Data Service Provider. The platform serves as the single source of truth for asbestos and hazardous materials information and supports surveys, inspections, re-inspections, clearances, reporting and asbestos register management. Respondents must demonstrate experience using online asbestos management systems and be capable of capturing, maintaining and updating accurate asbestos records through mobile and desktop applications. The Hygienist will be required to utilise the platform to access site information, manage work activities, update asbestos registers, generate documentation and provide relevant asbestos information to personnel who require access to current site-based asbestos data.

The intent of this EOI is to test the market and identify capable Asbestos Auditing Program service providers willing to participate in a Request For Tender (RFT) via SAP Ariba.

How to Register Your Interest:

1.	Email the Contact Officer: philip.leyden@energyq.com.au

2.	The email subject heading should contain the event title: Asbestos Auditing Program

The email should contain the following:

•	Express your interest by providing a summary or your organisation including a capability statement

•	Advise if Supplier is already registered in Energy Queensland’s realm in SAP Ariba. If not, EQL will require

o	Business legal entity name (as displayed in the ABN lookup)

o	ABN

o	Registered Business Street address

o	Contact name.

o	Contact phone number.

o	Contact email address.

Please note:

Suppliers are encouraged to read all relevant documentation located at https://www.energyq.com.au/suppliers

All queries are to be directed to Philip Leyden philip.leyden@energyq.com.au

publicQuestions.question:
BSC 26/27 – T21 – Supply and Deliver Dual Cab 4WD Utilities (Four)

As a multi-franchise dealer group, we have reviewed the specification against the current Australian new-vehicle market. The combination of an OEM approved GVM above 4,200kg, a 5-star ANCAP rating and net power of 150kW or more narrows the field considerably. To make sure our response meets Council's intent, could Council please clarify:

1. Is Council expecting or seeking a specific vehicle or model with this specification? If so, can Council confirm this so respondents can be sure they are quoting what Council has in mind?

2. To our knowledge, no new dual cab 4WD currently available in Australia meets every element of the specification exactly (OEM approved GVM above 4,200kg, 5-star ANCAP rating and 150kW or more). Are all three requirements mandatory, or would Council consider a vehicle that meets the GVM and power requirements but does not hold a 5-star ANCAP rating? Could Council also advise the operational driver behind the GVM requirement (e.g. payload, towing or licensing)?

3. The specification asks suppliers to nominate weeks to delivery. Does Council have a required delivery date or window, and will the nominated delivery time be assessed as part of the evaluation? Would staged delivery of the four vehicles be acceptable?

4. Is the noise compliance test report required for each vehicle supplied, or would a report for a representative vehicle of the same make and model be accepted? Would a manufacturer's test report be acceptable?

5. The specification calls for a steel tray with fold-down sides but does not state dimensions. Can Council advise the required tray length and width, or confirm the manufacturer's standard tray size is acceptable?

Thank you.
publicQuestions.answer:
1. Council is seeking a vehicle that meets the specifications.

2. All three are required and the driver behind the GVM is the vehicle’s ability to carry operational loads.

3. Suppliers are asked to nominate a delivery timeframe. All four vehicles should be delivered in that timeframe.

4. A report for a representative model will suffice.

5.Manufacturers standard tray size.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
The extreme weather events associated with the 1012/1025 disaster declarations resulted in slope instability and embankment failures of the local road network. These impacts have affected asset condition and functionality, reduced levels of service and, in some locations, created ongoing risks to road users and surrounding infrastructure.

Funding has been approved under the DRFA program to restore eligible public assets that were directly damaged by the disaster events. The principal objective of the DRFA funding is to assist local government in reinstating essential public infrastructure to the condition and level of service that existed immediately prior to the disaster.

Accordingly, the proposed remediation works are intended to restore the damaged NVC assets to their pre-disaster function, serviceability and operational performance, in accordance with DRFA eligibility requirements. The works do not include asset upgrades, increased capacity or betterment initiatives unless separately approved under the relevant DRFA provisions.

The remediation program comprises a range of geotechnical and civil engineering treatments tailored to site-specific conditions and failure mechanisms. Proposed works may include retaining structures, slope stabilisation measures, drainage improvements, erosion protection works, pavement reconstruction and other associated activities necessary to achieve a durable and compliant restoration outcome.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi,

Please see our request for information below -

A. In light of the decision to replace the TEMA PLC processor with a CJ3 PLC, we request Council consider descoping all works associated with the TEMA PLC Upgrade to allow for re-design and tendering of this portion of works at a future date. We believe this approach would ultimately deliver a more cost-effective outcome for Council. We do not require an extension of time to accommodate this significant change.

If the TEMA PLC upgrade is to remain within scope, can Council please confirm:

Is pricing still required for works per the IFC design of the TEMA PLC upgrade using the NJ processor? Or is this design now considered redundant?

We note the minimal effort required for electrical design given the mature state of the IFC design but recognise the significant engineering effort in migrating the existing PLC software to a new range. We also note the complexity of cutover between two ranges of hardware on an operating plant with a maximum 6hr shutdown window.

Is pricing now required for works per the minutes that a CJ3 processor is now to be used?

We note this would require a fresh electrical design of the hardware upgrade, negating the existing IFC design, but agree that there would be significant engineering savings in maintaining the existing PLC software on the CJ3 architecture. We also note the complexity of cutover will be reduced if the use of adaptor wiring kits are used to significantly reduce the re-wiring required. We also note the product is now scheduled for release Oct 2026. To-date OMRON have not been in a position to provide pricing or lead times on this product, but remain hopeful of providing prior to tender close.

If both pricing options are required, please confirm the format of response required.

 B. Could not locate the following tender documents -

5.2.d

5.2.a

5.2.e

 C. Can FCRC/KBR please:

Confirm Total cut and fill volumes (m³) for the bulk earthworks

Provide The 12d Model files /CAD files for the existing and design surfaces.

 D. Pensar acknowledges Council's position that no extensions will be granted. However, following feedback from our key suppliers and subcontractors, we respectfully request an extension of three (3)

weeks, from 15/10/26 to 05/11/26.

Several suppliers, notably for the switchboards, have advised that they cannot provide firm pricing within the current period. An extension would allow a more accurate tender.
publicQuestions.answer: Please refer to Addendum #3

publicQuestions.question:

This would help us identify the attending contractors and provide relevant equipment information and pricing for their tender submissions.

If the full attendance sheet cannot be released, a list of the companies represented would be appreciated.
publicQuestions.answer: Please refer to Addendum #3

publicQuestions.answer: Please refer to Addendum #5

title: Tender for land within the Lansdown Eco-Industrial Precinct
description:
The Lansdown Eco-Industrial Precinct (LEIP or Precinct) is positioned as a major industrial precinct for environmentally responsible advanced manufacturing, technology and processing activities. The Precinct is located approximately 40 kilometres south of the Townsville central business district in the suburb of Calcium and comprises approximately 2,200 hectares extending east from the Mingela State Forest and Lansdown Creek towards the Flinders Highway. Townsville City Council (Council) acquired the land in 2001 after its previous use by the Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation as a pasture research site.

LEIP is supported by strategic access to the Port of Townsville, major road and rail corridors, the North Queensland Gas Pipeline, the Woodstock Ergon Substation and planned industrial water infrastructure. Since 2019, Council has undertaken several open market processes for land within the Precinct. Those processes resulted in conditional land allocations across advanced manufacturing, energy, critical minerals, storage, chemical processing and related projects. This refreshed market land tender considers remaining available land with the LEIP.

publicQuestions.question:
The RFQ refers to assessment of Council’s “nominated sealed roads”. However, the supplied BSC_RD_PAVE.zip GIS layer has a total measured line length of approximately 1,725.980 km, with incomplete sealed-road classifications and features including State roads, shoulders, car parks and a cycleway.

Could Council please confirm:

1. Whether the entire supplied GIS layer is to be surveyed, or only a nominated sealed-road subset. If a subset, please provide the applicable road/segment IDs or a filtered GIS layer and confirm the total network length.

2. Whether State roads and the ancillary features listed above are included.

3. Whether roughness measurements are required in both travel directions, and whether any additional lanes require separate survey passes.

This clarification will enable us to establish the survey quantity, price and delivery program.
publicQuestions.answer:
Hi Alastair

Thank you for your enquiry. Please refer to the responses below.

1. Whether the entire supplied GIS layer is to be surveyed, or only a nominated sealed-road subset. If a subset, please provide the applicable road/segment IDs or a filtered GIS layer and confirm the total network length.

Council confirms that the intention of this RFQ is to undertake a roughness assessment of the entire Council-maintained road network, including both sealed and unsealed roads.

The supplied GIS dataset contains a number of asset types that do not form part of the Council-maintained road carriageway network. Respondents should base their submission on surveying all Council-maintained road carriageways and exclude those assets identified in Question 2 below.

Council reserves the right to confirm the final survey extent with the successful respondent prior to commencement of the project.

2. Whether State roads and the ancillary features listed above are included.

State Roads are excluded from the scope of this RFQ.

The following ancillary features are also excluded from the scope of works:

- Road shoulders;

- Car parks;

- Cycleways/shared paths; and

- Other ancillary transport assets that do not form part of Council's road carriageway network.

The assessment is limited to Council-managed road carriageways.

3. Whether roughness measurements are required in both travel directions, and whether any additional lanes require separate survey passes.

Council requires roughness data to be collected in both travel directions, where practical and safe to do so.

For roads with multiple traffic lanes in the same direction, respondents should detail their proposed survey methodology and any assumptions regarding lane coverage within their submission.

Where respondents consider additional lane surveys necessary to achieve the project objectives, this should be clearly identified and costed within the submission.

Council trusts the above clarification assists respondents in establishing the survey quantity, pricing and delivery program. Any assumptions adopted in preparing submissions should be clearly stated within the quotation.

If you have any other queries, please let me know

Quenten Graham

Asset Officer

Balranald Shire Council

Could Council please provide clarification on the following items to assist Tenderers in pricing and planning the works on a consistent basis.

RFI 01 - Exact Work Locations / Chainage Reference Points

Could Council please confirm the exact limits of works for each nominated road location and provide either GPS coordinates for the start and finish of each treatment section, or the GPS location/reference point for CH 0.000 for each road so the nominated chainages can be accurately located. We have also noted a discrepancy for Blue Hills Road within Attachment A. Section 3.1 identifies the works as CH 26.35 - 30.65 km, whereas Section 13.1.1 identifies Blue Hills Road as CH 14.26 - 16.26 km. Could Council please confirm the correct Blue Hills Road chainage and treatment limits to be used for tender pricing. Could Council also please confirm the correct chainages for the other nominated locations where the tender documents differ, including Donnybrook Road and Beverley Road.

RFI 02 - Triple Blend Composition

The Technical Specification nominates 3% Triple Blend stabilising agent for all work locations. Could Council please confirm the required constituents and blend proportions of the Triple Blend to be adopted for tender pricing.

RFI 03 - Construction Water Sources

Could Council please advise whether Council-owned or Council-controlled construction water sources are available for use by the Contractor for these works. If available, could Council please provide the locations of the water sources and advise whether any extraction or usage charges apply.

RFI 04 - Shoulder / Table Drain Material and Disposal

The Technical Specification requires removal of material from the shoulder to provide drainage to the table drain, together with de-grassing and clearing of the formation/table drain where applicable. Could Council please confirm the required treatment of material generated from these activities. In particular, can suitable material be graded and spread neatly within the road reserve adjacent to the works, or is the Contractor required to cart the material to a Council nominated stockpile or approved disposal location? Where Council directs material to be transported to a stockpile or disposal location rather than being managed within the immediate worksite, could Council please confirm whether the additional loading, cartage and disposal costs would be treated as a Variation.

RFI 05 - Trafficability of Stabilised Pavement / Requirement for Sidetracks

MRTS07B places restrictions on trafficking of the completed stabilised pavement prior to surfacing where damage may occur. Based on the nominated pavement widths, it appears that practical half-width construction may not provide sufficient width to maintain controlled traffic past the work area. If the completed stabilised pavement is required to remain closed to public traffic until the specified bituminous surfacing is applied, temporary sidetracks or bypasses may be required to maintain traffic. Could Council please confirm the intended traffic management arrangement during the period between completion of stabilisation and application of the bituminous surfacing. In particular, please confirm whether controlled public traffic may be permitted over the completed stabilised pavement prior to sealing, subject to the pavement remaining conforming and undamaged, or whether the stabilised pavement is required to remain closed to public traffic until sealed. If the pavement is required to remain closed to traffic, could Council please confirm whether temporary sidetracks/bypasses are expected and, if so, whether the cost of constructing, maintaining and removing these temporary works is to be included in the tendered square metre rates or treated separately.

In the design, the portal frame action at each pier is used to resist the high flood level loads which is dependent on the inferred Unit 3A and Unit 3B rock levels, especially in the river channel. We note that there are conflicts between the rock levels data in the different tender documents as mentioned at the Briefing. These documents include ;

-	Drg ST-0031 – Pwave profile and Unit Boundary profile

-	Drg ST-05001, and Drg ST-05002 – pile toe levels have been nominated

-	Appendix A Geotech Report – Borehole data and geophysical data

-	Appendix B Hydraulic Assessment Report – inferred bedrock levels appear to be different to the other documents.

This information is required to ascertain if the pile size nominated on the reference design is sufficient.
publicQuestions.answer:
The level of the pile toe estimate in the bridge drawings has been based on a nominal embedment of 1-2 pile diameters into the rock layer levels as defined in the geotechnical investigation. At concept stage for pile design the top of rock level from the geotechnical investigation report was simplified to two levels.

Where a conflict in rock levels is identified, the geotechnical investigation is the primary source of understanding of the nominated rock levels as discussed at the tender briefing.

publicQuestions.question:
Please clarify which scour protection details should be used for the tender design of the abutments and piers. We note that there is a significant discrepancy between the Drawings and the Hydraulic Assessment Report. The drawings call up a minimum thickness of scour protection of 600 mm at the abutments, whilst the Report calls up 2400 mm minimum thickness. Similar discrepancy also occurs at the piers.

Can you also clarify the extent of the scour protection in Phase 1 of the works with the earthworks at the abutments restricted to that provided in the Addenda No. 2 and as shown on the Briefing slide. Is the scour rock to be placed on the temporary face of the earthworks that will be later extended in Phase 2 (ie would then have to be removed and relocated in Phase 2?)
publicQuestions.answer:
Council draws tenderers attention to Contract Information - Design and Documentation Scope of design activities A - Design by the contractor: where scour protection design is to be fully undertaken by the contractor. The hydraulic report provides an assessment for the calculation for riprap scour protection via methodology within HEC-23 and Austroads. Council acknowledges that there are other solutions within Austroads and welcomes innovation to address these project requirements. The drawings note a typical min thickness and preliminary rock size. As such, Council recommend tenderers review the provided documentation and make themselves aware of the site conditions and make allowance in their tender for appropriately designed scour protection.

The Stage 1 extent of rock should extend for the proposed earthen extent for the stage 1 works. Council acknowledge that the rock on the eastern ramp section will need to be removed at the commencement of Stage 2 but require this to protect the works from washout between the stages.

publicQuestions.question:
In the drawing in Addenda No.3 showing the limit of earthworks for Phase 1 there is also a series of blue arrows at the toe of the embankment shown. This is presumed to show an overland water path contained in an earthwork swale around the new roadwork draining back into the river. Is this swale to be included in the scope for Phase 1 around the limited earthworks proposed at the abutments? Does this proposed swale require scour protection into the river? Is the swale lined?

Alternatively, should any swale in this location be ignored for the purposes of this tender and not be part of the current proposed scope.
publicQuestions.answer: The blue arrows on the Civil Drawings are “Clean Water Diversion Drains” or can be termed as “Catch Drains” to align with Austroads Terminology, these are provided to collect flows from the high side of the embankments and prevent erosion of the embankment toe. As the earthworks for Phase 1 are permanent, the embankment toe is to be protected and design is to be done as per Austroads guidelines (Part 5B - as adopted by TfNSW). The size and compositional makeup of the drainage asset is to be determined by the Tenderer through the design process which would include the appropriate treatment to prevent erosion of the channel or the adjacent embankment.

publicQuestions.question: To develop a well considered submission including design and robust construction methodology we request a 2 week extension of time.

publicQuestions.question:
As discussed during the tender briefing and later at the site inspection, the available time to complete the “Design & Construct” tender submission is very short for work of this nature. We believe that there are a number of options that could be pursued that will provide significant benefits to Council and the community which will require time to develop and verify.

We request that an additional two weeks be added to the tender ‘close date’ so that Council can receive the best possible submission for this important local Project.
publicQuestions.answer:
(edited on 28/Sep/2026 01:21 PM)

Council has extended the closing date by approximately 2 weeks. The new closing date is Thursday 22 October 2026 at 2pm. Council carefully considered funding milestone implications and the quantity of work and material to review and analyse to prepare quality submission when making this decision.

publicQuestions.question: Are the batters shown on the roadworks drawings including the cross sections drawn to the extent of the scour rock or fill. Given there is going to be 2m thick of scour rock it will make a significant difference to the volume of fill.
publicQuestions.answer: The drawings show the earthworks extent that would need to comply with the requirements of TS 02158.1. The abutment scour protection would be placed over the shown earthwork’s extent with the thickness subject to the scour design.

Access will only be available between Armidale Road and the River along Councils Road Corridor.

Minimum PPE requirements for the site inspection include lace up boots, long pants and high vis vest.

All questions and responses will be minuted with records of minutes provided to all tenderers as an addendum through VendorPanel.

title: DETSI Regulated Waste Tracking System Proof of Concept
description:
The department is seeking to modernise the administration of regulated waste transport across Queensland, leveraging contemporary digital services.

The waste tracking framework provides oversight to the movement of regulated waste throughout Queensland. It enables the management of data about generation, transport and disposal of waste, which supports environmental protection, regulatory compliance and accountability throughout its lifecycle.

While the existing IT solution supports core waste tracking requirements, the department is seeking opportunities to modernise and enhance this capability to improve industry adoption, data collection, process efficiency, and provide a foundation for future service delivery.

To inform this strategic investment path, the department is undertaking a Proof of Concept (PoC) to assess potential delivery approaches in the market.

title: Palm Island Indigenous and Arts Installation Precinct (Cultural Walk) – Construction Works
description:
Palm Island Aboriginal Shire Council (Council) is seeking to engage a suitably qualified, experienced and appropriately licensed Principal Contractor to undertake the construction of the Palm Island Indigenous and Arts Installation Precinct (Cultural Walk) on the Palm Island foreshore.

The procurement is principally construct-only, based on the design and technical documentation issued with this Invitation to Tender. The Contractor will be responsible for the complete construction, coordination, commissioning, certification and handover of the Works, including all labour, plant, materials, supervision, subcontractors, logistics and incidental activities necessary to complete the Works in accordance with the Contract Documents.

The Contractor will also be responsible for defined incidental design obligations associated with its construction methodology, temporary works, shop detailing and specialist supplier interfaces, together with any supplementary investigations or engineering expressly directed under the Contract.

Council will retain overall project leadership, cultural oversight and responsibility for the Principal-provided permanent works design except where the Contract expressly allocates a design responsibility to the Contractor.

title: Bushfire Resilience Specialists
description:
Bushfire Resilient Communities (BRC) unit within the Bushfire Resilience and Operational Support (BROS) branch is responsible for carriage of several Queensland Fire Department (QFD) functions. BRC is seeking to establish a SOA with a panel of specialist consultants with the objective of delivering critical projects including VHC as part of ongoing RFSQ bushfire hazard mapping program.

These include the mitigation of bushfire risks to communities through hazard map development, Land Use Planning (LUP), training and support programs.

In line with Government commitments, BRC is currently providing advice on several high-priority development proposals to support these functions and provide services in the following fields:

•Vegetation Hazard Spatial and Modelling Services - Services related to the delivery of specialist vegetation models, machine learning tools and spatial products to support interpretation of vegetation attributes.

•Bushfire Ecological Services - Services related to the undertaking of specialist site assessments, reporting and product development regarding fire ecology, vegetation assessment, fuel hazard characteristics.

•Bushfire Risk, Planning and Policy Services - Services relate to the delivery of specialist bushfire assessments and application of knowledge in the fields of bushfire risk assessment, plan making, statutory planning and policy development.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
BRC engages services and expertise from time to time to support the development of products and services including Bushfire Prone Area (BPA), Vegetation Hazard Class (VHC) and Vegetation Structural State (VSS) mapping and land use planning functions.

These services are required to support fluctuations in service delivery requirements beyond capacity of the BRC unit, ensuring time critical program delivery including provision of up-to-date and accurate bushfire hazard mapping.

BRC unit is seeking to engage consultants to undertake four key projects:

•VHC mapping for the Far-North Queensland and Cape York Planning Regions (pending sufficient budget), and Land Use Planning studies for the Western Downs Bushfire Risk and Resilience Strategy Project.

•VHC, VSS and Vegetation Structure Attribute (VSA) field surveys across key locations in Queensland to support spatial modelling of vegetation parameters used as inputs to BPA mapping.

• Development of a long term, evidence-based spatial methodology to identify bushfire risk. The model will apply key hazard and risk considerations (i.e. vegetation structure and landform, through existing hazard mapping products) as well as the development of risk inputs to develop a bushfire risk model; and

•Develop a long term, evidence-based bushfire management strategy for the Western Downs Regional Council (WDRC) through the application of forward-looking bushfire hazard and community risk profiles to achieve critical community safety and resilience outcomes.
