title: Call for Submissions: System Restart Service – North Metro Sub-network of the SWIS
description:
AEMO is calling for submissions from Market Participants to provide a System Restart Service (SRS) for the North Metro sub-network of the South West Interconnected System (SWIS) in Western Australia.

This is to address contract expiry in the sub-network and to ensure continuity of System Restart Services.

A System Restart Service is a service from a Registered Facility, with an energy producing system, that can start without requiring energy to be supplied from a Network to assist in the re-energisation of the SWIS in the event of a system shut down or major supply disruption.

Tender approach: Open to Market Participants capable of providing SRS in the North Metro sub-network.

Service commencement: 1 April 2027

Contract term: 5 years from the service commencement date, although shorter durations can be considered by AEMO.

Technical requirements: Service capability must meet the requirements set out in the WEM System Restart Standard and the North Metro SRS Specification.

Standard-form contract: Contract terms are provided as part of the tender documentation.

The tender process is conducted in accordance with the Electricity System and Market Rules (ESM Rules 3.7).

title: 2027/336 Environmental Audit Services - Mildura Landfill Capping Design
description:
Mildura Rural City Council is seeking Tender responses from suitably qualified individuals and organisations to provide independent audit oversight for the design of capping and rehabilitation works at Mildura Landfill. For background information on Mildura Landfill refer to appendix 2027-336 Mildura Landfill Background Information.

The audit engagement is structured across two stages:

•	Stage 1: Audit scoping and concept design review

•	Stage 2: Detailed design and tender documentation review

The appendix 2027-336 Mildura Landfill Final Capping Works - Engagement Schedule provides a visual overview of the full engagement workflow, including the sequencing of deliverables, auditor checkpoints, and the roles and responsibilities of all parties at each stage.

This tender is informed by appendix 2027-336 Waste Services Strategy 2026–2036 which identifies the transition of the Mildura Landfill site to a Transfer Station only operating model. The timing of cessation of landfilling is planned to be from the 2028/29 financial year.

ENQUIRIES: Any tender enquiries should be directed to the online forum in VendorPanel.

INSPECTION: A site inspection is scheduled for 11.00am on Thursday, 22 October 2026. Inspections are highly recommended but not mandatory.

SUBMISSIONS: Completed responses can ONLY be submitted electronically by uploading into the VendorPanel System. Respondents will receive a confirmation email response upon completion. Should assistance be required please use the help function or the online chat available from the home page of VendorPanel.

Submissions must be fully received by the closing time as late submissions will not be accepted. Council is not bound to accept the lowest priced Tender or all or any part of a Tender and reserves the right to conduct the Request for Tender process and select the successful respondent(s) as it sees fit. All responses must be made by online submission. Any response made by any other means (open email, facsimile, post or in person) will not be considered.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi there, errors on the price file as follows:

Category C Lump Sum: The summary at the bottom pulls from the wrong rows for the last four groups. Once prices are in, the totals would be wrong:

Ballarat Mining Exchange (F60) points at a blank heading row (F33), not its subtotal in F38.

Civic Hall (F61) points at F34, which is a Mining Exchange line, not its subtotal in F44.

Sporting Venues (F62) points at F35, another Mining Exchange line, not its subtotal in F50.

City of Ballarat Events (F63) points at F36, a third Mining Exchange line, not its subtotal in F53.

Schedule of Rates (identical in all three workbooks)

Errors on screen: The Min. Call Out Charge rows (items 2, 5, 8, 11 and 14) have "[##]" in the Qty column. That produces #VALUE! errors, which flow into those subtotals, the summary, the Total and the GST. The sheet can't calculate until someone enters a number. Council hasn't said what the minimum call-out hours are, so I wouldn't guess.

Sunday and "Other" rates left out of the total: Total Excluding GST (F56) adds only the first four summary lines. The Sunday and the two "Other" lines are left out.

"Other" subtotals miss rows: The "Other" business-hours subtotal (F37) skips items 22 and 23. The after-hours one (F47) skips items 30 and 31.

Theatre chairs line: Items 20 and 28 (deep clean of Her Majesty's Theatre chairs) appear in the A and B workbooks, although the theatre is a Category C venue.

Part-hourly rate: Items 3, 6, 9, 12 and 15 have a quantity of 0.5 hour and a rate "per 30m". If a bidder enters the price for a 30-minute block, the amount comes out at half of it. It needs clarifying how that rate should be entered.
publicQuestions.answer: Adjusted pricing schedule added as addendum

publicQuestions.question:
Pricing Schedule 26 27 79 Cat C — clarification request regarding apparent formula issues

We have identified several apparent formula issues in the supplied pricing workbook and would appreciate Council’s clarification.

In the “Lump Sum Category C” sheet, summary cells F60:F63 for Ballarat Mining Exchange, Civic Hall, Sporting Venues and City of Ballarat Events use a shared formula resolving to F33:F36, rather than the corresponding subtotals at F38, F44, F50 and F53. As a result, the summary values and Total Excluding GST at F64 do not correctly capture those four sections.

In the “Schedule of Rates” sheet:

- F56 sums F49:F52 only, excluding Sunday (F53) and the two “Other” subtotals (F54:F55);

- subtotals F37 and F47 exclude rows 35–36 and 45–46 respectively; and

- the Min. Call Out Charge quantity cells C5, C10, C15, C20 and C25 currently contain the placeholder text “[##]”, which causes the associated formulas to return #VALUE! until replaced with a numeric value.

Could Council please issue a corrected workbook, or alternatively confirm:

1. whether bidders are permitted to correct the affected formulas in their submission;

2. whether the [##] quantity placeholders are intended to be replaced by bidders; and

3. that tender evaluation will be based on the submitted line-item values and correctly calculated totals.

Thank you.

Adjusted pricing schedule added as addendum

Where # is listed under Qty it is to included minimum call out period e.g 30 minutes = 0.5

publicQuestions.question:
Barista2Go confirms our attendance at the mandatory EOI briefing and site inspection for EOI 2671 – Bronte House Tea Room on 1 October 2026 at 11:00 am at Bronte House, 470 Bronte Road, Bronte.

We look forward to attending the site inspection and gaining a better understanding of the premises and the opportunity.

We have also listed a set of Commercial Viability Questionnaire with clarification questions about the proposed operating model, licensed areas, commercial arrangements, and the scope of the Tea Room opportunity. Your responses will help us assess the opportunity's commercial viability and prepare an informed EOI submission, including the indicative annual rental offer.

1.	Licensed/lettable area

o	Can Council confirm precisely which areas shown in the premises plan would form part of the Tea Room's licensed or lettable area?

o	Would the operator have ongoing access to the kitchen, lounge room, verandas and nominated garden area for the duration of the license?

o	Are there any other indoor or outdoor areas, besides those marked in the space map, that may be made available for customer seating or Tea Room operations?

o	Is there a proposed maximum seating or patron capacity for the Tea Room?

2.	Meaning of "non-exclusive license"

o	Can Council clarify what "non-exclusive" means in practical terms for the successful operator?

o	During agreed Tea Room operating hours, would Council or third parties also be permitted to use the licensed areas?

o	Could Council appoint another food, beverage, coffee or catering operator to operate at Bronte House during the license period?

o	Would the successful Tea Room operator have exclusive food and beverage trading rights during its agreed operating hours?

o	If not, in what circumstances could another food and beverage provider operate at the property?

3.	Trading days and operating hours

o	The EOI states that the Tea Room will operate on several days per week "to be agreed." Can Council provide its current expectation regarding minimum or preferred trading days?

o	Are there proposed minimum or maximum operating hours?

o	Will weekend and/or public holiday trading be expected?

o	Would the operator have flexibility to adjust trading days/hours according to seasonality, visitor demand and commercial viability?

o	Will access to Bronte House outside public opening hours be available for preparation, cleaning, deliveries and stock management?

4.	Community access and other activities at Bronte House

o	How frequently does Council anticipate Bronte House being used for exhibitions, heritage talks, workshops and small-scale events?

o	Would these activities occur concurrently with normal Tea Room operations?

o	Where an activity requires use of the lounge, veranda or garden areas allocated to the Tea Room, how would this be managed?

o	Would there be occasions when the Tea Room would be required to close or reduce its operating area to accommodate Council activities?

o	If so, would this be reflected in the license fee/rent or otherwise compensated?

5.	Event and catering opportunities

o	Would the successful Tea Room operator have the first opportunity/right of refusal to provide food and beverage services for Council, community or private events held at Bronte House?

o	Would the operator be permitted to provide expanded catering beyond the normal Tea Room menu for these events?

o	Would private functions, corporate events or other small-scale events be permitted under the proposed operating model?

o	Would the operator be permitted to accept direct event/catering bookings at Bronte House, subject to Council approval?

o	If external caterers are permitted, would they be able to use the Tea Room operator's kitchen, equipment, furniture or licensed areas?

6.	Approvals and Development Application

o	The EOI indicates that the Tea Room use will require an amendment to the Plan of Management and potentially Development Approval.

o	Will Council be responsible for obtaining the required Plan of Management amendment and DA/other planning approvals?

o	What approvals, licenses or consents would be the responsibility of the operator?

o	Would commencement of rent be conditional upon all necessary approvals being obtained?

o	If approvals materially restrict operating days, hours, seating capacity or the proposed offering, would the commercial terms be reconsidered?

7.	Rent and commercial structure

o	Is Council seeking a fixed annual rent only, or would it consider alternative commercial structures such as a base rent plus turnover component?

o	Is there a minimum annual rental expectation or valuation that respondents should be aware of?

o	Will rent commence from execution of the license, possession of the premises, or commencement of commercial trading?

o	Will there be a fit-out/rent-free establishment period?

o	What outgoings, if any, will be payable in addition to the annual rent?

o	Will Council require a security deposit, bank guarantee or bond?

o	Will annual rent escalation apply during the initial term or option periods?

8.	Visitor numbers and commercial information

o	Does Council have historical visitor numbers for Bronte House and the surrounding grounds?

o	What visitation levels does Council anticipate under the new community access model?

o	Are there particular days or periods when visitation is expected to be highest?

o	Does Council intend to actively market Bronte House and the Tea Room to increase visitation?

o	Will the Tea Room be included on Council's website, visitor information, events program and promotional material?

9.	Menu, Cuisine & Experiential Offering

o	How does Council define “light refreshments” for this EOI?

o	Would Council be open to a contemporary and experiential interpretation of the Tea Room, rather than a traditional tea-room format, provided the offering remains appropriate to the heritage setting?

o	Would the operator be permitted to offer rotating or themed culinary experiences, including different cuisines and styles of light dining — for example, French-inspired finger food and canapés, Asian-inspired offerings, or other seasonal and culturally diverse menus?

o	Would Council be open to bookable High Tea experiences, including contemporary or cuisine-inspired interpretations of High Tea, using appropriate indoor, veranda and/or garden areas?

o	Would the operator be permitted to develop special menus or culinary experiences aligned with exhibitions, heritage talks, workshops, seasonal occasions and other events held at Bronte House?

o	Are there any limitations on the onsite preparation, assembly, heating and finishing of food being permitted, subject to the relevant approvals and food-safety requirements?

o	Would the operator have flexibility to rotate and evolve the menu and experiences over time based on seasonality, visitor demand and programming at Bronte House?

o	Are there any specific menu, cuisine, service-style or food-preparation restrictions Council expects the operator to observe?

10.	Branding and signage

o	Would the operator be permitted to trade under its own business/brand name?

o	What external and internal signage would be permitted?

o	Would menu boards, branded cups, uniforms and other operator branding be permitted?

o	Are there heritage restrictions governing signage or visual merchandising?

11.	License term and option periods

o	The EOI refers to a term of up to three years, structured as one year plus two one-year options.

o	Who holds the right to exercise each option — Council, the operator, or both parties by agreement?

o	What performance criteria would Council use when deciding whether to extend the license?

o	Given the potential capital investment in equipment, furniture and establishment costs, would Council consider a longer initial term or alternative license structure at the RFT stage?

12.	Sales and visitation reporting

o	The EOI requires the operator to provide sales figures and visitation information.

o	What level of sales information will be required — total turnover only or detailed transaction/category information?

o	How frequently will reporting be required?

o	How does Council intend to use this commercially sensitive information?

o	Will operator sales information remain confidential subject to Council's statutory disclosure obligations?

title: Murray Aquatic and Leisure Centre Masterplan Review, Strategy and Business Case
description:
The Shire of Murray is seeking submissions from suitably qualified multidisciplinary consultant teams to undertake a review and update of the Murray Aquatic and Leisure Centre Masterplan 2016 and prepare a contemporary, staged redevelopment and investment strategy for the future development of the Centre.

The project includes a strategic review and update of the existing Masterplan, preparation of a staged redevelopment strategy and implementation framework, operational feasibility assessment, supporting business case and investment strategy, and concept designs and preliminary construction cost estimates for prioritised Stage 1 redevelopment works.

The Murray Aquatic and Leisure Centre is located at 16 Camp Road, Pinjarra, Western Australia.

The Shire is seeking completion of the project by June 2027 where practicable, with the preferred Masterplan, staging and indicative high-level capital costs sufficiently advanced by May 2027 to support preliminary advocacy and forward planning.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerAddress:
1915 Pinjarra Rd
Pinjarra, Western Australia 6208
Australia
vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
The Shire of Murray is a local government area of Western Australia. It has an area of 1,710.1 square kilometres (660.3 sq mi) and is located in the Peel Region about 80 kilometres (50 mi) south of the Perth central business district.

The Shire extends across the Peel Inlet and the Swan Coastal Plain into the Darling Scarp, including about 77,000 hectares (190,000 acres) of State forests. Timber logging and agriculture were the traditional enterprises of the district. However, in recent decades, bauxite mining and a significant equine and tourism industry have emerged.

The Murray River flows all year throughout the district. It offers premier country racing and trotting facilities, a golf course and an array of festivals and events.
vendorPanelDetails.queryCutoffAtRaw: Tuesday 27 October 2026 05:00 PM (W. Australia Standard Time)
vendorPanelDetails.background:
The successful consultant will build upon the significant strategic planning, needs analysis and internal operational assessments already undertaken by the Shire. The project is not intended to recommence strategic planning and needs assessment work already completed, but rather to validate and refine this work in response to current conditions and future requirements.

A multidisciplinary and collaborative approach is required to ensure strategic planning, operational modelling, architectural planning and financial analysis collectively inform the recommended redevelopment outcomes. Relevant background documents and available operational and asset information will be provided to the successful consultant.
vendorPanelDetails.desiredOutcomes:
The project will establish a contemporary, evidence-based framework to guide future investment in the Murray Aquatic and Leisure Centre, support long-term financial planning and strengthen advocacy for external funding.

Key outcomes include a preferred long-term Masterplan, staged redevelopment and implementation framework, asset renewal and lifecycle assessment, operational and financial investment modelling, business case and funding strategy, and concept designs with preliminary cost estimates for priority Stage 1 redevelopment works.

The preferred approach should provide practical, achievable and financially responsible solutions capable of staged implementation.

title: T2026-10 EOI - Design, Supply and Delivery of Turn-Key Residential Dwellings and Duplexes - Bedourie
description: Diamantina Shire Council (the Principal) invites Expressions of Interest (EOI) from suitably experienced and capable respondents to present options for the design, supply, delivery and turn-key construction of one or more residential dwellings and/or duplexes, including 1-bedroom houses, 2-bedroom houses, 3-bedroom houses, 1-bedroom duplexes and 2-bedroom duplexes, at Bedourie.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerAddress:
17 Herbert St
Bedourie, Queensland 4829
Australia
vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
Diamantina consists of two main towns Birdsville and Bedourie, with a third town of Betoota.

Bedourie is located 1,600km west of Brisbane, while Birdsville is 200km south of Bedourie and 1,200km from Adelaide.

Our towns have four aircraft services per week on the Brisbane- Mount Isa Circuit. REX (Regional Express) provides this service.

Despite it's size, Birdsville is a well-known destination for many Australian and International visitors. The town hosts one horse race meeting a year, when over 6,000 people swell the town population. It is the start of the famous Birdsville Track, which originally was used as a stock route for moving cattle from Queensland to Southern markets.

Bedourie is the Shire's administration centre. The last ten years has seen its population more than double to 140 people. The town boasts many new amenities including an aquatic centre, hot artesian spa and a community hall. Visitor numbers have increased to over 120,000 per year.

The Shire's wealth lies within its cattle industry, tourism and natural environment. Located within Queensland's Channel Country, bordering South Australia and the Northern Territory, this area is renown for producing prime quality beef. The natural irrigation from the Diamantina and Georgina River Systems is also assisting with developing an organic cattle industry.

We are fortunate that National Parks comprise 25% of our shire's area. The Simpson Desert, Diamantina National Park, (just been named in the top ten National Parks in Australia) and Astrebla National Park all offer unique scenery and wildlife for visitors to experience.

Visit the Diamantina Shire for a unique outback experience.

publicQuestions.question:
Good afternoon,

We are preparing a submission for the Bedourie residential dwellings EOI and would appreciate clarification on the following:

Sites and available information: Have the proposed lots been identified? If available, please provide site plans, survey, geotechnical information, flood levels and minimum finished floor levels.

Services: Can Council confirm the availability, location and capacity of power, water and sewer connections, together with stormwater discharge requirements? Where these are not yet established, is there a preferred assumption for comparable indicative pricing?

Turnkey inclusions: Please confirm Council’s expectations for carports, fencing, window furnishings, landscaping and external paths, including any minimum specifications or allowances.

Delivery: Is there a preferred commencement or completion timeframe, and should multiple-dwelling prices assume construction at adjoining sites under one mobilisation?
publicQuestions.answer:
Thank you for your enquiry, please see below Council responses.

1. Sites and available information - Sites and available information: Have the proposed lots been identified? If available, please provide site plans, survey, geotechnical information, flood levels and minimum finished floor levels.

Response - Parcels of land have not yet been chosen, contractors are to assume flat/ level sites which are above flood level with H site soil classification. Site layouts and survey information is not available.

2. Services - Can Council confirm the availability, location and capacity of power, water and sewer connections, together with stormwater discharge requirements? Where these are not yet established, is there a preferred assumption for comparable indicative pricing?

Response - Yes all services are currently in the street. All services will require connection to the house/s. Stormwater to street.

3. Turnkey inclusions - Please confirm Council’s expectations for carports, fencing, window furnishings, landscaping and external paths, including any minimum specifications or allowances.

Response - No internal soft furnishings. External fence, 2 car lockable garage, with concrete driveway and concrete footpath to front door.

4. Delivery - Is there a preferred commencement or completion timeframe, and should multiple-dwelling prices assume construction at adjoining sites under one mobilisation?

Response - Completion by end 2027. Construction under one mobilisation for multiple dwellings.

RFI-001

Response Validity Period: The Expression of Interest Form references a Response Validity Period but this period is not stated in Part 2 General Information or the Procurement Process Conditions as issued. Please confirm the period respondents are required to hold their EOI response open.

RFI-002

For example, will Stage 2 be conducted as an open tender to shortlisted respondents, a negotiated process with a preferred respondent, or a panel arrangement?

Clarification is needed so respondents can determine the appropriate treatment of proprietary design, methodology and cost content included in their response.

Please confirm (a) the total number of dwellings and duplexes across all configurations that Council intends to deliver under this program, and (b) whether the program is staged across multiple financial years or is intended as a single procurement. This information is required to size and confirm capacity commitments accurately.

 - 90 Days Validity Period. Noting that the Pricing is indicative and where Council decides to proceed to Tender, pricing can be reviewed and updated.

- Stage 2 step has not yet been determined, however the most likely approach will be an open tender to shortlisted respondents.

RFI-003

- Held confidential to Council

RFI-004

- Yet to be determined, EOI responses will influence actual requirements. If more than one (1) dwelling is put to market the intention will be to deliver them at the same time.

title: DESIGN AND CONSTRUCT – BIRKDALE COMMUNITY PRECINCT ENABLING INFRASTRUCTURE AND LAGOON SUB-PRECINCT
description:
Redland City Council invites suitably qualified and experienced Contractors to submit Expressions of Interest (EOI) for the Design and Construct delivery of the Birkdale Community Precinct (BCP) Enabling Works and Lagoon Precinct.

Respondents may submit an EOI for the complete scope of works and/or any of the identified separable portions.

Enabling Works generally comprise:

Bulk earthworks and site preparation works.

Internal roads and associated pavement construction.

Site entry intersection and roundabout works.

Car parks and bus laydown facilities.

Stormwater drainage, wetlands, bioretention and water quality infrastructure.

Water, sewer, fire and utility infrastructure.

Electrical, communications and high voltage reticulation infrastructure.

Shared pathways and pedestrian infrastructure.

Landscaping, rectification, signage and wayfinding.

Management of project interfaces and construction staging requirements.

Lagoon Sub-Precinct generally comprises:

A large-scale public swimming lagoon, comprising distinct adult and children's lagoons with accessible beach-style entries and ramp access to the main lagoon

Interactive waterplay facilities and splash zones.

A 1,518m² two-storey pavilion incorporating a Restaurant, cafe, retail and function spaces.

Public plazas and activated gathering spaces.

Outdoor BBQ facilities.

Two amenities' buildings, including a DDA compliant Changing Places facility.

Plant rooms, water treatment infrastructure and operational support facilities.

Associated landscaping, pathways and public realm infrastructure.

The Birkdale Community Precinct is a 62-hectare regionally significant community, recreation and events destination that will support delivery of the future Redland Whitewater Centre, which will host Canoe Slalom events during the Brisbane 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games.

The EOI includes a number of identified separable portions within both the Enabling Works and Lagoon Precinct scopes. Council may consider submissions for individual separable portions, complete project components, or the combined scope of works.

The proposed procurement is a two-stage EOI and Request for Proposal (RFP) process. Council may shortlist one or more Respondents and reserves the right to procure the Enabling Works and Lagoon Precinct either separately or collectively.

The project site is located at 390 Old Cleveland Road East, Birkdale, Queensland. Contract award is anticipated in early 2027, with construction commencing approximately February 2027. Contractors with demonstrated Design and Construct experience delivering major civil infrastructure, aquatic facilities and/or multi-stage precinct developments are encouraged to submit an Expression of Interest.

publicQuestions.question:
•	Can Council release the Stantec 30% design, the geotech report and the earthworks cut/fill volumes?

•	What exactly are the "particular manner" conditions of the environmental approval?

•	What contract form will be used at the RFP stage? Will Stantec and vT be novated or stay under council?

•	Is a sitting planned with GIICA's contractor?
publicQuestions.answer:
1. Can Council release the Stantec 30% design, the geotech report and the earthworks cut/fill volumes?

Detailed design documentation, including the Stantec design package, is intended to be issued as part of the Request for Proposal (RFP) stage. The current EOI is focused on identifying suitably qualified and experienced contractors and assessing market capability and interest. Geotechnical information and earthworks modelling/cut and fill information will also be released as part of the RFP documentation package.

2. What exactly are the "particular manner" conditions of the environmental approval?

The environmental approval documentation is publicly available.

The EPBC Act referral decision documentation can be accessed through the Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water (DCCEEW) EPBC Act Public Portal under Reference Number 2026/10471, including the May 2026 Notification of Referral Decision and September 2026 Outcome of Reconsideration.

The supporting referral documentation prepared by Redland City Council is also available on Council's website via the Birkdale Community Precinct – Environmental Stewardship page: https://www.redland.qld.gov.au/Project-updates/Birkdale-Community-Precinct/Environmental-stewardship

Respondents are encouraged to review these publicly available documents when considering the project and associated environmental requirements.

3. What contract form will be used at the RFP stage? Will Stantec and vT be novated or stay under Council?

Council is currently considering the most appropriate contract form, including arrangements for completion of the design works. While Council may make existing design consultants available to the successful contractor, respondents should not assume novation will occur. Further information regarding the final contract form, design responsibilities and consultant arrangements will be provided during the RFP stage.

4. Is a sitting planned with GIICA's contractor?

There is currently no meeting planned between respondents and GIICA's contractor during the EOI phase. Should Council determine that further stakeholder engagement sessions are required as part of the procurement process, all respondents will be advised via VendorPanel.

publicQuestions.answer: A coordinated design for wayfinding and signage across the precinct is yet to be developed. The final coordinated wayfinding strategy and design will be informed by the Redland City Council Wayfinding Signage Manual, approved precinct masterplan design narratives, and concept designs produced by sub-precinct design teams. Further information will be provided as part of the Request for Proposal (RFP) documentation including the requirements relevant to the scope of works being procured.

title: GIS support and development services
description: Walcha Council is seeking proposals through a reverse brief process, to provide GIS services for the establishment and ongoing maintenance of its ArcGIS software platform.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerAddress:
2W Hamilton St
Walcha, New South Wales 2354
Australia
vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
The natural beauty of the Shire is quite breathtaking. The Shire is home to the magnificent Macleay Gorges and boasts some 205,000 hectares of dedicated national park, wilderness and state forest. Parts of our Werrikimbe National Park are World Heritage listed.

The Shire is also a well known trout fishing mecca, boasting some 1,500 km of trout streams which are a home to Rainbow and Brown trout. The township of Walcha is 1,067 metres above sea level, with one of the highest point in the district being at "The Flags" (42 kilometres south of Walcha) which is 1,400 metres above sea level. The highest point is in the Riamukka area, 38 kilometres south of Walcha, where the Grundy Trig Station and the Grundy Fire Tower are situated which is recorded as 1,463 metres. The Shire covers an area of 640,028 hectares (2,475 square miles/6,400 square kilometres). The population of the Shire is approximately 3,224 (Census 2016) which includes approximately 1,700 in the Town of Walcha.

5.	Widgets and Applications to enhance service

6.	Value-add Components

Conditions - Relevant information on Council’s existing GIS can be released after a signed NDA.

title: Winter Harvest Festival 2027 - Marquee & Underhire Supplier
description:
Scenic Rim Regional Council is seeking quotations from suitably qualified suppliers to provide marquee and underhire services for the 2027 Winter Harvest Festival, to be held in Kalbar on Saturday 26 June 2027.

The successful supplier will provide a full-service solution including the supply, delivery, installation, furniture placement, dismantle and collection of event infrastructure across multiple festival locations. Required infrastructure includes, but is not limited to, marquees, furniture, staging, fencing, flooring, crowd control barriers, décor items and associated underhire equipment.

The festival is expected to attract approximately 5,500 attendees and operates across several locations throughout Kalbar including George Street, Kalbar Civic Centre Park, Salvation Army Grounds, School of Arts precinct and surrounding activation areas.

The contract period is anticipated to commence on 1 May 2027 and conclude on 30 July 2027. Installation will occur on 24-25 June 2027, with dismantle occurring on 26-27 June 2027.

Services must be delivered onsite in Kalbar, Queensland.

Please refer to the RFQ documentation for the full scope of works, equipment schedule, production schedule and submission requirements.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerAddress:
82 Brisbane St
Beaudesert, Queensland 4285
Australia
vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
The Scenic Rim region is a thriving rural paradise set in the foothills of the Great Dividing Range and surrounded by world heritage listed national parks. Home to a population of more than 37,780, the region covers 4248sq km and is located an hour south of Brisbane and an hour inland from the Gold Coast. Known for its breathtaking scenery, it is a popular tourist destination offering visitors plenty to see and do. From its myriad of wineries and art galleries to expansive bushwalking tracks, state of the art equine facilities, growing rural communities and friendly country charm, the Scenic Rim region is a must see destination.

Its main towns are Beaudesert, Boonah, Rathdowney, Kooralbyn, Kalbar, Aratula, Canungra, Tamborine Mountain, Harrisville and Peak Crossing. The region's primary businesses are agricultural/horticultural production, the equine industry and tourism/ecotourism. The Scenic Rim region contains more than 30,000 hectares of parkland, including national parks and council controlled parks. The region also contains three dams: Lake Moogerah, Lake Maroon and Wyaralong Dam. Supported by a thriving economy, a farming industry and a vibrant arts community, the Scenic Rim has a strong community spirit and friendly locals.
vendorPanelDetails.queryCutoffAtRaw: Wednesday 28 October 2026 12:00 PM (E. Australia Standard Time)
vendorPanelDetails.background:
Winter Harvest Festival is the flagship event of Scenic Rim Eat Local Month and is a major regional food, farming and tourism event. The festival requires a supplier with demonstrated experience delivering infrastructure for large-scale outdoor events and food and wine festivals of comparable size and complexity.

The successful supplier must:

- Provide high-quality event infrastructure suitable for a premium regional food and wine event.

- Supply sufficient inventory and resources to service multiple event locations simultaneously.

- Provide an experienced Project Manager as the primary point of contact throughout planning and delivery.

- Deliver all infrastructure within the prescribed production schedule and road closure constraints.

- Provide all required engineering certifications, structural documentation, safety plans and risk management documentation.

- Ensure all equipment complies with relevant Australian standards, WHS legislation and event requirements.

- Maintain the capability to respond to weather conditions and operational changes throughout the event period.

- Hold Public Liability Insurance with a minimum coverage of $20 million.
vendorPanelDetails.desiredOutcomes:
- Proven experience delivering infrastructure for regional festivals, food and wine events or major outdoor community events.

- High presentation standards with clean, well-maintained stock.

- Ability to provide alternative or more cost-efficient marquee configurations where appropriate.

- Strong project management, communication and onsite support capability.

- Capacity to provide sponsorship support or value-add opportunities through discounts or in-kind contributions.

- Commitment to safety, quality service delivery and collaborative event planning.

Council is seeking competitive pricing and value for money while ensuring the successful delivery of a high-quality visitor experience.
buyerQuestions: The successful supplier will be required to enter into Scenic Rim Regional Council's Goods and Services Contract. Any proposed departures, qualifications or requested amendments must be clearly identified in the response.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi there, errors on price file

Schedule of Rates (identical in all three workbooks)

Errors on screen: The Min. Call Out Charge rows (items 2, 5, 8, 11 and 14) have "[##]" in the Qty column. That produces #VALUE! errors, which flow into those subtotals, the summary, the Total and the GST. The sheet can't calculate until someone enters a number. Council hasn't said what the minimum call-out hours are, so I wouldn't guess.

Sunday and "Other" rates left out of the total: Total Excluding GST (F56) adds only the first four summary lines. The Sunday and the two "Other" lines are left out.

"Other" subtotals miss rows: The "Other" business-hours subtotal (F37) skips items 22 and 23. The after-hours one (F47) skips items 30 and 31.

Theatre chairs line: Items 20 and 28 (deep clean of Her Majesty's Theatre chairs) appear in the A and B workbooks, although the theatre is a Category C venue.

Part-hourly rate: Items 3, 6, 9, 12 and 15 have a quantity of 0.5 hour and a rate "per 30m". If a bidder enters the price for a 30-minute block, the amount comes out at half of it. It needs clarifying how that rate should be entered.
publicQuestions.answer:
Please see adjusted Pricing Schedule added as addendum

Note where there is a # under Qty it is to indicate your minimum call out time. eg. 30 minutes = .5

Doc108221143

Energy Queensland is seeking expressions of interest from suitably qualified contractors for inclusion on its PCP125 Substation Civil Works Prequalification Scheme.

Contractors will be assessed as meeting the applicable requirements may be admitted to the Scheme and subsequently invited to participate in sourcing activities for relevant work packages. Appointment to the Scheme does not guarantee any minimum volume of work, expenditure, invitation to quote or contract award.

Work may be undertaken within operational high-voltage substations and other energised electricity network environments across Queensland. Contractors must demonstrate suitable safety systems, competencies, training, experience, resources and capacity to work in these environments.

Vendor Panel (advertised on QTender in parallel, but respondents must submit via Vendor Panel)

Final Date for Request for Clarification:	27/10/2026

All queries are to be directed to nadia.milton@energyq.com.au

Outlined in Reference Document 'EQL Prequalification Scheme' Applicants may apply for one or both of the following work categories Civil Works and Minor Works:

Civil Works: Construction of projects in new or existing substation which may include but not limited to Civil, Structural, Drainage, Concrete Footings, Pavements, Buildings, Foundations, Earth Grid, Oil Separator, Fence, Yard Stone, Transformer Bund, Erection of Support Structures, Trenches, Conduit Installation. Minor Civil Works includes maintenance style work or minor projects in new or existing substations covering similar activities to Civil Works. This category applies to works generally valued below $250,000 excluding GST.

EQL has identified increased demand for Minor Civil Works in Southeast Queensland, particularly:

•	Area 14: Brisbane Central;

•	Area 15: Brisbane South; and

•	Area 16: Ipswich Lockyer.

Applications are also sought from contractors capable of delivering the work categories across other Queensland regions.

The Contractor must provide the Project/Contract Manager with a minimum of two (2) business days’ notice prior to commencing works and must notify the Project/Contract Manager immediately upon completion of vessel removal.

•	Approved Methodology

All works must be undertaken in accordance with the approved methodology. No variation to the methodology is permitted without the prior written approval of the Project/Contract Manager.

•	Any subcontractors employed by the principal must have all appropriate qualifications and insurances to undertake the scope of work they are employed to undertake.

•	Additional Works

The Contractor must not undertake any additional works outside the approved scope without obtaining prior written approval from the Project/Contract Manager.

•	Disposal Requirements

The Contractor must ensure the vessel is lawfully destroyed and disposed of at a licensed and approved waste disposal facility. The proposed disposal facility must be identified within the submitted methodology.

•	Evidence of Disposal

The Contractor must provide documentary evidence confirming disposal of the vessel at the approved facility, including a waste disposal facility weighbridge receipt and any other relevant disposal records.

•	Final Report and Invoice

Within five (5) business days of completing the removal and disposal of the vessel, the Contractor must submit a final report and invoice to the Project/Contract Manager.

title: Expansion of Bamaga Sewer Ponds
description:
The Northern Peninsular Area Regional Council is seeking proposals from suitably qualified and experienced contractors to carry out works to expand the capacity of the Sewer Treatment Ponds in Bamaga.

Concept designs are attached. NPARC will accept variation to these designs.

The work involves the increase in size of the 2 primary lagoons and the addition of a 3rd secondary lagoon.

Other works include: New interconnecting pipework and valves; new bypass pipelines, relocation of a rising main, relocation of electrical wires, fencing and landscaping works.

The current STP must be able to operate for as long as possible during the construction works.

In addition, the contractor will provide an improved screening and grit removal system at the inlet to the STP. The design and type of these systems has not been specified and therefore the Contractor can propose the most cost effective system, with a focus on total life-cycle costs.

There is some desludging work required in the existing ponds. That work can be delivered as a variation, using unit rates.

publicQuestions.question:
To establish a clear scope and pricing basis, could Council please respond to the following through VendorPanel?

1. Effluent irrigation scope: Drawing W010 shows a proposed new 33 ha effluent irrigation area and refers to a specification that was not supplied. Is construction of this area, including associated pipework, pumping, controls and access roads, part of this contract, or is W010 provided for information only? If included, please provide the required extent and performance criteria.

2. Design capacity and acceptance criteria: Council has directed tenderers to use the 2032 projections for all five communities in the 2012 report, which show 3,949 people, 19 L/s ADWF and approximately 95 L/s PWWF. The request also sets a 6,000 EP objective. Please confirm how Council expects the 6,000 EP objective to be demonstrated and provide the treated effluent, storage and reuse performance criteria for acceptance.

3. Current approvals and operating data: Please provide the current environmental authority or licence conditions, available recent influent and effluent monitoring results, and any updated flow data. If none is available, please confirm that tenderers should state their proposed design assumptions.

4. Survey and existing services: Please issue the survey data and GHD drawings in DWG format offered in the request, including the permanent survey marker details. Please also provide any available current survey, pond levels, service plans and as-built information for existing pipework, electrical supply and controls. Please confirm whether contractors can arrange site access for survey, service location and borrow-source sampling before tender close.

5. Live plant staging: What minimum treatment capacity must remain operational during construction? Please advise any permitted isolation or shutdown windows and any requirements for temporary bypass pumping, monitoring or emergency response.

6. Council-supplied materials: Please identify the proposed borrow sources and confirm whether the available clay can be sampled and tested against the contractor’s proposed liner specification. Does Council’s free concrete supply include grout suitable for the W003 mattress? Please clarify whether concrete and grout will be delivered to the workfront, the required advance notice for quantities, and the source of construction water.

7. Overhead electrical work: W002 notes that an existing pole is to be decommissioned and the overhead line re-spanned between existing poles. Please confirm the asset owner, the intended extent of this work, and responsibility for design approval, outages and network charges. Is any further overhead diversion required?

8. Rising main relocation: Please provide the existing rising main’s size, material, alignment, operating requirements and connection details, and confirm the required diversion limits and isolation arrangements.

9. Accommodation: Council has confirmed that accommodation will be provided free of charge, subject to availability. Can Council reserve sufficient beds for a crew of up to ten during the proposed May–October 2027 construction period? Our proposed roster is three weeks on and one week off, with no personnel remaining on site during the off week.

10. Desludging variation: Please confirm whether tenderers should provide unit rates only, with the quantity established by a new survey. Please also advise who will arrange sludge testing, waste classification and approval of the disposal location.

11. Completion milestone: The request asks tenderers to demonstrate capacity to deliver “prior to October 2027,” while the stated construction window is May to October 2027. Is practical completion required by 30 September 2027, or is completion during October acceptable?
publicQuestions.answer:
1. Firstly, I do apologise but I have stolen the design drawings from old network folders. This work was planned to be done about 11 years ago, but never went ahead for reasons unknown. Now that the population in NPA is growing, the project HAS to go ahead. However, the irrigation system and pump station were built and are therefore NOT part of this project.

2. We will not be able to demonstrate capacity limits from this project. At the moment 3 communities do not get pumped to the Bamaga Ponds (Injinoo, Umagico and New Mapoon). But they will in the future. That is part of another project. We are relying on the design drawings that we have and asking contractors to build new ponds to match those capacities.

3. You are correct, there is no data available. We are connecting a flow meter up at the inlet to Bamaga Ponds soon, but there will be no data available during the tender process. Tenderers should state their proposed design assumptions.

4. All information that I could locate was provided in the files area. Tenderers are able to access the site at any time to undertake their own investigations if required.

5. We have very little opportunity to restrict flow to the plant for any extended period of time. Our sewer pump stations are quite small so there are only a couple of hours storage at the main Bamaga Pump Station. However, we could set up a bypass arrangement for the Primary Pond for a short period of time and just use the other ponds during that time. How this can be achieved should be part of your tender.

6. Council has a number of borrow pits within close proximity to the site. I will try to find some test results from these borrow pits and put those in the Files section. Concrete and grout will be delivered to site. Please note that we only have a "rudimentary" batch plant. If specialised mixes are required, we need the contractor to assist with the batching process. NPARC will send the test samples away and provide the reports back to the contractor to include in the QA Documentation.

7. That overhead line and pole are no longer there. Please ignore that note.

8. The rising main is 150mm DICL pipe. The alignment is roughly as shown on the drawings. The realignment is part of your design work. Location of the main will be part of your site investigations.

9. We have capacity for 10 people. Please include these requirements in your tender submission.

10. Yes, please provide unit rates only for desludging. Disposal will be on site and NPARC will arrange for all approvals.

11. May to October was put in the milestones because that aligns with the dry season. There is no "hard" requirement for be finished by end of October.

Sutherland Shire Council invites suitably qualified and experienced contractors to tender for the Prince Edward Park Woronora Pedestrian Bridge Renewal Project.

The project involves the demolition of the existing pedestrian bridge and the construction of a new bridge to provide a safe, compliant, and durable pedestrian and cyclist crossing over the Woronora River. publicQuestions.question:
Good morning,

We note that execution under Section 127 is required in multiple sections of the response document. As the document refers to an authorised signatory, could this please be amended to allow execution under Section 126?

Obtaining director signatures under Section 127 is a lengthy internal process and can take several weeks. Given the tender timeframe, we are unlikely to be able to secure the required director approvals prior to the closing date.

Should Reece be successful, we would be happy to arrange execution under Section 127 at the contract award stage. However, for the purposes of the tender submission, we would appreciate confirmation that execution by an authorised signatory under Section 126 is acceptable.

Thank you, and we look forward to your response.
publicQuestions.answer:
Signing the tender documents under ASIC 126 is acceptable. The tenderer may amend the Instrument of Tender at their end, as long as the person signing has the appropriate delegation and authority to bind the organisation to the submission.

SSROC's preference, if the tenderer is successful in their bid, is that the PSMA - the Preferred Supplier Master Agreement, being the contractual document, is signed under ASIC 127.

The tenders are to note that

•	the PSMA is in draft form until agreed and hence is not to be signed at this stage. It is to be signed on award

•	The PSA (Preferred Supplier Agreement) is executed on agreed engagement with the selected Participating Council. It is provided here as a sample copy

title: Home Recycling Service
description: Council is seeking a service provider to carry out collections of hard to recycle items from households as a separate home collection service in the Lane Cove Local Government Area (LGA). Items to be considered for acceptance include soft plastics, batteries, e-waste, small household electrical items, shoes, clothing, textiles, manchester, paint, blister packs, DVD’s, CD’s, and other tricky to recycle or problem wastes. Respondents are invited to include additional products that could be included in the collection for processing and reuse. Council has offered a collection service for problematic waste since August 2022. As of 1st July 2026, the service collects an average of 360 households per month and average annual collection of 45,000kgs.

vendorPanelDetails.queryCutoffAtRaw: Tuesday 03 November 2026 05:00 PM (AUS Eastern Daylight Time)
vendorPanelDetails.background:
Councils Sustainability Action Plan 2026-2030 (SAP) demonstrates Councils commitment to reducing waste to landfill and supporting a circular economy. As part of this commitment, Council aims to increase access to recycling options for problematic materials so as to divert materials from landfill and keep them in use at their highest value.

Council currently provides our residents with a 5-bin system for the separate collection of paper and cardboard recycling, container recycling, garden organics, food organics and residual wastes. An audit of the kerbside bins undertaken in 2023 found that residents generate an average of 8.2kg of residual waste per household per week. Of this, 13.14% was problematic wastes such as soft plastics (6.44%), textiles (5.79%) and electronic wastes including smoke detectors, printer cartridges, and batteries (0.91%).
vendorPanelDetails.desiredOutcomes:
Whilst Councils preference is to engage an organisation capable of collecting and arranging downstream processing of a wide range of recyclable items, we welcome proposals from organisations that can provide only part of the service.

Submissions may address:

•	collection-only (of materials taken to Council’s approved drop-off collection points); or

•	collection and processing of materials (either by the same organisations or through a direct agreement with third party organisations)

Solutions that follow the highest order of the waste hierarchy and prioritise re-use followed by recycling, recovery and disposal will be highly regarded.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi There, errors in price file

Schedule of Rates (identical in all three workbooks)

Errors on screen: The Min. Call Out Charge rows (items 2, 5, 8, 11 and 14) have "[##]" in the Qty column. That produces #VALUE! errors, which flow into those subtotals, the summary, the Total and the GST. The sheet can't calculate until someone enters a number. Council hasn't said what the minimum call-out hours are, so I wouldn't guess.

Sunday and "Other" rates left out of the total: Total Excluding GST (F56) adds only the first four summary lines. The Sunday and the two "Other" lines are left out.

"Other" subtotals miss rows: The "Other" business-hours subtotal (F37) skips items 22 and 23. The after-hours one (F47) skips items 30 and 31.

Theatre chairs line: Items 20 and 28 (deep clean of Her Majesty's Theatre chairs) appear in the A and B workbooks, although the theatre is a Category C venue.

Part-hourly rate: Items 3, 6, 9, 12 and 15 have a quantity of 0.5 hour and a rate "per 30m". If a bidder enters the price for a 30-minute block, the amount comes out at half of it. It needs clarifying how that rate should be entered.

title: CQURFQ-26-COMP10-DFM - Asbestos Register - Re-inspection
description:
CQUniversity (CQU) invites quotes from suitably qualified and licensed contractors to undertake comprehensive re-inspections of asbestos-containing materials (ACM) across multiple CQU campuses. The purpose of this engagement is to verify the current condition of known and presumed ACMs, identify any previously unrecorded ACMs, assess associated risks, and provide updated ACM survey reports and asbestos register information for each site.

Inspection and servicing must comply with all requirements of relevant Australian Standards, State and legislative requirements and industry best practices. The plan must be implemented with minimal disruption to campus operations, and all works must be performed to a standard that maintains compliance and achieves the agreed deliverables.

The University's five-year review is due by the end of November 2026.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
** ABOUT THE BEGA VALLEY **

The Bega Valley Shire is located at the south-eastern corner of New South Wales, halfway between Australia’s two largest cities, Sydney and Melbourne and three hours’ drive from the nation’s capital, Canberra.

Our coastal fringe extends from Wallaga Lake in the north to Cape Howe and the Victorian border in the south. Collectively this 225-kilometre section forms the beautiful Sapphire Coast, the heart of Australia’s Coastal Wilderness.

Our community vision explains our collective aspiration that we are an inclusive and welcoming community that integrates quality of life, prosperity, sustainable development and conservation of the environment. Our connection to Country is guided by the culture and heritage of our Traditional Owners.

** ABOUT COUNCIL **

Bega Valley Shire Council is responsible for providing all of the typical local government services across the Bega Valley Shire including maintaining a broad range of assets valued at over $1.7 billion that allow our visitors and community alike to live, work and play.

The Bega Valley Shire is governed by an elected Council comprising nine Councillors. Councillors provide leadership and establish policy and strategic direction for the organisation and the future of the shire.

Delivering the day to day services for council is a professional and dynamic staff cohort of over 560 people including full time, contract and casual positions.

Contractors to council play an important and valued role, assisting us delivering services and projects to the highest of standards and value for money.

** WHAT COUNCIL DOES **

Provide and maintain community facilities such as:
•	Parks and sportsgrounds
•	Playgrounds and skate parks
•	Sapphire Aquatic centre Pambula and swimming pools throughout the shire
•	Sports and recreation facilities throughout the Shire
•	Local libraries in Bega, Bermagui, Eden and Merimbula
•	Preschools and Childcare centres in Bega and Eden, and our Mobile service for Candelo and Bemboka
•	Merimbula Airport, Bega Saleyards and Cemeteries throughout the Shire

We care for the environment by:
•	Managing and enhancing bushland areas
•	Providing environmental and waste education and recycling services
•	Responding to pollution incidents and prosecuting polluters
•	Monitoring the water quality of the Shire’s estuaries
•	Planting trees and controlling noxious weeds
•	Beneficially recycling and reusing treated effluent

We create a safer place to live by:
•	Maintaining and improving roads, footpaths and stormwater drains
•	Working with emergency organisations such as the Rural Fire Service, State Emergency Service, NSW Police and NSW Surf Life Saving
•	Managing the keeping of companion animals
•	Inspecting food premises
•	Treating and supplying drinking water to our community
•	Treating sewage to a high standard to protect human health

We enhance our community by:
•	Listening to community views
•	Holding citizenship ceremonies, Australia Day Celebrations and the Seniors week luncheon known as the Golden Gig
•	Offering services for seniors, young people, new migrants and people with a disability
•	Providing grants to community organisations
•	Supporting local community groups such as sporting clubs, arts, migrant groups and charities
•	Encouraging and promoting volunteering in our communities

We plan for the future by:
•	Planning and managing the urban environment
•	Preserving heritage sites
•	Consulting with the community about its needs
•	Developing long term strategic plans for Council and the Shire

publicQuestions.question:
Hi,

Can you please clarify the following:

1. The drawings shows civil works (drainage, concrete etc). Is this part of the tender request?

2. In terms of pavement treatments for the roundabouts and 90 deg bend, why is there reference to MRWA Specifications when this is a Local Government road? Can the tenderer provide a design based on IPWEA/AfPA Specification?

3. Given the volatility in Bitumen prices at the moment, can the rates for asphalt be subject to rise and fall of bitumen?

publicQuestions.answer:
Please see answers to the questions below.

Concrete - Yes, concrete path reconstruction is to be included in the submission. Path construction works will be contained within the designated road reconstruction areas. Sections identified for asphalt resurfacing and profiling will be limited to profiling and asphalt works only, with no path construction proposed within these areas.

2.Yes, the concept design from the tenderer can be based on the IPWEA/AfPA. The City’s standard practice is to utilize MRWA specifications as a default project spec framework. However, the City of Busselton does adopt the IPWEA specifications where it best suits the project requirements within a local government area. We have no objections to the use of IPWEA specifications to develop the concept design.

3. The City is seeking a lump sum price for construction of these works. However, Tenderers may submit an alternative tender in accordance with clause 2.8 of RFT26-019 Request for Tender.

Mount Barker District Council seeks to engage suitably qualified contractors who are experienced in providing tree maintenance services under three separate works packages as follows:

vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
** ABOUT THE BEGA VALLEY **

The Bega Valley Shire is located at the south-eastern corner of New South Wales, halfway between Australia’s two largest cities, Sydney and Melbourne and three hours’ drive from the nation’s capital, Canberra.

Our coastal fringe extends from Wallaga Lake in the north to Cape Howe and the Victorian border in the south. Collectively this 225-kilometre section forms the beautiful Sapphire Coast, the heart of Australia’s Coastal Wilderness.

Our community vision explains our collective aspiration that we are an inclusive and welcoming community that integrates quality of life, prosperity, sustainable development and conservation of the environment. Our connection to Country is guided by the culture and heritage of our Traditional Owners.

** ABOUT COUNCIL **

Bega Valley Shire Council is responsible for providing all of the typical local government services across the Bega Valley Shire including maintaining a broad range of assets valued at over $1.7 billion that allow our visitors and community alike to live, work and play.

The Bega Valley Shire is governed by an elected Council comprising nine Councillors. Councillors provide leadership and establish policy and strategic direction for the organisation and the future of the shire.

Delivering the day to day services for council is a professional and dynamic staff cohort of over 560 people including full time, contract and casual positions.

Contractors to council play an important and valued role, assisting us delivering services and projects to the highest of standards and value for money.

** WHAT COUNCIL DOES **

Provide and maintain community facilities such as:
•	Parks and sportsgrounds
•	Playgrounds and skate parks
•	Sapphire Aquatic centre Pambula and swimming pools throughout the shire
•	Sports and recreation facilities throughout the Shire
•	Local libraries in Bega, Bermagui, Eden and Merimbula
•	Preschools and Childcare centres in Bega and Eden, and our Mobile service for Candelo and Bemboka
•	Merimbula Airport, Bega Saleyards and Cemeteries throughout the Shire

We care for the environment by:
•	Managing and enhancing bushland areas
•	Providing environmental and waste education and recycling services
•	Responding to pollution incidents and prosecuting polluters
•	Monitoring the water quality of the Shire’s estuaries
•	Planting trees and controlling noxious weeds
•	Beneficially recycling and reusing treated effluent

We create a safer place to live by:
•	Maintaining and improving roads, footpaths and stormwater drains
•	Working with emergency organisations such as the Rural Fire Service, State Emergency Service, NSW Police and NSW Surf Life Saving
•	Managing the keeping of companion animals
•	Inspecting food premises
•	Treating and supplying drinking water to our community
•	Treating sewage to a high standard to protect human health

We enhance our community by:
•	Listening to community views
•	Holding citizenship ceremonies, Australia Day Celebrations and the Seniors week luncheon known as the Golden Gig
•	Offering services for seniors, young people, new migrants and people with a disability
•	Providing grants to community organisations
•	Supporting local community groups such as sporting clubs, arts, migrant groups and charities
•	Encouraging and promoting volunteering in our communities

We plan for the future by:
•	Planning and managing the urban environment
•	Preserving heritage sites
•	Consulting with the community about its needs
•	Developing long term strategic plans for Council and the Shire

title: Queensland Government - Preferred Supplier Panel for Grocery, Dairy and Beverages
description:
Queensland Government is seeking applications from Suppliers who wish to register to be a Preferred Supplier for Grocery, Dairy and Beverage Products. This is a follow on from the initial application request period released on QTenders in March 2021 (HSQ101256). As part of this Preferred Supplier Panel we are accepting supplier applications at any time. Suppliers who have submitted an application via the initial registration process (HSQ101256) do not need to resubmit an application.

The Preferred Supplier Panel categories include:

Grocery Products Dry Goods

Biscuits; baking mixes and supplies; flour and milled products; soups; stocks; powders; packaged desserts; savoury snacks; confectionary; nuts; grains; legumes; jelly; spreads; jams; preserves; sugar; sweetener; dry pasta; rice; noodles; cereals; oats; porridge; pulses; seasoning; dried herbs; spices; sauces; dressing; canned goods; vinegar; condiments; dried fruit; dried vegetables; fruit cups pureed fruit.

Frozen Goods

Meat; poultry; fish and seafood; vegetables; fruit; pies; pastries; cakes; generic prepared frozen meals; muffins; desserts, ice cream and convenience foods.

Miscellaneous

Packaged (chilled or dry) smallgoods such as sliced meats, fats and oils; butter; margarine; eggs and egg products; tofu; hommus.

Dairy Products All milk products (such as white milk; flavoured milk; specialty milks (soy, Ultra-high treatment and lactose free milk); long life milk; powdered milk; evaporated milk; condensed milk; buttermilk); yoghurt; custard; cream; sour cream; cheese

Beverages Tea; coffee; chocolate powders; juice; cordial; spring water; soft drink; sports drinks.

The following Categories of ‘Groceries, Dairy and Beverages’ are excluded:

•Fresh Food (Vegetable, Meat and Bread Products)

•Texture modified foods

•Prepared meals for Therapeutic Diet Requirements of Texture Modified Diets

•Thickened fluids

•Kitchen Consumables

vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
Ipswich is centrally located in the booming south east Queensland region of Australia. To the east is the capital city Brisbane, and to the west are the rural and agricultural areas of the Brisbane, Lockyer and Fassifern Valleys. The city is ideally positioned on the national road network - 40 minutes drive from Brisbane, an hours drive from the Gold Coast and 60 minutes drive from domestic and international air and sea ports.
Ipswich comprises an area of 1090 square kms and has a population of 180,000 people. Ipswich enjoys a subtropical climate and is a safe, friendly and multicultural city. Residents come from 115 different ethnic backgrounds, speaking 84 languages.
As Queensland's oldest provincial city, Ipswich has a rich history. It is renowned for its architectural, natural and cultural heritage. Ipswich proudly preserves and still operates from many of its historical buildings and homes, with more than 6000 heritage-listed sites. Ipswich also has a range of charming townships within the western rural areas of the city, each with its own legitimate claims of historical significance.

title: Long-Term Reliability and System Strength Services for the North Country
description:
Reliability and System Strength Services for the North Country (Long-Term) - WS5659204351

The Coordinator of Energy has determined, under clause 3.11A.4 of the Electricity System Market (ESM) Rules, to trigger a Non-Co-optimised Essential System Services (NCESS) procurement process by Western Power for Reliability and System Strength Services for the North Country.

The proposed services aim to address reliability and system strength concerns during planned or unplanned outage events affecting one or more 132 kV transmission lines supplying the North Country.

Call for NCESS Submissions

Western Power invites NCESS Submissions from prospective NCESS providers to deliver Reliability Services and/or System Strength Services located in the North Country. The North Country is defined as the area supplied by the Rangeway, Geraldton and Chapman substations.

This tender relates to the Long-Term contract term option (10-25 year terms). Proponents may offer a solution that fully or partially meets the requirements for either service (or both).

Activation requirements, performance measures, preferred connection locations and other technical requirements are set out in the Final NCESS Service Specification.

Queries may be submitted by email to emerging.technology.portfolio@westernpower.com.au or via the Q&A function in the VendorPanel portal.

Please submit NCESS Submissions via VendorPanel no later than 5:00pm (AWST) on 1 February 2027.

Interested NCESS providers should register with VendorPanel to be informed of whether any supporting documentation such as clarifications to questions may be published.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
The Central Highlands region is in Central Queensland, Australia. The region encompasses an area of around 60 000 square kilometres, making it just short of the size of Tasmania.

It is home to around 30 000 people who live in the thirteen unique communities of Arcadia Valley, Bauhinia, Blackwater, Bluff, Capella, Comet, Dingo, Duaringa, Emerald, Rolleston, Sapphire Gemfields, Springsure and Tieri.

Our region is rich in minerals and agriculture, thriving on irrigation sourced from water storage on the Nogoa and Comet rivers. We claim the largest sapphire-producing fields in the Southern Hemisphere.

Major freight routes through the region include the north-south link between Charters Towers and northern New South Wales—identified as the inland transport alternative between Cairns and Melbourne.

publicQuestions.answer:
- 20 business day construction period / LDs – Pages 5 and 12:

Can we please check whether the 20 days is actually intended to be mandatory, because it seems very tight for the scope of works.

Response - The proposed date for Practical Completion has been amended to be 50 business days from the date of the Letter of Acceptance. A Notice To Tenderers will be issued separately confirming this change.

- Potholing / IFC drawings / pre-start – Pages 97, 98 and 100

Council requires potholing to be completed and any changes incorporated into For Construction drawings before the pre-start meeting. If potholing identifies a design issue, it may also require a Minor Change approval. 01-230176(C)_260925_TENDER_DOCU…

Can we confirm who is responsible for doing and paying for the required potholing, and whether the contract period only starts once the IFC drawings and pre-start approvals are in place? Traffic permits will be required for the potholing to take place.

Response - Contractor is responsible for undertaking service locating and shall allow for this. If design amendments are required these will be undertaken by the Principal. Timing for Practical Completion has been updated as per above.

- Rock and ground conditions – Pages 7 and 24 - Please confirm if the 100m3 of rock quantity will be adjusted to suit if the volume is exceeded.

Response - Rock quantity is a provisional allowance. All rock encountered will be subject to approval by the Superintendent.

- Insurance requirement – Pages 11 and 21 - Please confirm if PL insurance is to be 20 or 25M?

Response - Public Liability is to be 20 million as indicated within the Annexure.

- Please confirm if the contract will take 5% retention monies (e.g. 10% of each claim until 5% of the contract sum is reached) and no additional security will be taken.

Response - Retention moneys will be held (10% until 5%) as per the Annexure. Security will also be taken in accordance with the amounts listed in the Annexure.

publicQuestions.answer:

publicQuestions.question:
To ensure our submission fully aligns with the project requirements and expectations, we would appreciate the opportunity to participate in a tender walkthrough with the project team.

publicQuestions.answer: Unfortunately, time is not available for a meeting during the Tender period and this would not be fair and reasonable to other Tenderers. We believe sufficient information is contained within the Tender Documents however if you require clarifications please provide questions in this forum.

publicQuestions.question:
1. City permit lead times

Please confirm whether the Principal will lodge or has lodged the required City of Gold Coast LONO and road/footpath works permit applications prior to award. If permit approval exceeds 10 business days from lodgement, will the Date for Practical Completion be adjusted accordingly?

2. Live water connections

For BOQ items A8 and A9, please confirm whether the City of Gold Coast will undertake the shutdown and cut-in for both live water connections, with the Contractor responsible for excavation, fittings and reinstatement, or whether the Contractor is required to undertake the connections under City supervision. Please also confirm whether the shutdowns are expected to be carried out after hours.

3. Sewer manhole lid – A15

Drawing C250 Note 4 states that works on live sewers or maintenance holes are to be carried out by the SEQ service provider at the developer's cost. Please confirm whether BOQ item A15, replacement of the lid, frame and surround, is to be undertaken by the Contractor or the City. Please also confirm the A15 quantity of 8 m² relates to one manhole only (ID 000000009000105855).

4. RPEQ supervision and certification

Council Conditions 7 and 9 require RPEQ supervision and certification of the works. Please confirm that RPEQ supervision and completion certification will be provided by the Principal's engineer, Cozens Regan, and are excluded from the Contractor's scope.

5. Trench backfill

Please confirm whether suitable excavated material can be reused as trench backfill above the embedment zone within the verge, or whether imported material is required for the full trench depth.

6. Hydrant and fitting configuration

Please confirm whether the on-line hydrants at CH80, CH160, CH240 and CH320 are to be constructed using PE100 butt-welded tees or DI flanged tees with PE stub flanges, in accordance with City of Gold Coast requirements.

7. Site compound and access

Please confirm whether an area within Lot 37 will be available to the Contractor for site compound, plant storage, pipe stringing and stockpiling, or whether all activities must be contained within the road reserve.

8. Clearing and kerb works

The Job Specification includes clauses for tree clearing, kerb and channel works (Clause 10) and road surfacing (Clause 11), which do not appear to be shown on the drawings or BOQ. Please confirm whether these clauses apply to this contract.

9. Defects and maintenance period

Annexure A states a 14-month defects liability period, while Council Condition 6 states a 12-month maintenance period. Please confirm the applicable Contractor defects liability/maintenance period and whether the City's maintenance bond under Schedule 1 Clause 4.7 is to be provided by the Principal.
publicQuestions.answer:
Please see response below

1. All required permits to construct the works are the responsibility of the Contractor. The Contract duration period has been extended as per Notice To Tenderers No 2 which provides additional time to obtain necessary permits.

2. All live connections are to be undertaken by the Contractor. Allow for connections be undertaken during business hours and make this clear in the submission.

3. Works to the sewer manhole are to be undertaken by the Contractor. Item A15 should be priced as an Item, the 8m2 is a typo.

4. RPEQ Supervision will be provided by the Principals Engineer at the Principals cost.

5. Excavated material can be reused for backfill above the embedment zone, provided it is clean and free of large particles.

6. On-line hydrants at CH80, CH160, CH240 and CH320 are to be constructed using DI flanged tees with PE stub flanges.

7. Lot 37 will be available to the Contractor for site compound, plant storage, pipe stringing and stockpiling.

8. If the referenced items in the specification are not contained in the drawings or BOQ they are not required to be included.

9. Defects Liability Period for the Contract works will be for 14 months. The Maintenance Bond will be provided by the Principal.

title: Council Facilities Minor Works, Asset Maintenance and Associated Services Standing Offer Agreement
description:
Scenic Rim Regional Council is situated in South-East Queensland, recognised for its stunning landscapes and vibrant communities. The Council is dedicated to enhancing the quality of life for residents and visitors through sustainable development and economic growth, partnering with reputable contractors to support ongoing projects.

The Scenic Rim Regional Council is inviting tenders for the supply of minor works, asset maintenance and associated services to Council properties and assets throughout the Scenic Rim Region. The initial contract term is two (2) years, from 1 November 2026 to 31?October 2028, with two (2) optional 12-month extensions exercisable at Council’s sole discretion.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerAddress:
82 Brisbane St
Beaudesert, Queensland 4285
Australia
vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
The Scenic Rim region is a thriving rural paradise set in the foothills of the Great Dividing Range and surrounded by world heritage listed national parks. Home to a population of more than 37,780, the region covers 4248sq km and is located an hour south of Brisbane and an hour inland from the Gold Coast. Known for its breathtaking scenery, it is a popular tourist destination offering visitors plenty to see and do. From its myriad of wineries and art galleries to expansive bushwalking tracks, state of the art equine facilities, growing rural communities and friendly country charm, the Scenic Rim region is a must see destination.

Its main towns are Beaudesert, Boonah, Rathdowney, Kooralbyn, Kalbar, Aratula, Canungra, Tamborine Mountain, Harrisville and Peak Crossing. The region's primary businesses are agricultural/horticultural production, the equine industry and tourism/ecotourism. The Scenic Rim region contains more than 30,000 hectares of parkland, including national parks and council controlled parks. The region also contains three dams: Lake Moogerah, Lake Maroon and Wyaralong Dam. Supported by a thriving economy, a farming industry and a vibrant arts community, the Scenic Rim has a strong community spirit and friendly locals.

publicQuestions.question: Please clarify whether we can adjust Part E - Pricing Schedule to align with our pricing model? Part A says we can, but Part E itself says we can't.
