publicQuestions.question:

“Respondents must print and complete the above Tender Form in Schedule 8, as part of the Tender submission”

publicQuestions.question:
Clarification of Insurance Requirements.

Could you please provide further clarity around the requested Third Party insurance requested on Tab 1. Respondent Details of VP506370_Council_Minor_Works__Asset_Maintenance_and_Associated_Services_Par (4), item 18 – Insurances?

The requirement is given as QLD, rather than Not Applicable as for some other insurances so it appears to be a requirement.

However, it is not specified in 3.3 Mandatory Requirements – Insurances of VP506370_Council_Minor_Works__Asset_Maintenance_and_Associated_Services_Par (3), Part C – Scope of Works. This document specifies Public & Product Liability, Workers Compensation Insurance, Professional Indemnity and Motor Vehicle Insurances as mandatory.

In conflict to the scope of works, the description of the third party insurance given in the Conditions of Tender, VP506370_Council_Minor_Works__Asset_Maintenance_and_Associated_Services_Par (2) – 4.3 Insurance Requirements, is “Third-Party Insurance: Insurance to cover liability for any damages or injuries caused to third parties as a result of the tenderer's operations”. This appears to indicate that the third party insurance is a requirement of the tender.

From speaking to other respondents, the inclusion of QLD as the requirement for the third party insurance has prompted some to assume it was referring to vehicle CTP insurance, however this doesn’t match to the tender documents description.

-	Is Public & Product Liability insurance mandatory and do you have to have the existing policies extended to include the name of Council as principal as the specified in the scope of works section 3.3?
publicQuestions.answer:

For your clarification:

1. Third Party Car insurance is generally included with full comprehensive car insurance

3. Minimum motor vehicle insurance is $20 million

4. Product liability is not required. Public Liability Insurance is.

whether "minor roofing, waterproofing and flashing" is limited to roof plumbing and flashings

publicQuestions.answer:

publicQuestions.answer: Please see the added Addenda that adds additional scope for landscaping.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi,

Thank you for confirming that subcontractors may deliver the relevant services subject to Council approval, and that Professional Indemnity Insurance is not required.

Could Council please clarify one final insurance point for a contractor intending to subcontract all on-site service delivery?

Is the principal contractor itself required to hold the specified $20 million Public Liability Insurance and $30 million Motor Vehicle Insurance, or can these requirements be satisfied by Council-approved subcontractors who perform the on-site works and hold the required levels of insurance?

The principal contractor would remain responsible for contract management, scheduling, quality assurance and compliance.

Thank you,

Simon O'Donnell

Supreme Surface Refresh
publicQuestions.answer:
Thanks for your continuing enquires Simon,

After discussion with the Facilities Coordinator, we have determined that Motor Vehicle Insurance is $20 Million.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi,

Thank you for the clarification.

Supreme Surface Refresh does not own or operate any motor vehicles in connection with the proposed contract. All on-site services, including transport to and from Council sites, would be performed by Council-approved subcontractors using their own vehicles and holding their own motor vehicle insurance.

In this circumstance, is Supreme Surface Refresh still required to hold a $20 million Motor Vehicle Insurance policy despite having no vehicle to insure, or would the motor vehicle insurance requirement apply to the subcontractors operating the vehicles?

Thank you,

Simon O'Donnell

Supreme Surface Refresh
publicQuestions.answer:
Hello,

As the responsible contractor, Supreme Surface Refresh would be be responsible for all relevant insurances and requirements to the people you employ if you so choose to subcontract or not.

publicQuestions.question: Could Council please provide an indicative historical annual spend or approximate annual work volume for the Cleaning – Buildings, High Pressure Cleaning, Gutter Vac, Graffiti Removal and Solar Panel Cleaning category? Alternatively, could Council provide an indicative number or value range of work orders issued annually for comparable cleaning services? publicQuestions.answer:
At this stage, the tender is focused on establishing an hourly rate for service provision across the region, rather than pricing individual assets. As such, a detailed asset list is not required for tender pricing and will be provided to the successful Contractor as needed for service delivery.

As such a historical annual result does not exist for publication.

Wentworth Street, Bellerive - Stormwater Upgrade

T1586-25

Tenders are invited from suitably qualified Contractors for the above.

A pre-tender site briefing is scheduled for 10:30am on Wednesday 16 September 2026, on site. Attendance is recommended but is not mandatory. Please register your interest with the contact officer for the pre-tender site briefing.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
Clarence City Council (or City of Clarence) is a local government body in Tasmania, and one of the five municipalities that constitutes the Greater Hobart Area. The Clarence local government area has a population of 56,945, covering the eastern shore of the Derwent River from Otago to the South Arm Peninsula and the smaller localities of Cambridge, Richmond, and Seven Mile Beach.

The administrative centre and main commercial district of Clarence is Rosny Park, approximately 5 kilometres from the CBD of Hobart. Bellerive Oval lies immediately to the south, and the Hobart International Airport is located further north-west along the Tasman Highway.

title: Depena Cafe
description:
Bayside Council invites suitably experienced and qualified Contractors to submit a tender for the demolition of the existing Le Beach Hut and Dolls Point Café building and the construction of a new restaurant, kiosk and public amenities building at 179 Russell Avenue, Dolls Point NSW. The Le Beach Hut was constructed in the 1950s and is located on Lot 67-70 on Deposited Plan 2237 within the Peter Depena Reserve.

Bayside Council anticipates awarding the Contract in March 2027, subject to completion of the procurement process. Site establishment is expected to commence upon execution of the contract. Tenderers must all hold their submitted prices valid until contract award.

Further information regarding the project background, existing conditions and description of the works is included within Appendix A - Project Overview.

A mandatory site inspection will be held on Tuesday, 29 September 2026 at 2:00 pm. The meeting point is the loading bay adjacent to Coffee in the Park Café.

Attendance will be recorded and only Contractors who attend the site inspection will be eligible to submit a conforming tender.

Tenderers are strongly encouraged to review all tender documents prior to attending the inspection. While queries may be submitted following the inspection via VendorPanel, this will be the only opportunity to inspect and photograph the restaurant and cafe's internal areas and to seek clarification of project requirements in person.

Tenderers should attend fully prepared with any questions. Any subcontractors, consultants, or other parties whose advice will be relied upon in preparing the tender may also attend.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
The Le Beach Hut is a single level building comprising a restaurant and a separate kiosk. The building’s total floor area is approximately 830m2. The restaurant is located on the eastern side of the building and has a floor area of approximately 650m2. Primary access to the restaurant is via Carruthers Drive and secondary access is available from Peter Depena Reserve. The kiosk is located on the western side of the building and has a floor area of approximately 180m2.

The building is constructed on concrete foundations which are in fair condition. The brick perimeter walls have been partially rendered and the roof is timber construction with a metal cover. The condition of the load bearing walls is poor to fair and the roof structure, roof cover and general external finishes are in poor condition with significant deterioration.

The perimeter metal frame windows, fittings and fitments have severely corroded and moving parts are limited in terms of functionality. The timber frame windows are also in very poor condition with significant deterioration. A roof mounted antenna has collapsed and is not functional.

publicQuestions.question:
1. Ausgrid: What has been accepted, designed and paid for; who funds ASP/3, ASP/1, Ausgrid fees and the existing substation upgrade; and what energisation date should tenderers program?

2. Approvals: Current status of the section 4.55 modification, CC1/CC2, lot consolidation and any outstanding Sydney Water or authority approvals; identify the party responsible for each condition and fee.

3. Documents: Issue the promised BOQ and confirm when the structural, hydraulic, electrical, mechanical, civil, food-service and roof safety construction drawing sets will be available. They appear in the tender index but were not among the files supplied to me; the combined architectural set does contain its architectural sheets.

4. Ground and hazardous materials: Confirm the payment mechanism for concealed asbestos or contaminated material outside the surveyed areas, additional waste classification, groundwater control and unknown services, given item 37’s risk allocation.

5. Document control: Appendix F’s repeated page header says “DA-2024/128 — Sir Joseph Banks Park”, and one line within it retains that DA number, while its project field and the actual consent identify DA-2024/374 Depena Café. Request a corrected CC matrix and confirmation that every assigned condition has been checked against the actual consent.

6. Fees: Contract Information item 14A says the contractor does not pay the long service levy, while the CC matrix labels its $14,051 payment as a contractor requirement. Ask Council to reconcile this and the housing contribution and certification fees before pricing.
publicQuestions.answer:
1. Ausgrid: What has been accepted, designed and paid for; who funds ASP/3, ASP/1, Ausgrid fees and the existing substation upgrade; and what energisation date should tenderers program?

Council has engaged Sam Crawford Architects, who in turn has engaged JN Electrical Consultant to undertake the ASP3 design for the Ausgrid electricity supply upgrade. The ASP3 scope includes:

 1. 1 x 400A LV Direct Distributor Design as per the Ausgrid offer.

 2. Low voltage underground design activities including field measurements and BYDA searches.

 3. Preparation of Concept plan and notification to council and as required under the T&I SEPP, Part 5 of the EPA&A Act (1979) and Electricity Supply Act s45 – providing 40-day notification.

 4. Preparation of Standard Ausgrid Environmental Impact Assessment (SER).

 5. Preparation of all standard Ausgrid documentation required for design submission and certification to RFT stage.

 6. Attendance of 1 off pre-construction meeting with Ausgrid Contract Inspector and selected L1 ASP contractor allowed for in Part A scope. Additional meetings charged at hourly rates as part of RFC stage – only where required.

 7. Alterations to designs at RFC stage requiring recertification is excluded and charged at hourly rates or for an agreed fee depending upon scope.

The ASP3 design is currently being finalised and has not yet received Ausgrid approval. Will provide a preliminary ASP3 drawing named ‘ASP3 PRELIM Design Drawings - Depena Cafe’ in Addendum 02. Note the design is preliminary.

The successful contractor will be responsible for engaging an ASP1 contractor to undertake the electrical works in accordance with the approved ASP3 design, including coordination with Ausgrid for construction, commissioning and energisation.

Council has funded the ASP3 design consultant engagement. Tenderers should allow for all costs associated with the ASP1 works, Ausgrid coordination, approvals, inspections, fees and charges required to complete the electrical supply upgrade.

As the ASP3 design has not yet been approved by Ausgrid, an energisation date cannot be confirmed at this stage. Tenderers should liaise with their proposed ASP1 contractor and Ausgrid when developing their construction programme and allow sufficient time for Ausgrid approvals, construction, commissioning and energisation activities.

2. Approvals: Current status of the section 4.55 modification, CC1/CC2, lot consolidation and any outstanding Sydney Water or authority approvals; identify the party responsible for each condition and fee.

Below is the status as of 28/09/2026:

 • S4.55(1A) to be submitted to Council early October 2026

 • CC1 to be submitted by Contractor once engaged

 • CC2 to be managed by future tenant

 • Lot Consolidation managed by Council. Should be finalised by February 2027

 • Council has engaged Opal Water Management (Water Services Coordinator) for S73, sewer minor works design and Building Plan Approval. Contractor’s plumber to liaise with SW for tap-in. Contractor to liaise directly with Opal Water Management.

 • All authority fees to be paid by Contractor. Please indicate a cost for all Authority Fees in Tender Schedule - Schedule of Lump Sums

3. Documents: Issue the promised BOQ and confirm when the structural, hydraulic, electrical, mechanical, civil, food-service and roof safety construction drawing sets will be available. They appear in the tender index but were not among the files supplied to me; the combined architectural set does contain its architectural sheets.

 • Council has reconfirmed that all drawings were included in the RFT package. Please advise if there are still issues downloading the file

 • Addendum 01 – Depena Café zip file was issued on Friday 25th September which included the BOQ excel file and updated Tender Schedule - Schedule of Lump Sums

4. Ground and hazardous materials: Confirm the payment mechanism for concealed asbestos or contaminated material outside the surveyed areas, additional waste classification, groundwater control and unknown services, given item 37’s risk allocation.

Contractors are to satisfy themselves as to existing site conditions and include for reasonable investigation of the site, including obtaining Before You Dig Australia records, service locating and geotechnical investigations. Existing information available to Council has been provided as part of the RFT documentation.

Groundwater management and dewatering measures required to satisfy the Development Consent, including Condition 57, are to be included within the tendered price.

Council has engaged geotechnical consultant, Aretas Group, who has installed a groundwater monitoring well. Groundwater monitoring, laboratory testing and reporting are currently underway, with results anticipated in mid-October 2026. Any information available prior to RFT closing will be issued to tenderers by addendum.

In relation to concealed asbestos, contamination outside surveyed areas, unexpected waste classifications, groundwater conditions and unidentified services, any entitlement to additional payment will be assessed in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Contract and the risk allocation set out in the RFT documentation. Tenderers should identify any assumptions, exclusions or departures in their submissions.

5. Document control: Appendix F’s repeated page header says “DA-2024/128 — Sir Joseph Banks Park”, and one line within it retains that DA number, while its project field and the actual consent identify DA-2024/374 Depena Café. Request a corrected CC matrix and confirmation that every assigned condition has been checked against the actual consent.

Will provide the updated file named ‘F - CC Conditions Matrix 260928’ in Addendum 02.

6. Fees: Contract Information item 14A says the contractor does not pay the long service levy, while the CC matrix labels its $14,051 payment as a contractor requirement. Ask Council to reconcile this and the housing contribution and certification fees before pricing.

Contractor to pay all fees.

Community Transport is a key enabler of economic and community participation. The purpose of this procurement activity is to purchase community transport services in 5 locations listed in Section 1 Part 5 below. This funding is targeting locations that have been assessed as requiring a service as they are areas where there is no current provision.

title: 201222 Minor Works Construction Panel
description:
Council is seeking to establish a panel of suitably qualified contractors to deliver minor construction, refurbishment, repair, installation and associated trade services across its owned and managed assets.

The panel will provide a flexible and efficient procurement mechanism for engaging pre-qualified suppliers to undertake minor works activities valued at up to $250,000 (including GST) per engagement. Services may be required across a diverse range of Council facilities and infrastructure, including community buildings, sporting and recreational facilities, parks, depots, commercial properties, heritage assets and public amenities. Contractors will be required to provide all labour, materials, plant, equipment, supervision, permits and associated resources necessary to complete assigned works.

This panel will support Council asset management, service delivery and capital works objectives by ensuring timely access to capable contractors, improving procurement efficiency, reducing project delivery timeframes and maintaining the safety, functionality and value of Council assets.

This panel contract is intended for the delivery of minor construction works with an individual project, work order, quotation or engagement value not exceeding $250,000 (including GST). Council reserves the right to determine the suitability of works for procurement through this panel and may elect to undertake separate procurement processes for projects exceeding this threshold.

title: Remove and Replace Roof Structures, Opal Street WTP Filters
description:
Central Highlands Regional Council operates the Opal Street Water Treatment Plant (WTP) located in Emerald, Queensland. The WTP incorporates four rapid gravity sand filters which form a critical component of the potable water treatment process.

Each filter is currently protected by an individual structural steel roof structure. Over time, these roof structures have deteriorated and are approaching the end of their serviceable life. In addition to their deteriorated condition, the existing roof structures do not adequately facilitate the operational requirements associated with periodic filter media replacement.

During future filter media replacement campaigns, one-tonne bulk sandbags are required to be lowered into the filter compartments via crane. The existing roof structures do not provide suitable openings through which these bags can be safely lowered into the filters. This creates operational difficulties and increases risk during maintenance activities.

Central Highlands Regional Council is seeking responses from suitably qualified and experienced contractors to undertake the design, removal, disposal, supply and construction of replacement roof structures over the four rapid gravity filters.

The replacement roof structures must incorporate suitable access openings that facilitate the future lowering of one-tonne bulk bags of filter media into each filter compartment by others under a separate contract.

The Works are to be delivered under a Design and Construct Contract.

The Contractor must provide all labour, design services, engineering services, supervision, plant, equipment, materials, transport, certifications and incidentals required to complete the Works.

The Works include, but are not limited to:

• Site inspection and verification of existing conditions.

• Detailed design of replacement roof structures for four rapid gravity sand filters.

• Structural design certification by a Registered Professional Engineer of Queensland (RPEQ).

• Preparation and submission of design documentation and drawings.

• Attendance at, facilitation of and incorporation of feedback from an 80% design review workshop with Central Highlands Regional Council Water Utilities personnel. The Contractor must present theproposed design, demonstrate how operational requirements have been addressed, and provide draft design documentation for review prior to finalisation of the design.

• Removal and lawful disposal of existing roof structures. This includes the temporary covering of the sand filter opening to avoid any contaminants entering the filter media.

• Supply and installation of new roof structures.

• Provision of access openings to facilitate future filter media replacement activities.

• Supply and installation of all structural steelwork, roofing, flashings, lighting, stormwater runoff piping to prevent filter contamination, fixings and protective coatings.

• Final inspection and commissioning.

• Provision of as-constructed drawings and documentation.

• Handover of the completed Works.

The Contractor must be responsible for delivering a complete and fit-for-purpose solution.

Prior to commencing work on site, the Contractor must prepare, submit, revise and implement project-specific management plans suitable for the Works, including safety/WHS, environmental, quality, demolition, construction methodology/site management and traffic/pedestrian/access management plans, as applicable.

The replacement of filter media is specifically excluded from this Contract and will be undertaken by others under a separate contract.

Where the Opal St WTP Filter Media Replacement technical specification prepared by AECOM is provided with this RFT, only Sections 3.0 Materials and Construction, 4.0 Design and Documentation and 5.0 Roof Structure Removal and Reinstatement apply to this Contract, and only to the extent relevant to the design, removal, disposal, supply and construction of replacement roof structures. All other sections of that document are provided for information only unless expressly referenced in this Specification. In the event of inconsistency, this Specification takes precedence.

The Contractor must supply all labour, supervision, engineering services, design services, plant, equipment, materials, transport, temporary works and incidentals necessary to complete the Works.

The Works must be undertaken at the Opal Street Water Treatment Plant, Opal Street, Emerald, Queensland.

The Contract will commence within 7 days after the Award Letter and Contractual Arrangement are provided to and signed by the successful Contractor. Central Highlands Regional Council anticipates the contract end date to be as per the approved contract schedule.

title: Finniss Street Multi Storey Car Park - Stormwater & Structural improvement works
description:
The Town of Gawler invites quotes from Respondents for the provision of Finniss Street Multi Storey Car Park - Structural and Stormwater Works.

The Finniss Street Multi Storey Car Park is an important public asset supporting access to the Gawler town centre. A condition assessment undertaken by Tonkin Consulting Pty Ltd in 2020 identified structural and stormwater deficiencies, including cracking to precast wall panels, floor slabs, slab edges and areas adjacent to internal columns, corrosion of structural bolts and Bondek metal formwork, and inadequate stormwater management resulting in water ponding and basement flooding.

Council has allocated funding in the 2026/27 financial year to address these defects and improve the long-term performance, safety and serviceability of the facility. The project will involve engaging a suitably qualified contractor to undertake structural remediation and stormwater improvement works.

The scope includes repair of concrete cracking, treatment of exposed/corroded reinforcement, remediation and protective coating of corroded Bondek, and replacement of corroded bolts and missing or damaged fixings. Stormwater works include upgrading the existing Level 1 sump, constructing concrete plinths and road humps on Levels 3/4 to improve surface flow paths, and designing, installing and commissioning a new pump station to discharge basement stormwater to the street drainage system.

The Contractor will provide all labour, materials, plant, supervision, temporary works, barricading and traffic management. The car park will remain operational, with localised work areas closed as required.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
** ABOUT THE BEGA VALLEY **

The Bega Valley Shire is located at the south-eastern corner of New South Wales, halfway between Australia’s two largest cities, Sydney and Melbourne and three hours’ drive from the nation’s capital, Canberra.

Our coastal fringe extends from Wallaga Lake in the north to Cape Howe and the Victorian border in the south. Collectively this 225-kilometre section forms the beautiful Sapphire Coast, the heart of Australia’s Coastal Wilderness.

Our community vision explains our collective aspiration that we are an inclusive and welcoming community that integrates quality of life, prosperity, sustainable development and conservation of the environment. Our connection to Country is guided by the culture and heritage of our Traditional Owners.

** ABOUT COUNCIL **

Bega Valley Shire Council is responsible for providing all of the typical local government services across the Bega Valley Shire including maintaining a broad range of assets valued at over $1.7 billion that allow our visitors and community alike to live, work and play.

The Bega Valley Shire is governed by an elected Council comprising nine Councillors. Councillors provide leadership and establish policy and strategic direction for the organisation and the future of the shire.

Delivering the day to day services for council is a professional and dynamic staff cohort of over 560 people including full time, contract and casual positions.

Contractors to council play an important and valued role, assisting us delivering services and projects to the highest of standards and value for money.

** WHAT COUNCIL DOES **

Provide and maintain community facilities such as:
•	Parks and sportsgrounds
•	Playgrounds and skate parks
•	Sapphire Aquatic centre Pambula and swimming pools throughout the shire
•	Sports and recreation facilities throughout the Shire
•	Local libraries in Bega, Bermagui, Eden and Merimbula
•	Preschools and Childcare centres in Bega and Eden, and our Mobile service for Candelo and Bemboka
•	Merimbula Airport, Bega Saleyards and Cemeteries throughout the Shire

We care for the environment by:
•	Managing and enhancing bushland areas
•	Providing environmental and waste education and recycling services
•	Responding to pollution incidents and prosecuting polluters
•	Monitoring the water quality of the Shire’s estuaries
•	Planting trees and controlling noxious weeds
•	Beneficially recycling and reusing treated effluent

We create a safer place to live by:
•	Maintaining and improving roads, footpaths and stormwater drains
•	Working with emergency organisations such as the Rural Fire Service, State Emergency Service, NSW Police and NSW Surf Life Saving
•	Managing the keeping of companion animals
•	Inspecting food premises
•	Treating and supplying drinking water to our community
•	Treating sewage to a high standard to protect human health

We enhance our community by:
•	Listening to community views
•	Holding citizenship ceremonies, Australia Day Celebrations and the Seniors week luncheon known as the Golden Gig
•	Offering services for seniors, young people, new migrants and people with a disability
•	Providing grants to community organisations
•	Supporting local community groups such as sporting clubs, arts, migrant groups and charities
•	Encouraging and promoting volunteering in our communities

We plan for the future by:
•	Planning and managing the urban environment
•	Preserving heritage sites
•	Consulting with the community about its needs
•	Developing long term strategic plans for Council and the Shire

title: WT25-25/26 Pechey PAC Dosing and WTP Upgrades
description:
Toowoomba Regional Council (TRC) is seeking quotations for the supply and installation of a new Powdered Activated Carbon (PAC) dosing system. This PAC system is to be installed at the Pechey Water Treatment Plant located on Grapetree Road. The scope of works involved are detailed in this document and consists of a mixture of mechanical, electrical, and control systems integration.

The existing PAC dosing system and layout has resulted in issues such as improper powder feed, blockages, inaccurate dosing, and corrosion of the hopper frame. Due to these issues and the age of the unit, Council is looking at replacing this PAC dosing system.

To cater for the new PAC dosing system, several Control System upgrades are required to be undertaken. This includes a PLC Platform upgrade and the installation of a new RIO network. Several other plant modifications are also required including waste pit level instrument control, automated UV duty selection and ATV600 upgrade.

Pechey Water Treatment Plant is located north of Toowoomba in the Pechey State Forest along Grapetree Rd, QLD 4355.

A non-mandatory site inspection is scheduled for Thursday 27th August 2026 at 10am AEST. Offerors are encouraged to attend this site inspection. Refer to the Annexure to Conditions of Offering within the Conditions of Offer document for further information including Council contact details and registering for the site inspection.

Pensar seeks clarification on the queries below, which relate to conflicting specification requirements and information required to accurately scope and price the works:

1. There is conflicting information regarding the Fibre Optic Cable. The provided General Electrical Installation spec (ELE-SPEC-001) references.

- Section 7.14.2 Fibre Optic Cabling: All in-plant control systems networks and patch leads (Remote I/O LAN, PLC LAN, SCADA LAN), fibre optic cabling shall be 50/125 µm (OM2) multi-mode glass fibre type cable.

- In Appendix A: Preferred Managed Ethernet Switches are Moxa EDS-5xxA-T Series.

The provided Principal’s Project Requirements (Contract Annexure Part E) references:

- First page, bullet point: Install vermin resistant (armoured) Single Mode Optical Fibre cabling between the Switchroom and the PAC dosing system. This shall include FOBOT installation at both ends.

 The provided Principal’s Project Requirements (Contract Annexure Part E) references:

- Section 3.4 PAC RIO Integration: The RIO shall be connected to the main WTP PLC using simple Daisy Chain Loop via parallel cores of the multicore fibre cable

- Section 3.4 PAC RIO Integration: Councils preferred switch with fibre capabilities is Planet Technologies ISW-621TF with MFB-TF20 SFP modules (Our engineers tell me this hardware seems to be more appropriate for connecting long distances to sites that don’t require a managed switch for redundant loops. And would likely require attenuators to be installed due to the short distance (50m) run.

Can TRC confirm whether the fibre is to be multi-mode or single-mode, and which brand (and series) of Ethernet Switches are required?

2. Shutdown windows

- Section 8 of the RFO allows the plant to be taken offline for "short periods of time (4hrs)" within the 20-day window, but states no maximum duration. Can TRC confirm the maximum continuous shutdown duration that will be approved?

- Can TRC confirm the frequency of approved shutdowns (e.g. one 8-hour shut per day, twice a week, or five days a week) and the required plant recovery period between shutdowns?

- Can TRC confirm whether a multi-day continuous outage would be considered for the PLC platform cutover, subject to an approved cut-over plan?

Existing plant documentation

- Can TRC provide the current Functional Description (Parts A and B) and any design report for the existing plant, to show how the plant currently operates and its condition?

- Can TRC provide the current PLC I/O list, to allow control systems pricing to reflect the actual scope?

- Can TRC provide the as-constructed electrical drawings for the site, including layout drawings?

- Can TRC provide the existing switchboard drawings and photographs behind the 415V escutcheons and doors, relevant to the VSD replacement in the existing switchboard?
publicQuestions.answer:
Question: Can TRC confirm whether the fibre is to be multi-mode or single-mode, and which brand (and series) of Ethernet Switches are required?

Council Response: With Planet Technologies ISW-621TF hardware, neither multi or single mode fibre modules require attenuators over a 50m run. Council uses this configuration without issue at other sites. MFB-TF20 single mode modules are to be used.

Question: Can TRC confirm the maximum continuous shutdown duration that will be approved?

Council Response: The maximum shutdown that will be guaranteed to be approved is 4 hours. However, depending on operational constraints, weather and other contributing factors this could be extended by agreement at the time of the works. For further reference, works completed between October – March summer period will typically have less flexibility for the maximum outage duration. Works in Winter months (~March onwards) have more flexibility. The long term rainfall will also affect the maximum outage time.

Question: Can TRC confirm the frequency of approved shutdowns (e.g. one 8-hour shut per day, twice a week, or five days a week) and the required plant recovery period between shutdowns?

Council Response: Council can guarantee 1 x 4hr shutdown, twice per week on non-consecutive days. This will be governed by recovery periods during works, which are impacted as per the above, but typically 2 days recovery is sufficient.

Question: Can TRC confirm whether a multi-day continuous outage would be considered for the PLC platform cutover, subject to an approved cut-over plan?

Council Response: No multi-day continuous outages would be considered.

Question: Can TRC provide the current Functional Description (Parts A and B) and any design report for the existing plant, to show how the plant currently operates and its condition?

Council Response: Council can provide the Functional Description directly to your approved integrator if you provide details. Council will not provide this information to parties not bound under its system integration panel. If you wish to pursue this please email Ben.John@tr.qld.gov.au with the name of your integrator.

Question: Can TRC provide the current PLC I/O list, to allow control systems pricing to reflect the actual scope?

Response: Council can provide the I/O list directly to your approved integrator if you provide details. Council will not provide this information to parties not bound under its system integration panel. If you wish to pursue this please email Ben.John@tr.qld.gov.au with the name of your integrator.

Question: Can TRC provide the as-constructed electrical drawings for the site, including layout drawings?

Response: Council can provide a view only link to the As-Constructed Drawings for the site, however Council cannot guarantee all modifications that occurred on site have been reflected in the changes. If you wish to pursue this please email Ben.John@tr.qld.gov.au with the email address you wish to have the files shared to.

Question: Can TRC provide the existing switchboard drawings and photographs behind the 415V escutcheons and doors, relevant to the VSD replacement in the existing switchboard?

Response: Council can provide a view only link to the As-Constructed Drawings for the site, however Council cannot guarantee all modifications that occurred on site have been reflected in the changes. publicQuestions.question:
Please see below queries:

1. Council to provide any preferred vendors for valves, pipes, cables, instrumentation and other bulk items.

2. Council to specify any site induction requirements

3. Please provide piping spec for the UPVC pipes to be installed

4. Please provide datasheets for the pneumatic valves for the UV system. Please advise of the OEM and model number of the UV system or possibly IOM/spare parts list from the UV OEM

5. Please provide typical or standard trenching details for the buried UPVC piping

6. From PPR Clause 4, the new booster pumps shall be sized to provide sufficient flowrate and pressure for the services in the treatment plant, can the Council confirm the total duty required (flow and head) for the pump set both for the PAC dosing system and the required services for the WTP?

7. Council to provide existing P&ID, Functional description and Control philosophy relevant to the SOW

Thank you and hope to hear from you the soonest.
publicQuestions.answer:
1. Council to provide any preferred vendors for valves, pipes, cables, instrumentation and other bulk items.

The preferred suppliers and specifications can be found in the attached MEC-SPEC and ELE SPEC documents. Anything not listed here or in Part D and E of the AS4906 contract can be Tenderer’s choice however relevant Australian Standards must be met.

2. Council to specify any site induction requirements

Council uses an online system called Beakon which will be provided to the successful Tenderers. A brief on site induction will be conducted by a Council representative during the first on-site meeting.

3. Please provide piping spec for the UPVC pipes to be installed

uPVC piping should be rated for a minimum of PN16, but based on the maximum pressure of the Tenderer’s service water pump selection e.g. higher maximum discharge may require higher ratings. Barrel unions should be used to allow for future maintenance when required.

4. Please provide datasheets for the pneumatic valves for the UV system. Please advise of the OEM and model number of the UV system or possibly IOM/spare parts list from the UV OEM

There are no pneumatic valves currently fitted to the UV system, these are manual handwheel operated butterfly valves currently. TRC’s preferred provider for the new pneumatic valves is Challenger Valves. The OEM UV system is a Wedeco Spektron 250e.

5. Please provide typical or standard trenching details for the buried UPVC piping

Buried uPVC should be uniformly bedded according to WSAA standard requirements with a minimum cover of 600mm.

6. From PPR Clause 4, the new booster pumps shall be sized to provide sufficient flowrate and pressure for the services in the treatment plant, can the Council confirm the total duty required (flow and head) for the pump set both for the PAC dosing system and the required services for the WTP?

The new duty point selection for the new pump set will be the Tenderer’s responsibility. As a guide, the new pumps should be sized to supply at least 5000L/hr and at least 450kPa to service all the needs of the WTP.

7. Council to provide existing P&ID, Functional description and Control philosophy relevant to the SOW

The attached document ‘Pechey Key Drawings’ in the tender package should contain sufficient information for this SOW. The Functional Description and Control Philosophy along with I/O list can be provided directly to your approved integrator if you provide their details. Council will not provide this information to parties not bound under the approved system integration panel (set out in Part E, Section 3).

We have sought preliminary lead-time information, and been advised that the current estimated lead time for delivery of the new PAC system is approximately 36–40 weeks.

Based on this lead time, an order would need to have been placed approximately 2–4 weeks prior to the current date to achieve delivery by the end of June 2027. This would not be achievable where procurement commences following contract award assumed in mid-November 2026.

On this basis, an order placed following the anticipated mid-November 2026 award date would result in an estimated delivery timeframe of approximately mid-August 2027, prior to installation.

Can Council please confirm whether completion of the PAC system installation beyond June 2027 would be acceptable, given the current supplier lead time and anticipated contract award date?

Toowoomba Regional Council (TRC) is seeking quotations for the supply and installation of a new Powdered Activated Carbon (PAC) dosing system. title: Waste and Resource Recovery Digital Engagement Platform
description:
The procurement is for the provision, implementation, hosting, support and ongoing maintenance of a Waste and Resource Recovery Digital Engagement Platform, including a mobile application, publicly accessible web-based collection calendar, website integration tools and a secure administration portal.

The solution must provide Council with the ability to independently manage and update content through a secure, web-based administration portal without requiring supplier intervention for routine operational changes.

The successful supplier will provide:

•	iOS and Android mobile applications.

•	Cloud hosting, software licensing, cybersecurity, upgrades and technical support.

•	Property-specific waste collection calendars.

•	Public web-based collection calendar suitable for integration into Council's website.

•	Bin collection reminder notifications.

•	Property based, geographic and service-area-specific notifications.

•	Waste and recycling education resources, including an A-Z disposal guide.

•	Event promotion and notification capabilities.

•	Reporting, analytics and user engagement metrics.

•	Integration with Council systems and databases.

Administration Portal Requirements

The solution must include a secure, role-based administration portal that enables authorised Council staff to:

•	Create, edit and publish content.

•	Update collection schedules and calendars.

•	Manage waste and recycling information.

•	Publish and schedule notifications.

•	Create and manage educational campaigns.

•	Update event information and community recycling initiatives.

•	Upload and manage documents, images and multimedia content.

•	Generate reports and analytics.

•	Manage user permissions and access levels.

The administration portal should be intuitive and user-friendly, requiring minimal technical expertise and enabling Council staff to make updates in real time.

Future Capability

The platform must be scalable and capable of supporting future enhancements including:

•	Community Recycling Centre services.

•	Circular economy and reuse initiatives.

•	Multi-language support.

•	Additional environmental and sustainability programs.

The proposed solution must provide a single source of truth across mobile applications, web platforms and future digital channels, ensuring information can be maintained efficiently by Council staff through the administration portal.

title: Request for Information - Cyber Security Dashboard
description:
The Queensland Government is seeking information from the market to better understand available products, services and delivery approaches that could support an executive-level cyber security dashboard and/or reporting capability.

The intended capability would provide executive government with a consolidated view of the cyber security position across Queensland Government budget sector agencies, with potential future expansion to include Government Owned Corporations (GOCs) and statutory authorities. The current budget sector comprises approximately 21 agencies/entities, with a broader future scope potentially including statutory authorities, in addition to relevant GOCs.

Queensland Government agencies operate in a complex and diverse digital environment, with varying business functions, risk profiles, technology landscapes and levels of cyber security maturity. Cyber security information is often generated through a range of sources, including assessments, assurance activities, operational reporting, incident information, risk reporting and control performance measures. This information may be held in different formats, at different levels of maturity, and with varying degrees of consistency across entities.

Executive government requires clear, timely and meaningful insight into the overall cyber security posture of the Queensland Government to support strategic oversight, risk-informed decision-making, prioritisation of investment, and whole-of-government assurance. This includes the ability to understand broad trends, emerging issues, areas of elevated risk, and comparative performance across a diverse operating environment.

This Request for Information is intended to inform the Queensland Government’s understanding of the market and the range of possible approaches available. It is not intended to prescribe a particular technical solution, architecture, product type or delivery model.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerAddress:
140 Creek St
Brisbane City, Queensland 4000
Australia

vendorPanelDetails.queryCutoffAtRaw: Monday 26 October 2026 03:00 PM (E. Australia Standard Time)
vendorPanelDetails.background:
At present, there is no single, fit-for-purpose executive-level mechanism that consistently aggregates and presents cyber security information across in-scope Queensland Government entities in a way that is sufficiently clear, comparable and decision-useful for executive government.

Relevant cyber security information may exist across multiple systems, reporting processes and assessment mechanisms, which can make it difficult to obtain a consolidated whole-of-government view. Differences in data quality, reporting methods, terminology, technical maturity and system capability across entities may also limit the ability to produce consistent and trusted reporting for senior decision-makers.
vendorPanelDetails.desiredOutcomes:
The Queensland Government is seeking to understand what the market can offer to address this problem through a capability that could:

•	provide a consolidated view of cyber security posture across multiple entities

•	support reporting at whole-of-government, portfolio, agency and, where appropriate, entity level

•	present information in a form suitable for executive audiences, including dashboards, summary reporting and trend analysis

•	draw on a range of potential data inputs, including manual, semi-automated and automated sources

•	support consistent interpretation and aggregation of information across entities with differing size, complexity and maturity

•	minimise reporting burden on participating entities

•	support phased implementation, beginning with budget sector agencies and potentially expanding over time

•	operate in a manner that is interoperable, scalable and adaptable to existing and evolving government environments.

The Queensland Government is interested in practical, proportionate and achievable approaches, including those that may be delivered through configurable products, managed services, implementation support, advisory services, or hybrid models. Responses from a broad range of suppliers are encouraged, including small and medium enterprises.

Through this Request for Information, the Queensland Government seeks to better understand the maturity of the market, the types of solutions and services available, implementation considerations, and the options for establishing an executive cyber security reporting capability that is trusted, scalable and fit for purpose.

publicQuestions.question:
Thank you for the opportunity to respond to this Request for Information. To help us provide information that is genuinely useful to the department's planning, we would appreciate clarification on the following.

1. The RFI refers to data inputs including assessments, assurance activities, operational reporting, incident information, risk reporting and control performance measures. Could the department indicate which of these are considered in scope for an initial phase, and whether the capability is primarily intended to consolidate information submitted by entities, to draw directly from entity systems, or a combination of both?

2. Is the capability intended to support or replace any part of the existing IS18 information security annual return and IS18 Annual Report process, or is it intended to operate alongside those existing reporting mechanisms?

3. Does the department currently operate a governance, risk and compliance, or enterprise risk platform that this capability would be expected to integrate with or extend, rather than replace?

4. Is reporting expected to remain periodic, consistent with current annual and incident-based reporting cycles, or is there an intent to move toward more frequent or near-continuous reporting over time?

5. Is the capability expected to be centrally funded and centrally enabled, or is there an expectation that participating entities would fund and operate their own components under a federated model? This materially affects the rough order of magnitude we can provide under section 2.9.

6. What information security classification is the aggregated data expected to carry, and is assessment under the Infosec Registered Assessors Program at a particular classification level a requirement or a preference for solutions in scope?

7. Is there a preferred or mandated hosting arrangement, for example existing whole-of-government cloud arrangements or a specific Australian region, that responses should assume?

8. For the purposes of section 2.9, could the department confirm the scale assumptions we should use, in particular the approximate number of entities in an initial phase and the expected number of executive and agency-level users of the capability?

9. Section 2.5 requests two referees. Given this is an early market information exercise with no evaluation or shortlisting, would the department accept referees from comparable multi-entity or whole-of-government engagements outside Queensland, including international public sector references?

10. Would the department consider supplier briefings or demonstrations as part of the further engagement referenced in section 1.2, and if so, is there an indicative timeframe?

11. Is there an indicative timeframe or budget envelope for any subsequent procurement, to help suppliers frame proportionate and achievable options?

12. Section 2.12 asks how the solution would further purposeful public procurement objectives. For responses that involve a combination of a product and local implementation or managed service partners, should these objectives be addressed on a combined basis across the proposed delivery model?
publicQuestions.answer:
Q: The RFI refers to data inputs including assessments, assurance activities, operational reporting, incident information, risk reporting and control performance measures. Could the department indicate which of these are considered in scope for an initial phase, and whether the capability is primarily intended to consolidate information submitted by entities, to draw directly from entity systems, or a combination of both?

A: All are in scope, whether sourced directly from entities through either manual submission or system pull or indirectly from aggregated sources.

Q: Is the capability intended to support or replace any part of the existing IS18 information security annual return and IS18 Annual Report process, or is it intended to operate alongside those existing reporting mechanisms?

A: The capability is currently not intended to support or replace any part of the IS18 annual return process, but it is intended to operate alongside it.

Q: Does the department currently operate a governance, risk and compliance, or enterprise risk platform that this capability would be expected to integrate with or extend, rather than replace?

A: The scope of the sought capability is whole-of-government. There is no standardisation of GRC platforms across the sector. Potential integrations may involve an array of platforms.

Q: Is reporting expected to remain periodic, consistent with current annual and incident-based reporting cycles, or is there an intent to move toward more frequent or near-continuous reporting over time?

A: There is an intent for more frequent and near-continuous reporting.

Q: Is the capability expected to be centrally funded and centrally enabled, or is there an expectation that participating entities would fund and operate their own components under a federated model? This materially affects the rough order of magnitude we can provide under section 2.9.

A: Both funding options will be considered.

Q: What information security classification is the aggregated data expected to carry, and is assessment under the Infosec Registered Assessors Program at a particular classification level a requirement or a preference for solutions in scope?

A: Up to PROTECTED.

IRAP assessments will be considered

Q: Is there a preferred or mandated hosting arrangement, for example existing whole-of-government cloud arrangements or a specific Australian region, that responses should assume?

A: Specific hosting arrangements to consider the data classification and Australian data storage.

Q: For the purposes of section 2.9, could the department confirm the scale assumptions we should use, in particular the approximate number of entities in an initial phase and the expected number of executive and agency-level users of the capability?

A: Consider 21 departments, and an average of 5 executives/users per department.

Q: Section 2.5 requests two referees. Given this is an early market information exercise with no evaluation or shortlisting, would the department accept referees from comparable multi-entity or whole-of-government engagements outside Queensland, including international public sector references?

A: Yes

Q: Would the department consider supplier briefings or demonstrations as part of the further engagement referenced in section 1.2, and if so, is there an indicative timeframe?

A: The department may consider supplier briefings/demonstrations. No timeframes have been developed.

Q: Is there an indicative timeframe or budget envelope for any subsequent procurement, to help suppliers frame proportionate and achievable options?

A: No

Q: Section 2.12 asks how the solution would further purposeful public procurement objectives. For responses that involve a combination of a product and local implementation or managed service partners, should these objectives be addressed on a combined basis across the proposed delivery model?

A: At the discretion of the respondent

description:
Byron Shire Council is seeking Expressions of Interest to Manage Ocean Shores Tennis Facility.

Byron Shire Council is seeking a suitably qualified and experienced entity to manage the facility known as the Ocean Shores Tennis Courts, located in Waterlily Park, Ocean Shores and activate the site as outlined within this document and in accordance with its various objectives, policies, and plans. The preference is for a not-for-profit community organisation to manage the Tennis Facility; however, Byron Shire Council invites and will consider submissions from all entities. The license period is to be negotiated, to a maximum of five years.

publicQuestions.question:
PROPOSED DEPARTURES TO THE CONTRACT

RFT26-020 Undalup Solar Expansion – RFT Section 2.9

With reference to RFT section 2.9, we hereby request the City's response in writing to our proposed departures to the Contract (Attachment C) set out below. We acknowledge that, under section 2.9, these departures are not binding on the City unless agreed by the City in writing.

Departure 1 – Schedule 2, Item 7 (Clause 12(a))

RFT / Contract position: Liquidated Damages Cap: Unlimited. LDs of $500/day accrue until Completion with no ceiling.

Proposed departure: Liquidated Damages Cap: 10% of the Contract Price.

Departure 2 – Schedule 2, Item 4 (Clause 24.2(a))

RFT / Contract position: Contractor Maximum Liability Amount: Unlimited.

Proposed departure: Contractor Maximum Liability Amount: 100% of the Contract Price, subject to the existing carve-outs in clause 24.2(c) (other than 24.2(c)(10) – see Departure 3).

Departure 3 – Clause 24.2(c)(10)

RFT / Contract position: Liquidated damages sit outside the liability cap and do not count towards it.

Proposed departure: Delete clause 24.2(c)(10), so LDs count towards the Contractor Maximum Liability Amount.

Departure 4 – Clause 12(f)

RFT / Contract position: If LDs are unenforceable for any reason, the City may claim general damages for delay.

Proposed departure: Delete clause 12(f). LDs under clause 12 are the City's sole remedy for delay in achieving Completion, other than termination rights under clause 27.
publicQuestions.answer:
The City acknowledges the proposed departures to the Contract identified in your correspondence dated 1 October 2026.

The City does not agree to the proposed amendments through this clarification process. The Contract terms and conditions remain unchanged.

Tenderers must submit any proposed contractual departures in accordance with section 2.9 of the RFT.

Any proposed departures will be considered in accordance with the RFT and the City's tender evaluation process. The submission or consideration of a proposed departure does not constitute acceptance by the City.

title: Palm Island Tourism Commercial & Operating Partner
description:
Palm Island Aboriginal Shire Council (Council) is seeking to appoint a suitably qualified and experienced Palm Island Tourism Commercial & Operating Partner (Partner) to support the development, commercial activation, operational readiness and initial operation of Palm Island’s emerging tourism offering.

The engagement will provide Council with specialist tourism, commercial and operating capability across the full establishment lifecycle, commencing during procurement and delivery of the associated tourism infrastructure and continuing through tourism product development, operational mobilisation, Commercial Opening and the initial operating period.

The Partner will work collaboratively with Council and relevant local, cultural, government and tourism-sector stakeholders to establish a coordinated, commercially sustainable and culturally appropriate tourism offering that supports increased visitation and economic participation on Palm Island.

The engagement will broadly progress through the following lifecycle:

1.	D&C Procurement Support – providing specialist tourism, commercial and operational input to Council during procurement of the Design and Construct (D&C) contractor for the Walking Trails and associated tourism infrastructure.

2.	Design and Tourism Product Development – providing operational and commercial input during design development while progressively developing the tourism products, visitor experience and operating arrangements that will utilise the infrastructure.

3.	Operational Readiness and Commercial Mobilisation – establishing the systems, processes, market channels, workforce and service-provider arrangements necessary for Commercial Opening.

4.	Commercial Operations – leading the commercial coordination and day-to-day operation of the Council tourism offering following Commercial Opening, in accordance with the requirements of this Specification.

The Contract will comprise a Pre-Opening Period, followed by an Initial Operating Term of twenty-four (24) months from Commercial Opening, with a Council-controlled option to extend the operating term for up to a further three (3) years.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
Tourism Master Plan – 2023

Council has undertaken a staged program of tourism planning and development aimed at establishing a sustainable visitor economy on Palm Island.

The Palm Island Tourism Master Plan provides the strategic foundation for this work. It identified governance and partnerships, local capability, sharing Palm Island's story and caring for Country as key enablers of tourism development. It also contemplated a staged pathway incorporating local workforce and business development, Ranger participation, tourism product development, visitor transport, walking trails, accommodation and appropriate tourism partnerships.

Council is now progressing from strategic planning and community engagement into infrastructure delivery, commercial activation and operational establishment.

Preliminary Track Network Investigation – 2025-2026

Following the Tourism Master Plan, Council commissioned further investigation of potential walking trail alignments during late 2025 and early 2026.

The resulting Palm Island Track Network Report investigated and ground-truthed potential trail alignments across Palm Island and developed a preliminary network comprising approximately 26 kilometres of proposed new or substantially upgraded walking tracks, which, together with approximately 10 kilometres of existing roads and paths, could form a connected walking network of around 35 kilometres. The report also explored concepts for future expansion into more remote parts of the Island, including potential multi-day walking experiences.

The Track Network Report was a preliminary technical and concept-development exercise rather than a final determination of the walking trail network. Its findings subsequently informed the community and stakeholder engagement process and further project definition.

Community and Stakeholder Engagement – 2026

Council undertook a structured community and stakeholder engagement process during 2026 to test and further develop the proposed approach to the Walking Trails Project and the broader Palm Island tourism offering.

The engagement activities were undertaken principally during April and May 2026, with the outcomes documented in the Engagement Outcomes Report – Consultation Summary in June 2026.

The engagement considered both the proposed walking trails and their relationship with Palm Island's broader visitor economy. It reinforced the importance of cultural authority, local employment and capability development, guided and managed tourism, protection of family camps, privacy and sensitive areas, staged development, transparency and continuing community involvement.

The engagement also considered the need for specialist commercial tourism capability to provide market access, distribution, operating systems, safety capability and commercial expertise while supporting local participation and community leadership.

The resulting recommendations were received and supported for further planning and development by Elected Council under Resolution 2026-R138 and have subsequently informed the scope, priorities and implementation approach for the Walking Trails & Tourism Activation Project.

Walking Trails & Tourism Activation Investment

The Palm Island Walking Trails & Tourism Activation Project represents a major implementation initiative arising from the Tourism Master Plan and subsequent project development.

The Queensland Government, through the Department of the Environment, Tourism, Science and Innovation (DETSI), has committed approximately $4.9 million towards implementation of the Tourism Master Plan, initially focused on development of the walking trails and associated tourism infrastructure.

The project is intended to establish foundational visitor infrastructure while supporting First Nations-led tourism, nature-based tourism and increased economic participation on Palm Island. The project has been developed with an emphasis on culturally appropriate and environmentally sensitive delivery and increased employment, training and business participation for Palm Island residents, Rangers and local businesses.

D&C Procurement and Delivery

Council is separately procuring a Design and Construct (D&C) Contractor for delivery of the Walking Trails and associated tourism infrastructure.

The Tourism Commercial & Operating Partner procurement is being undertaken in parallel with the D&C procurement so that specialist tourism, visitor-experience, commercial and operational considerations can inform relevant procurement and design decisions before the infrastructure is completed.

Indigenous and Arts Installation Precinct / Cultural Walk Interface

The Walking Trails & Tourism Activation Project forms part of a wider emerging visitor offering on Palm Island and is not intended to operate as an isolated tourism asset.

In particular, the tourism offering will interface with the separately delivered Indigenous and Arts Installation Precinct / Cultural Walk, together with other existing and future visitor assets and experiences. The broader approach is to progressively create a connected visitor journey encompassing arrival and orientation, cultural interpretation, walking trails, accommodation, cultural and nature-based experiences, local businesses and visitor departure.

Detailed interface and coordination requirements applicable to the Partner are set out elsewhere in this Specification.

DETSI Strategic Role

DETSI is the principal State funding and strategic tourism partner for the current establishment phase.

In addition to administering the relevant project funding arrangements, DETSI has a strategic interest in tourism-policy alignment, First Nations tourism, regional economic participation, operational readiness and demonstration of the tourism, employment and enterprise outcomes generated from the State's infrastructure investment.

Council retains responsibility for its statutory, procurement, contractual, financial and asset-management decisions, subject to the requirements of applicable funding agreements.

Palm Island Community Economic Development Foundation

The Palm Island Community Economic Development Foundation (Foundation) is an important local economic-development partner within the emerging tourism model.

The Foundation's role is focused on developing the local employment, workforce, enterprise and business capability required to enable Palm Island residents and businesses to participate in and benefit from tourism growth. This includes potential workforce pathways, training, supplier and enterprise development, local procurement and development of locally delivered tourism products and services.

The detailed interface between the Partner and the Foundation is addressed in the local economic participation requirements of this Specification.

Minggamingga Rangers

The Minggamingga Rangers are recognised as a central participant in the development of tourism on Palm Island, providing important cultural, environmental, Country-management and operational capability.

The tourism model provides for Ranger involvement to progressively extend across relevant aspects of tourism product development, visitor experiences, guiding and hosting, environmental and cultural activities, visitor management and stewardship of Country.

Specific requirements for engagement and coordination with the Minggamingga Rangers are set out elsewhere in this Specification.

Tourism Governance, Commercial and Operating Model

Council has developed a preliminary Palm Island Tourism Governance, Commercial and Operating Model to establish an overarching framework for the development, activation and ongoing operation of tourism on Palm Island.

The Model addresses the respective roles of Council, the Tourism Commercial & Operating Partner, the Foundation, Rangers, cultural authorities and key government, destination, transport and market partners, together with the proposed governance, commercial, local-participation and longer-term operating framework.

The Model is included with this Invitation to Tender as a Reference Document to provide Tenderers with the broader strategic and institutional context within which this engagement will operate.

The Model does not replace or override this Specification or the Contract. All obligations of the Partner are those expressly established through the Invitation to Tender and Contract Documents. Where an element of the Model is required to be performed by the Partner, the applicable requirement is set out in this Specification or elsewhere in the Contract Documents.

publicQuestions.question:
Re: RFT260094 – Pricing Schedule Clarifications

We are reviewing the tender as a prospective main contractor. Could Council please clarify the following items in the ScopeReport worksheet?

Optional kennel works — rows 85–89: The subtotal in row 90 sums rows 68–84 only, excluding ventilation, water tanks, insulation, roof venting and the western shade screen. Rows 88–89 also have no pricing formulas. Please confirm how these items should be priced and included in the tender total.

Temporary fencing — row 18: This row describes temporary fencing but operates as the preliminaries subtotal, summing rows 16–17. Please confirm where the temporary fencing allowance should be entered.

Alternative roof options — rows 46–47: Both roof options feed into the exercise-pen subtotal. Should tenderers include the standard roof in the base price and show the heat-reflective option separately as an alternative or additional cost?

Alternative concrete works — rows 30–38: The subtotal includes both Option 1 and Option 2. Please confirm the required base option and how the alternative should be presented without counting both options in the total.

Exercise-pen gates — rows 49 and 63: Row 49 includes nine exercise-pen gates, while row 63 includes thirteen gates comprising those same nine plus four others. Please confirm whether row 63 should exclude the nine gates priced in row 49.

Shipping containers — rows 95–97: Each row has a quantity of two, whereas the descriptions and specification refer to relocating one existing cattery container and supplying/installing one new storage container. Please confirm the correct quantity and pricing basis for each row.

Concrete area — row 36: The quantity is 157 m² and the comments state 157.58 m². However, the dimensions and deductions listed appear to calculate to approximately 151.77 m². Please confirm the intended area and measurement boundaries.

Items without clear standalone pricing lines: Please confirm where tenderers should allow for the nine garden taps, 3.5 m sliding gate, provisional stainless-steel kennel screens and reinforced bund around kennel 11, and whether each belongs in the base price or a separate provisional allowance.

Could Council please issue a revised pricing schedule, or confirm the permitted amendments, so tender submissions are prepared on a consistent basis?

Thank you.
publicQuestions.answer:

Regards,

publicQuestions.question:
Re: RFT260094 – Further clarification of updated BOQ

Thank you for issuing the updated pricing schedule.

We have reviewed the revised ScopeReport worksheet and identified remaining calculation issues that appear to materially affect the tender total. All row references below relate to the updated workbook.

1. Subtotals overlap and repeatedly include earlier totals. For example, J42 includes the modular-building subtotal J32; J44 includes J42 alongside the individual concrete costs; and subtotals within rows 54–64 overlap further. Please review the subtotal structure throughout columns J–L.

2. Temporary fencing at row 18 is excluded from subtotal row 19. The sliding gate at row 78 is excluded from subtotal row 79. The kennel bund, sheeting, stainless panels and optional improvements in rows 98–107 are excluded from subtotal row 108 and the grand total.

3. Nine exercise-pen gates appear at both rows 53 and 58. Please confirm which line should be priced.

4. Row 78 uses addition rather than quantity × rate, and its GST formula is incorrect. GST and inclusive totals in rows 48–49 also reference preceding rows.

5. Please confirm the quantity/unit for painting at row 49, currently 95.5 EACH, and the intended input arrangement for demolition at row 74, where the rate is 1 and quantity is blank.

6. Row 73 reduces Colorbond fencing to 18.49 m, but the comment still describes 54.61 m across the western and northern boundaries. Is the western boundary now excluded?

7. Row 40 now states 157.58 m², but its listed dimensions and deductions calculate to approximately 151.77 m². Please confirm the intended measurement.

8. Please confirm how the concrete and roof alternatives should be presented separately from the base offer, where the nine garden taps should be priced, and whether securing the cattery in row 113 overlaps the work in row 115.

Could Council please issue a further corrected workbook with checked formulas and confirm the above scope points, so all tenderers price on a consistent basis?

Thank you.

title: Testing Orchestration, Automation, Support and Transition
description:
WorkCover Queensland is seeking a Test Orchestration Platform and associated implementation, integration, transition and support services to establish an enterprise-wide testing capability. The solution will support testing governance, orchestration, automation, test data management, reporting, and assurance across WCQ's increasingly integrated SaaS and cloud-based technology landscape.

The procurement includes three capability areas:

Test Orchestration Platform

- Enterprise test orchestration and management platform.

- Software licensing for the proposed platform.

- Test orchestration, workflow management, reporting, governance, traceability and release assurance capabilities.

- Integration with testing tools, CI/CD pipelines, SaaS platforms, cloud services, enterprise applications and iPaaS.

Testing and Test Data Capabilities

- Test automation capabilities supporting UI, API, integration and contract testing.

- Enterprise Test Data Management capabilities including data masking, anonymisation, synthetic data generation and governed test data provisioning.

- Reporting, analytics, monitoring and evidence management capabilities.

Implementation, Support and Maintenance Services

- Solution architecture, validation and detailed design services

- Platform configuration, deployment and implementation services.

- Systems integration and onboarding services.

- Test data management implementation services.

- Knowledge transfer, training and operational readiness activities.

- Transition, go-live and hypercare support services.

- Ongoing Level 3 support and maintenance services.

Anticipated Contract award is March 2027
