title: EOI: NS2703 Underground Civil Construction (UCC)
description:
This EOI seeks to identify suppliers with the capability, capacity, resources and operational presence required to deliver underground civil construction services supporting Energy Queensland’s electricity networks across Queensland.

Services may include trenching, conduit installation, cable hauling and placement, construction of pits, joint holes and bays, and specialist activities such as Horizontal Directional Drilling where integrated into a broader Underground Civil Construction work package.

This open EOI covers the following proposed delivery tiers:

•	Tier 1: Suppliers with an established or substantively committed operational presence in South East Queensland and the capability to deliver higher-value, higher-risk and more complex Transmission and Distribution civil construction works statewide. Tier 1 suppliers will be appointed as Principal Contractor for all work undertaken through this tier. Where electrical supervision is required, it must be provided through electrical workers directly employed by the appointed contractor.

•	Tier 2: Suppliers with an established or substantively committed operational presence in major regional centres capable of delivering moderate to higher-value Distribution civil construction works across areas in which the supplier demonstrates an operational presence and delivery capability. Tier 2 suppliers will be appointed as Principal Contractor for all work undertaken through this tier. Where electrical supervision is required, it may be provided through directly employed, labour hire, subcontracted or related-entity personnel, provided the appointed contractor retains responsibility and effective control over the safe planning, supervision, management and delivery of the work.

Subject to the outcomes of the EOI and subsequent tender process, Energy Queensland may also appoint up to one Tier 2 supplier to support Distribution works in South East Queensland.

This EOI is the first stage of a multi-stage procurement process comprising EOI evaluation and shortlisting, a selective tender process, and capability assessment before any appointment to the future UCC framework.

Energy Queensland will determine the number and mix of suppliers required to support its operational delivery program. Appointment decisions will consider anticipated work demand, demonstrated capability and capacity, geographic coverage, competition and value for money, and Energy Queensland’s capacity to onboard, assure and manage contractors.

Energy Queensland may appoint fewer suppliers than the number assessed as capable of meeting the relevant tier requirements. Satisfying the evaluation criteria does not create an entitlement to shortlisting or appointment.

Appointment to the framework will not guarantee:

•	any minimum volume or value of work;

•	an invitation to quote for every work package relevant to the contractor’s appointed tier; or

Energy Queensland will determine which contractors are invited to quote for each work package. Tier and operational location will inform that decision but won’t create an automatic entitlement to participate or receive work. Energy Queensland will also consider the contractor’s capability, capacity, availability and mobilisation arrangements, the risk and requirements of the work package, competitive pricing and overall value for money.

Out of Scope:

Tier 3 does not form part of this open EOI. Tier 3 is intended to provide a separate participation pathway for regional Queensland small and medium enterprises currently delivering relevant activities through Energy Queensland’s 1628 Minor Works arrangement

Tier classification and EQL discretion:

Proponents may nominate Tier 1, Tier 2 or both tiers when responding to the open EOI.

Energy Queensland will determine whether a Proponent is suitable to progress for the nominated tier, or another tier where appropriate, based on the EOI and subsequent tender assessments. This may include consideration of demonstrated capability, experience, workforce and supervision model, operational presence, geographic coverage, capacity and applicable safety requirements. Nomination of a tier does not guarantee shortlisting, progression or appointment to that tier.

Refer to Section 2 Scope to review the full Scope of Works.

Located 10 minutes from the Perth CBD and home to state and national-level sporting grounds, Curtin University, green spaces galore and thriving communities, all centred around Albany Highway – one of the longest main strips in the Southern Hemisphere, packed with all manner of restaurants, cafes and retail stores – the Town of Victoria Park is a cultural hub nestled on the southern banks of Derbarl Yerrigan (the Swan River).

Suburbs within the Town include Victoria Park, East Victoria Park, Lathlain, Carlisle and Burswood, as well as sections of Welshpool, Bentley and St. James, with the current population of 38,000 expected to grow to 77,000 by 2050.

While the Town as we know it today has existed since the early 90s, recorded history of the area dates back to pre-European settlement, where there was evidence of Aboriginal presence on the Perth Coastal Plain and the site near the present-day Causeway was known as ‘Matta Gerup’ (knee deep). The Town’s Mindeera Advisory Group is named for Mindeera Springs, which served as a neutral meeting point for different tribes near this area. In 1829 the first non-Indigenous people settled in the area and the first land grants were issued. Originally established in 1894, it was absorbed into the City of Perth in 1917, before being proclaimed an independent municipality and closely resuming its original boundaries in 1994.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi there,

To confirm:

-Are the library guarding services permanent and scheduled Mon-Fri and Sat as outlined? Or are they ad-hoc and on an as-required basis only?

-All other guarding services and sites are ad-hoc only?

-In terms of pricing, it is fixed for the first 12 months from Jan 2027 as the contract commencement date? But will increase as per the Award and Fair Work guidelines each year from July 2028? Or, is the initial 3 year period expected to be a flat rate?

Thank you
publicQuestions.answer:
Response To Questions:

1. Are the Library guarding services permanent and scheduled Mon-Fri and Sat as outlined, or are they ad hoc and on an as-required basis only?

The Victoria Park Library security service is the primary ongoing requirement under the Contract. The Town intends to engage one (1) licensed Security Officer during the Library operating hours specified in the Request, unless otherwise directed by the Town.

2. Are all other guarding services and sites ad hoc only?

Yes. Security services required at Aqualife, Leisurelife, the Town Administration Centre, Council meetings, public meetings, community engagement activities, community events and other Town facilities are ad hoc and will be requested by the Town on an as-required basis.

The Town does not guarantee any minimum quantity or value of ad hoc services.

3. In terms of pricing, is it fixed for the first 12 months from January 2027 as the contract commencement date?

Yes. Tenderers should submit pricing on the basis that the offered rates will remain fixed for the first twelve (12) months of the Contract.

The Contract provides for rate adjustments after 12 months in accordance with the price adjustment mechanism stated in the Request document.

-End of Response-

Economic Development Queensland (EDQ) is the Queensland Government’s land use planning and property development agency. We embrace partnerships across government, industry and the community to deliver new residential communities, urban precincts and industrial ecosystems.

Backed by the Economic Development Act 2012, EDQ has unique planning and approval powers and a mandate to create private sector investment opportunities by de-risking and unlocking land for redevelopment. EDQ has planned and facilitated the delivery of some of the largest residential developments in Queensland, as well as some of the state’s most iconic urban renewal projects. We set benchmarks for the property industry through innovations and we’re creating jobs of the future in regional Queensland by unlocking land to promote priority industries, including clean energy and large-scale manufacturing.

We measure our success by the value we create in economic, social and environmental impacts. Over the last decade we have generated more than $3.7 billion in private sector investment and facilitated over $1 billion in trunk infrastructure for Queensland. EDQ focuses on achieving commercial outcomes for the state while delivering on government priorities.

title: Tender 1226248 - Design & Construction of Molong Water Security Pipeline Project
description:
Cabonne Council has been investigating options to:

- Improve water security and drought resilience;

- Ensure the availability of supply from the Molong Creek Dam to meet current and future town water demand; and

- Provide Molong, Cumnock and Yeoval with secure water supply to support the development of these centres.

The gravity main from Molong Creek Dam to the Molong Water Treatment Plant is a key component of the Molong Water Supply System. Sections of this pipeline were constructed in 1920 with various sections then added or replaced over time. This gravity pipeline is critical for the continued operation and security of the Molong WSS. Upgrades to this pipeline are proposed to improve the transfer capacity and operation including:

- Replacing a 9,300m section of the Molong Creek Dam to Molong Water Filtration Plant gravity raw water pipeline from a point known as Peter's Pit to a point known as Gabb's Pit. This section of the existing pipeline includes single and parallel pipes of various sizes and lengths; and

- Interconnections of the new pipeline to the existing pipeline/pipelines at Peter's Pit and Gabb's Pit; and

- Reconnection of existing customer services to the new pipeline; and

- Decommissioning of the existing pipeline/pipelines.

1.	Please confirm whether operating scenarios in which the OCC supply is feeding the gravity main are to be included in the water hammer analysis.

3.	Are any other flow and pressure data available for calibration, or are we to rely on Table 2-2 in the concept design report?

4.	Concept Design Report section 2.3.3.2 notes that friction losses between Gabb's Pit and the WTP were increased by 16 percent to match observed pressures, and attributes this to a possible partially closed valve or other constriction. Has the cause been located and confirmed? Is the contractor responsible for determining why this unexplained headloss is occurring.

5.	Please confirm that the full gravity main replacement in Concept Design Report section 2.3.4 is included or excluded from the water hammer analysis scope.

1. Water hammer analysis for the OCC supply is not required.

4. No, the cause has not been determined.

 No

6. This can be revised based on the Contractor’s analysis and agreed by the Principal.

 The hydraulic analysis should confirm the PRV selection and settings.

Nadun Wishvanath

publicQuestions.answer:
Good afternoon,

1. See attached Returnable Tender Schedules in Word format.

2. Trench stops to be in accordance with WSAA - Water Supply Code of Australia.

3. Trench stops to be in accordance with WSAA - Water Supply Code of Australia.

4. Water Management Act Cabonne Council, as a public authority, is exempt from the requirement to hold a controlled activity approval under section 91E(1) of the Water Management Act 2000 under section 64(2) of the Water Management (General) Regulation 2025. No controlled activity approval is required for the proposed pipeline works carried out by Council within waterfront land. Fisheries Management Act The creek crossings are subject to survey and detailed design as part of the design and construct contract. The extent to which the Fisheries Management Act 1994 is relevant depends on the detailed design (i.e. under bore vs trench). Under bore is likely to avoid any permit requirement. If the crossings are trenched, it is likely that permits will be required under section 200 of the Fisheries Management Act 1994. If the crossings create a short term (construction period) or long-term obstruction to a fish passage, it is likely a permit will be required under section 219 of the Fisheries Management Act 1994. REF The current REF has been prepared on the basis that the activity is subject to a design and construct contract which will require the appointed contractor to develop the design and prepare construction documentation. It may be necessary to amend the REF prior to commencement of construction of the activity to account for any potential change to its effect or likely affect. publicQuestions.question:
“In relation to allowing for excavation in rock, it is virtually impossible to calculate with any accuracy the quantity of rock that will be encountered. As such, it is likely that tenderers will allow vastly different quantities. This will make it difficult for Council to assess “apples for apples”.

Council’s own Geotech Report talks about the variability of the geological conditions introduces considerable geotechnical variability, most notably considerable potential for abrupt changes in subsurface/excavatability conditions, therefore making any accurate assessment of excavation in rock near impossible. On another page it describes conditions are expected to be variable and could vary substantially from those anticipated based on the bore holes and desk top assessments. On another page, it also describes that linear interpolation between test locations is not appropriate for the subsurface conditions of the site. If the consultant after all their testing cannot come up with a quantity of rock to excavate, then it wouldn’t be possible for a tenderer to do so either.

As such, will Council provide a Provisional Sum or a Provisional Quantity of Rock to Tenderers to account for any excavation in Rock?

This will ensure accuracy and equitability in the tender process.

Thanks”
publicQuestions.answer:
Good morning,

Tenderers are to inform themselves of the Geotechnical investigations and reports provided in the Tender documents. In addition to the Geotech reports the following information includes previous information in relation to rock.

Pre tender meeting minutes - As a result of a question raised regarding separate rates for removal / excavation of rock, it was advised the contractors lump sum should include excavation of all materials, including rock regardless of hardness, type and depth.

Specifications Section 5.10 -The Contractor shall review the Geotechnical Investigation carried out by Macquarie Geotech (Reference G24236 Rev 01 dated 4 October 2024) and determine if the assessment of the final pipeline route is sufficient to confirm the potential presence of rock or other subsoil features impacting the construction of the pipeline. The Contractor is to assess whether additional testing is required.

Following the review of the Macquarie Geotech Report, if additional testing is deemed to be required, the Contractor shall carry out all necessary additional Geotechnical Investigations along the pipeline route at their own expense and provide copies to the Council for their review and acceptance prior to the start of any designs and or construction works.

Tender Schedule 2 Lump Sum Contract - Pipeline construction from Peter’s Pit to Gabb’s Pit in all materials including rock regardless of rock type, hardness or depth.

General conditions of Contract - Section 36 and 37 refers to Site Conditions.

Regards,

Nadun Wishvanath

Coordinator - Water Utilities

Cabonne Council

publicQuestions.question:
Hi

The Schedule of Prices refers to item "Service connections". Can you please confirm the location, details and number of these service connections?

Further the Schedule of Prices also refers to "Operations and Maintenance manual". Can you please confirm for which items is the O&M manual required?
publicQuestions.answer:
Good morning,

1. Service connections refers to existing customer connections. As per the drawings these are located at CH1950, CH3150 and CH8950. As per previous RFI these service connections are 20mm and the meters will be supplied free by the Council.

2. O&M manual requirements - as per the specifications, the Contract requires operating manuals as necessary. This being a gravity pipeline would include the following:-

a) Normal operating procedures - instructions for fillings, routine flow monitoring, pressure verification and planned shutdowns.

 b) Technical information of all pipeline components and location of all valves including stop, scour, air and service connections.

c) Abnormal and emergency operations - Steps for handling unexpected pressure drops, leaks, including rapid closure valve sequences

 d) Pressure reduction valve - normal operating pressure settings and maintenance procedures and reset procedures and troubleshooting for abnormal pressures downstream.

e) Maintenance - schedules for ground inspections, easement encroachments, soil erosion checks, marker post inspections, valve surround inspections, air valve maintenance and leak detection.

Regards,

Nadun Wishvanath

Coordinator - Water Utilities

Cabonne Council

title: TEN/3083 - Disposal of Old Show Grounds Site, 45 Burrum Street, Bundaberg West
description:
Council is inviting offers from suitably qualified Respondents to purchase and develop the balance of the property located at 45 Burrum Street, Bundaberg West, via tender.

Property

Council is the owner of the freehold parcel, described as Lot 4 on SP270831 known as 45 Burrum Street, Bundaberg West, Queensland, Australia, 4670 (‘Property’). The site is bounded by Civic Avenue, Burrum Street, Pyefinch Boulevard and Saltwater Creek, and has an area of 7.0895 hectares, in its current form.

The Property is the remains of the former Bundaberg Showgrounds, and currently has minimal physical infrastructure on the site, but does include the remaining Bailey Gate which is a Local Heritage Place in the Bundaberg Regional Council Planning Scheme 2015. The northern portion of the site is currently occupied by the Campervan and Motorhome Club of Australia (‘CMCA’) under a lease agreement to operate a caravan park for their members. This lease area roughly aligns with the area impacted by Council's adopted Flood Hazard Area and will be retained by Council. Services are available to the site, although depending on the nature of any future development, may require some extension, relocation or upgrade.

Adjoining the Property is the recently constructed Bundaberg Aquatic Centre, a major regional facility intended to host significant sporting and community events. The Property is also located adjacent to Council's Multiplex precinct and is consequently, a strategically important location to support regional events, community infrastructure and the accommodation needs generated by these adjoining facilities and activities.

Council’s objective is to facilitate the sale and timely development of the Property in a manner that delivers economic, social and community benefits, while supporting the strategic vision for the precinct and addressing identified accommodation and housing needs within the Bundaberg Region.

title: MCKINLAY SHIRE COUNCIL REQUEST FOR TENDER YARD MAINTENANCE SERVICES
description:
McKinlay Shire Council (‘Council’) invites tenders from suitably qualified tenderers for the provision of lawn mowing and associated yard maintenance services for Council properties on a fixed service schedules. This tender is for a fixed schedule of lawn mowing services at nominated Council properties and other specified locations. Tenderers are required to submit pricing and information for the services described in the Scope and Response Schedules.

During the Term, Council may also request additional lawn mowing, yard maintenance or related works by mutual agreement between Council and the successful Tenderer.

Council intends for the contract to commence on 1 November 2026 and end on 30 October 2027 (‘Term’).

The Principal may extend the Term, at its discretion, for a further 12 months by giving written notice to the successful Tenderer.

The required services and service frequencies are further described in Part 5 – Yard Maintenance Tender - Response Schedules.

Please note Tenderers must be able to provide the fixed lawn mowing services for the nominated properties and schedules, unless otherwise agreed by Council.

The successful Tenderer will be required to enter into a contract with Council for the provision of the fixed lawn mowing and associated yard maintenance services described in this Request for Tender, including the properties, frequencies and pricing schedules set out in the Response Schedules and Part 4 – Standard TCs – yard Maintenance Services

The contract will apply to the fixed service schedule and nominated properties, with payment to be made in accordance with the accepted pricing and agreed service requirements. Council may request additional lawn mowing, yard maintenance or related works during the Term where those works are agreed in writing between Council and the successful Tenderer.

Scope of Services

1.1	The scope shall include but is not limited to labour by a licensed and experienced person(s) related to the provision of labour, plant and equipment for total maintenance of lawns inclusive of mowing, whipper snipping, pruning, weeding and poisoning as per the directive given for each property.

Yard maintenance will be required at Council Residences, Commonwealth Home Support Program (CHSP) Client Residences, McIntyre Park and Father Bill Busuttin Community Centre as directed by Council Staff in the Julia Creek Township.

Please note: No poisoning permitted unless agreed to in writing by Council.

1.2	Suppliers and their Personnel are to undergo a national criminal history record check and must be renewed every three (3) years as required under the CHSP Commonwealth Home Support Program.

1.3	Suppliers and their Personnel are to adhere to Associated Provider requirements under the Aged Care Act 2024 and as outlined in Associated Provider Schedule (Response Schedule 5)

1.4	Lawns are to be mowed every fortnight in summer and every three (3) weeks in winter.

Please note: Days scheduled need to be consistent and are to be agreed to with the CHSP Co-Ordinator. Forms are to be completed and submitted upon completion of service

1.5	Unless otherwise directed by Council, copies of the following policies/licences for the Supplier and each member of the Supplier’s Personnel (where applicable) are to be provided to Council prior to engagement:

?	Workers Compensation Policy

?	Public Liability Insurance Policy

title: TEN16730 - Mount Morgan Cemetery Extension
description:
Mount Morgan Cemetery is a heritage listed cemetery located at East Street, Mount Morgan, within the Rockhampton Region, Queensland. Established in 1886, the cemetery has served the Mount Morgan community for the majority of the town’s history and was entered on the Queensland Heritage Register on 21 October 1992. The site contains numerous memorials, structures, and landscape elements of historical, cultural, social, and aesthetic significance, including the Linda Memorial and a rare Chinese ceremonial burner.

The land formerly identified as Lot 3614 has undergone a boundary realignment along East Street South and has been consolidated with Lot 184 to form a single allotment. More recently, the consolidated site has been rezoned to Community to support and facilitate the proposed extension of the Mount Morgan Cemetery. This technical specification has been prepared to support the delivery of civil works associated with the cemetery extension, which is intended to provide additional burial capacity and associated infrastructure while maintaining the historic character, heritage values, layout and cultural significance of the existing cemetery.

publicQuestions.question:
Morning,

Question from one of our Contractors.

Are we only doing the ceilings, wall and bulkhead in the following areas: Restaurant Dining Space, Bar, Office, Community Room and Proshop? Suspended ceiling needed?

Assume Square set for windows/door?

Only Proshop the new building need wall insulation? How about the roof insulation?
publicQuestions.answer:
Are we only doing the ceilings, wall and bulkhead in the following areas: Restaurant Dining Space, Bar, Office, Community Room and Proshop? Suspended ceiling needed?

Refer to A-01-1500 for extent of new PB-01 / ACP-01 ceilings. No new ceiling to the office.

Pro shop will have a suspended ceiling but could also be framed between timber ceiling purlins if simpler.

Lockers and Staff Lunchroom will have a plasterboard ceiling.

Rondo Keylock suspended ceiling system captured in Arch Schedules.

Assume Square set for windows/door?

Painted Finger jointed pine reveals internally, refer A-01-5001 and A-02-4002/03

Only Proshop the new building need wall insulation? How about the roof insulation?

Refer to wall types schedule on A-01-1401 and arch schedules for existing club wall insulation. Acoustic insulation required between community room and restaurant. Ceiling insulation (INS-02) required above new ceilings in club.

Roof insulation in Pro shop building limited to pro shop and staff lunchroom.

title: RFT 1571-2026 Electrification of WaterMarc and 1 Flintoff Offices
description:
The Council is seeking Tenders from suitably qualified and capable contractors for the Electrification of WaterMarc and 1 Flintoff Offices at 1 Flintoff Street, Greensborough VIC 3088.

The scope of works generally includes but is not limited to construction activities involving:

•	Mobilisation and site establishment.

•	Set out of works.

•	All works as per design drawings and specification.

•	Decommissioning of redundant equipment.

•	Ensuring the works are undertaken safely and in accordance with all Council and statutory safety requirements.

•	The site will remain open to the public and users for the duration of the constructions works. The contractor is to schedule the works to provide minimal disturbance and shutdowns by completing work outside of business hours and over the weekend where necessary.

•	Supply and installation of air source heat pumps.

•	Supply and installation of thermal storage tanks.

•	Upgrade of mechanical, hydraulic and electrical infrastructure.

•	Building remediation works for disturbed areas.

•	Liaison with AusNet to coordinate works.

•	Location and protection of any underground and above-ground services in the works area.

•	Site clean-up.

•	O&M Manuals, As Built and handover documentation.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi Team

Could council advise re the following:

1.	Please confirm existing BMS platform and incumbent contractor for each building

2.	Confirm coils are adequately sized for AHU 6,7,8,9, & 10 seeing HHW pipework is being upsized to each unit

3.	Please confirm the following temp chiller details

•	Application of the temporary chiller system

•	Required supply and return water temperatures

•	Required cooling load / duty

•	Required water flow rate

•	Available site power supply

•	Any additional requirements such as pumps, heat exchangers, hoses, cabling, or controls

•	Expected rental duration

4. Please confirm whether one additional site visit can be arranged.
publicQuestions.answer:
(edited on 07/Oct/2026 10:06 AM)

1. Please confirm existing BMS platform and incumbent contractor for each building

Controltech has developed our BMS platform.

Ans: Controltech manages Banyule and Oztech manages Watermarc BMS both as sub-contractors of Chilltech.

2. Confirm coils are adequately sized for AHU 6,7,8,9, & 10 seeing HHW pipework is being upsized to each unit.

Ans: The existing heating coils in AHU 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10 do not have sufficient capacity to provide their design heating outputs using the revised heating hot water temperatures from the heat pumps. However, it is proposed that these will not be replaced but will instead be retained along with additional modifications. The pipe upgrades along with additional valving are proposed to enable the heating capacity to be delivered by the existing AHU heating and cooling coils in combination. Please refer to the 1 Flintoff HHW Schematic note number 14 and the typical coil detail in the bottom right of the HHW schematic drawing that shows the addition of 3-way valves to allow HHW to flow through both the HHW and CHW coils when heating is required. Th BMS controls modifications to enable this operation are described in section 14.4.4 of the Mechanical Specification. The modified coil arrangements shall be commissioned to enable stable control of AHU heating via the HHW control valve and existing sensors.

3. Please confirm the following temp chiller details

Ans: Application of the temporary chiller system

The Watermarc aquatic centre component of the project is currently cooled by an existing water-cooled chiller located in the basement with heat rejected to 3C Coolers on the roof of Watermarc. The space occupied by the 3C coolers is required to install the new ASHP1 and ASHP-2 and so the 3C coolers will be decommissioned and removed early in the project. The water-cooled chiller in the basement will be without heat rejection and is also surplus to future requirements and proposed to be decommissioned and removed. This will leave the Watermarc gym, group fitness and meeting rooms without cooling for an extended period, which is unacceptable from an operational perspective. The temporary air-cooled chiller is intended to provide cooling to Watermarc during the period between when the 3C coolers are decommissioned and when the new ASHP-1 and associated chilled water reticulation is commissioned and operational.

Tenderers can propose alternative options for the provision of temporary cooling, such as relocating one of the existing air-cooled chillers from the 1 Flintoff St roof instead of a hire chiller or providing temporary condensers to replace the heat rejection provided by the 3C Coolers.

• Required supply and return water temperatures

The temporary chiller shall have 7/14C flow and return temperatures to match the existing chilled water system.

• Required cooling load / duty

The minimum cooling load/duty required for the temporary chiller is 300kW.

• Required water flow rate

Based on a minimum load of 300kW and 7C chilled water delta T, the minimum CHW flow required will be 10.25 l/s.

• Available site power supply

The existing 800kW water-cooled chiller is supplied from MSSB3 in the basement chiller/boiler plantroom. Once this chiller is decommissioned, it’s existing power supply will be available to be extended to connect to the temporary chiller. Refer to the note on Mechanical drawing 00301.

• Any additional requirements such as pumps, heat exchangers, hoses, cabling, or controls

Refer to the note on Mechanical drawing 00301. The intent is to provide temporary chilled water connections into the existing chilled water pumps and reticulation to provide cooling through the existing reticulation.

• Expected rental duration

The duration that the temporary cooling plant is required will depend on the tenderers proposed program of works. This will be the period between when the 3C coolers are decommissioned and when the new ASHP-1 and associated chilled water reticulation is commissioned and operational to provide cooling to Watermarc.

An additional site visit for Thursday 8 October at 10am has been arranged.

This will be the final opportunity to visit the site.

Responses to questions 1-3 will be provided when prepared.

title: 2627-09 IT Hardware for DWC Project
description:
The City of Greater Dandenong is seeking tenders for the supply and delivery of enterprise-grade IT networking equipment and supporting infrastructure for the Dandenong Wellbeing Centre (DWC).

The required equipment is detailed in the Bill of Materials (BOM).

The procurement is for supply and delivery only and excludes installation, commissioning and maintenance services. Delivery is indicatively required within six weeks of Contract award and must be completed no later than February 2027.

The City of Greater Dandenong is a great place to live, work and invest, with great people for neighbours, colleagues and friends.

Tenderers must identify expected lead times for each item and clearly identify equipment that cannot be delivered within the required timeframe. The pricing schedule also allows tenderers to identify suitable in-stock refurbished Aruba equipment where applicable.

title: IRC-IS-0826-T488 IRC Reconstruction of Essential Public Assets (Cylone Koji)
description:
Isaac Regional Council (IRC) requires a suitable Contractor to undertake the construction of reconstruction works to essential public assets damaged by extreme weather experienced during Tropical Cyclone Koji, and subsequent weather events funded under the Disaster Recovery Funding Arrangements (DRFA).

The impacted area spans the entirety of the IRC administrative boundary and includes a range of construction activities including pavement works, repair of drainage structures, signage installation, and clearing of debris.

Subject to the discretion of the Principal, the works may include in whole or in parts thereof, the following works:

a) Package 1: Central/North Works

b) Package 2: West Works

c) Package 3: North-East Works

d) Package 4: Central/South Works

e) Package 5: East Works

Subject to the discretion of the Principal, the five packages may be awarded to a single Contractor or to multiple Contractors. Where a Contractor seeks to be awarded multiple packages, they should clearly articulate their capability to do this in ‘Methodology & Program’ Response Schedule.

An optional site meeting will be held on Teams Wednesday 7 October 2026 - see Request for Tender for further information.

Submissions close 2pm Thursday 22 October 2026.

All questions and queries are to be asked through this VendorPanel platform

Kind regards Isaac Regional Council

title: EOI - ELECTRIC VEHICLE CHARGING IN CITY OF VINCENT CAR PARKS
description:
The City of Vincent is seeking experienced electric vehicle (EV) charging providers to install, operate and maintain public EV charging infrastructure across its car park portfolio.

The opportunity is intended to expand access to public charging, support the uptake of electric vehicles, and provide charging solutions that reflect the different parking durations and user needs across the City’s activity centres, recreation precincts and community destinations.

The City of Vincent invites suitably qualified proponents to submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) for the licensing of car parking bays within any of the 13 car parks listed within the attached document, for use as EV charging bays.

Please refer to the attached EOI document for all information - including how to submit a response.

The EOI closes at 2pm (WST) on Monday 19 October.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerAddress:
244 Vincent St
Leederville, Western Australia 6007
Australia
vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription: The City of Vincent is a local government area of Western Australia. It covers an area of approximately 10.4 square kilometres in metropolitan Perth, the capital of Western Australia, and lies about 3 km from the Perth CBD. The City of Vincent maintains 139 km of roads and 104 ha of parks and gardens.
vendorPanelDetails.queryCutoffAtRaw: Monday 19 October 2026 02:00 PM (W. Australia Standard Time)
vendorPanelDetails.background: Proponents may submit proposals for individual or multiple car parks but are not required to respond for every car park. A single provider will be appointed for each car park; however, the City may appoint different providers across its portfolio.
vendorPanelDetails.desiredOutcomes: Where feasible, the City prefers EV charging infrastructure to be connected via a dedicated electrical point of supply with separate metering. For appropriate locations, preference may be given to proposals offering a mix of charging technologies and speeds to meet a range of user needs.

publicQuestions.answer: The City has two tariffs. Please email joanna.jenkin@vincent.wa.gov.au and this information can be sent to you directly.

publicQuestions.question:
As part of our assessment of the proposed charging locations, could you please assist with the following information for Beatty Park, Loftus Street and William Street

1. Do you have current electrical single line diagrams (SLDs) for these sites?

2. Could you provide 12 months of interval meter data for the associated Western Power meters (ideally 30-minute interval data or higher resolution)?

3. If SLDs are not available for Loftus Street or William Street, could you please connect us with your electrician so we can discuss the existing metering set up?

4. Could you also provide the NMI(s) associated with the relevant meters?
publicQuestions.answer:
Please see the City's responses below:

Q1. Do you have current electrical single line diagrams (SLDs) for these sites?

A1. We only have SLDs for Beatty Park, please e-mail joanna.jenkin@vincent.wa.gov.au and they can be sent to you.

Q2. Could you provide 12 months of interval meter data for the associated Western Power meters (ideally 30-minute interval data or higher resolution)?

A2. Please e-mail joanna.jenkin@vincent.wa.gov.au and they can be sent to you (for all sites which have meters that are interval capable).

Q3. If SLDs are not available for Loftus Street or William Street, could you please connect us with your electrician so we can discuss the existing metering set up?

A3. Please email joanna.jenkin@vincent.wa.gov.au and we can send this information to you.

Q4. Could you also provide the NMI(s) associated with the relevant meters?

A4. Yes, please e-mail joanna.jenkin@vincent.wa.gov.au and they can be sent to you.

updates.description:
SITE INSPECTION REMINDER - TOMORROW 9:30AM WEDNESDAY 23 SEPTEMBER 2026:

As per the EOI, please email joanna.jenkin@vincent.wa.gov.au with the car park(s) you wish to inspect.

Please see below questions received at the site visits and the City's official responses:

BEATTY PARK:

Q1. Do you need to be careful of the trees when installing infrastructure?

A1. Yes. Please email joanna.jenkin@vincent.wa.gov.au and these can be sent to you.

Q2. Did they future proof the cabling?

A2. Not that we are aware of.

Q3. Who would be responsible for parking line markings and signage?

A3. The CPO would be responsible for completing the line markings and signage, after the City had approved the designs.

Q4. Are there any plans for redevelopment of the Beatty Park car park?

A4. Not at this time.

Q5. Where is the existing Beatty Park HV feeder located?

A5. The HV line runs along Vincent Street and cuts through Beatty Park Reserve (between the boundary of the car park and the oval). Specific connection would need to be confirmed with Western Power.

Q6. Do you need to be careful of the trees when installing infrastructure?

A6. Yes. The City’s priority is to retain trees. Where there is limited alternative, the approach which removes the fewest trees would be preferred. Once proposals are submitted, the Parks team will review the drawing and provide comment. Generally, a 1m setback from the tree trunk is preferred.

Q7. Are there any sites which are off limits?

A7. No. However, if you wanted to use the current ACROD bays, an appropriate plan to relocate them would need to be considered and approved.

Q8. Is the car park available for 24-hour access?

A8. Yes. There is 24-hour access to Beatty Park and the other locations at all times.

Q9. Would you be open to moving the staff car parking bays (Moriston Street end, south-west corner)?

A9. Yes.

Q10. Would the City entertain an expanding model?

A10. Yes. The City is open to an expanding proposal as part of the EOI.

Please see questions received at the site visit and the City's official responses:

LOFTUS:

Q1. Is Loftus car parking free?

A1. Yes. 3-hour limit between 8am and 8pm Monday-Friday; 5-hour limit between 8am and 8pm Saturday-Sunday. Vehicle registration is required at the ticket machine or via the Pay by Phone app.

Q2. Are there any off-limit car parks at Loftus?

A2. The large car park adjacent to Richmond Street (3P and 5P parking) would be the preferred location. The area directly outside the Library is 30-minute parking and the area further south outside the Community Centre / Loftus Recreation Centre is 90-minute parking. The preference is to leave these areas unchanged.

Q3. What is the current power draw on the transformer at Loftus Car Park?

A3. Capacity is indicative only and based on a high-level assessment of current network thermal capacity. Actual connection feasibility, timeframes and costs will depend on site-specific and network factors, including switchboard limitations, allocated capacity and planned network augmentations, and must be confirmed through Western Power's standard connection process.

A high-level estimation of the current transformer thermal capacity indicates that the transformer is being used at 50% of its 1000 kVA). However, this does not mean that the capacity is available for new customers. This would be determined as part of the Western Power application process.

Q4. Who would police the use of EV bays to prevent ICE vehicles parking in them?

A4. Rangers would be able to enforce the restrictions, provided the signage is correctly installed.

Please see questions received at the site visit and the City's official responses:

ALL CAR PARKS:

Q1. Do we need to bring our own power to potential sites?

A1. The City is open to applications that propose either a separate point of supply or the use of existing electrical capacity and infrastructure, where feasible. However, where a larger power draw is anticipated, a separate point of supply may be preferred.

Q2. What are the Council restrictions on the width of footpaths that must be maintained for access?

A2. 1.2m is the minimum, with 1.5m preferred where feasible. Please copy and paste the following into your browser for more information: https://www.ipwea.org/westernaustralia/viewdocument/planning-and-designing-for-pedestri?CommunityKey=dffe60b0-f7ea-4f24-8740-c55ce992edb9

Q3. What are the considerations for drainage when installing the infrastructure?

A3. Ideally, a 1.5m setback should be maintained for excavation works and the EV charging infrastructure should not obstruct drainage flows.

Please see the following update to two answers provided at the site visit:

BEATTY PARK:

Q5. Where is the existing Beatty Park HV feeder located?

UPDATE A5. The HV line runs along Vincent Street and cuts through Beatty Park Reserve (between the boundary of the car park and the oval). Specific connection would need to be confirmed. Please email joanna.jenkin@vincent.wa.gov.au for further details.

LOFTUS:

Q3. What is the current power draw on the transformer at Loftus Car Park?

UPDATED A3. Capacity is indicative only and based on a high-level assessment of current network thermal capacity. Actual connection feasibility, timeframes and costs will depend on site-specific and network factors, including switchboard limitations, allocated capacity and planned network augmentations, and must be confirmed through Western Power's standard connection process.

A high-level estimation of the current transformer thermal capacity indicates that the transformer is being used at 50% of its 1000 kVA). However, this does not mean that the capacity is available for new customers. Please email joanna.jenkin@vincent.wa.gov.au for further details.

Please see the attached document in relation to questions received and the City's formal responses.

Please consider this attachment when responding.

The services to be provided under this Contract include, but are not limited to, the following workstreams:

Workstream 1 – Minor Building Construction, Repairs and Maintenance

Covers the delivery of general building and construction services across the Principals assets, including minor capital works, reactive maintenance, emergency response works, renovations, structural repairs, general handyman services and small-scale infrastructure projects.

Workstream 2 - Building Certification, Statutory Compliance and Specialist Building Services

Provides specialist technical, advisory, inspection, compliance and certification services associated with Principal assets. Services may include building certification, statutory compliance inspections, building condition assessments, design review, drafting services, budget estimates, repair methodologies, engineering advice, technical reporting and specialist consultancy services relating to structural, hydraulic, mechanical, fire and aquatic infrastructure.

Covers the supply, installation, maintenance and repair of commercial flooring systems, including vinyl, carpet, epoxy coatings, polishing, sanding, and associated flooring services.

Includes the supply, installation, maintenance and repair of glazing and aluminium systems including windows, doors, shopfronts and emergency glass replacement.

Includes the supply, installation and maintenance of blinds, awnings, drapes, tinting, frosting and associated window covering systems.

Provides furniture relocation, storage, internal moves, inter-site relocations and associated furniture handling services.

In response to Notice to Respondents No. 1, the Contractor requests clarification on the following:

1. Allocation of roads to Schedules 1A, 1B, 2A and 2B

Schedule 6 – Att 2 – Schedule of Rates provides total quantities only. It does not identify the roads or areas associated with each schedule. Clause 7.6 of RFT000143_Schedule_5 – Att_1 – Technical Specification states that possession of site will be awarded on a road-by-road basis in accordance with the Contractor's program. Without knowing which roads fall under each schedule, the Contractor cannot develop a realistic program or accurately price:

a. Haulage

b. Travel, and lost time between work areas

c. Traffic control

d. Site compounds and laydown areas

e. Water supply

f. Disposal of mixed debris and surplus material

g. Seal mobilisations

The Contractor requests that the Principal provide a list or map of the roads (with chainages where available) associated with each schedule. If final locations are not yet confirmed, the Contractor requests an indicative list of roads, or a nominated geographic area, to be used as a common pricing basis for all tenderers.

2. Extent and size of patches

The Schedule of Rates does not state the number, size or distribution of the patches making up each scheduled quantity. The rate per unit varies considerably between a small number of large patches and a large number of small, dispersed ones, both in production and in mobilisation.

The Contractor requests an indicative patch schedule for each schedule item, showing approximate location, size and number of discrete sites. Alternatively, the Principal could confirm an assumed average patch size and number of sites for pricing purposes.

3. Gravel supply and haulage

There are five TMR-registered quarries within the Gympie Regional Council area. Additional viable sources exist in neighbouring local government areas, and which of these is suitable depends on where the works are located. Without work locations, the Contractor cannot select the most economical source for each area or optimise haulage across the program.

The Contractor requests that, until locations are provided, the Principal either:

•	nominate an assumed average haul distance for pricing, or

•	confirm whether haulage will be measured and paid separately.

For example, Item No 92501.0X Heavy formation grading incorporating 50mm imported material is scheduled at 24,645 m³ [comprised of Schedule 1A = 7,567.8m3 | Schedule 1B = 976m3 | Schedule 2A = 14,660m3 | Schedule 2B = 1,441m3] against 82,266 m³ listed (30%), and Item No 91003.0X Heavy formation grading at 23,331 m [comprised of Schedule 1A = 3,959m | Schedule 1B = 2,752m | Schedule 2A = 12,775m3 | Schedule 2B = 3,845m3] against 74,121 m listed (31%). The scheduled works are therefore a selected subset of the listed damages, and tenderers have no information on which roads or damages make up that subset.

This is critical to pricing. Under Clause 7.6 of Sch 5 – Att 1 – Technical Specification, possession of site is awarded on a road-by-road basis. Without knowing which roads, or how many, make up the scheduled quantities, the Tenderer cannot assume continuous and concurrent deployment of multiple crews (drainage, grading, patching and pothole repair). Works must therefore be programmed and priced on a road-by-road basis. The resulting unit rates differ materially depending on whether the scheduled quantities are delivered:

•	as complete scopes on a smaller number of selected roads, with concentrated works and fewer mobilisations; or

•	as a portion of the damages dispersed across the full network, with small, scattered sites and high travel, set-up and traffic control costs for each unit of work.

Without a defined basis, each tenderer will adopt its own assumption, and submitted rates will not be comparable.

The Tenderer requests that Council:

1.	Hold an open tender meeting with all respondents to establish a common basis for programming and pricing; or

2.	Alternatively, provide by Notice to Respondents the following:

o	an indicative list of the roads, or Att 4 & 5 damage IDs, that make up the scheduled quantities for each of Schedules 1A, 1B, 2A and 2B to enable development of pricing and program; or

Given the closing date of 15 October 2026, the Tenderer also asks Council to consider an extension if a meeting or further information cannot be provided in time for tenderers to reflect it in their submissions.

description:
Ipswich City Council is Requesting Expressions of Interest (ROEI) for a Process Mapping Solution.

Council is seeking to better understand contemporary solutions available in the market that enable the creation, management, publication and maintenance of business process documentation while promoting user engagement and organisational consistency.

Please see the attached ROEI documentation for further information.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
Ipswich is centrally located in the booming south east Queensland region of Australia. To the east is the capital city Brisbane, and to the west are the rural and agricultural areas of the Brisbane, Lockyer and Fassifern Valleys. The city is ideally positioned on the national road network - 40 minutes drive from Brisbane, an hours drive from the Gold Coast and 60 minutes drive from domestic and international air and sea ports.
Ipswich comprises an area of 1090 square kms and has a population of 180,000 people. Ipswich enjoys a subtropical climate and is a safe, friendly and multicultural city. Residents come from 115 different ethnic backgrounds, speaking 84 languages.
As Queensland's oldest provincial city, Ipswich has a rich history. It is renowned for its architectural, natural and cultural heritage. Ipswich proudly preserves and still operates from many of its historical buildings and homes, with more than 6000 heritage-listed sites. Ipswich also has a range of charming townships within the western rural areas of the city, each with its own legitimate claims of historical significance.

title: DLGWV2026-0351 Design and Construction of the Mapoon New Treated Water Reservoir Project
description:
The Department of Local Government, Water and Volunteers (DLGWV) is seeking to engage a suitably qualified and experienced contractor to undertake the Design and Construction of the Mapoon New Treated Water Reservoir Project. The works includes geotechnical investigations and surveying to support the design of a new treated water reservoir and future upgrades to the Water Treatment Plant (WTP). The scope of works also includes the demolition and removal of the existing steel structure, relocation of two sheds for repurposing by Council, remediation of the existing 1.2 ML concrete reservoir, and the design, supply, delivery, construction, installation, testing, commissioning, and performance testing of a new treated water reservoir.

A non-mandatory Industry Briefing will be held at 10:30am AEST, 16 September 2026. title: Atherton Hospital Upgrades - Design and Construct Building Contractor
description:
The State of Queensland through Queensland Health, Health Infrastructure Queensland (HIQ) on behalf of Cairns and Hinterland Hospital and Health Service (CHHHS) is undertaking the procurement of a suitably qualified Design and Construct Building Contractor to deliver the Atherton Hospital Upgrades (the Project).

The Atherton Hospital Upgrade Program comprises a series of interconnected infrastructure projects designed to improve clinical service delivery, enhance patient outcomes, address infrastructure deficiencies, and support the future healthcare needs of the Atherton community and surrounding Tablelands region.

The Atherton Hospital Upgrade Program consists of the following projects:

•	25 Bed Ward Refurbishment;

•	Oncology Refurbishment;

•	New Morgue Building;

•	High Dependency Unit (HDU); and

•	Pathology Refurbishment.

The program includes the refurbishment and expansion of key clinical facilities within Atherton Hospital, together with the construction of new supporting infrastructure to improve service capability, operational efficiency, patient safety, and staff wellbeing. The projects have been developed in response to increasing service demand, ageing infrastructure, evolving healthcare models, and the need to provide contemporary, fit-for-purpose healthcare environments that support high-quality patient care.

Tenderers are invited to attend a site inspection on Wednesday 26 August 2026. Attendance at this meeting is non-mandatory but highly desirable.

'For detailed information on the specific goods / services sought under this Invitation to Tender, please review the "Request for Offer" documentation.

publicQuestions.answer:
Preventative maintenance must be carried out to an extent that no more than two service call-outs are carried out per year (Service A and B in returnable schedule 2 - Price),

but also no less than would be appropriate to prevent failures.

As example:

 - if an activity is required every 2 weeks, price for it in Service A and B, which implies 6 monthly

 - if an activity is required every 3 months, price for it in Service A and B, which implies 6 monthly

Preventative maintenance activities in scope are the same as that which would be required by OEM.

title: MICC Road Construction and Maintenance (RoPS)
description:
Mount Isa City Council (the Principal) invites Tenders from suitably qualified Tenderers for selection as a pre-qualified supplier of road construction and maintenance as described in more detail in Part 5 – Scope.

The principle intends to establish the register of pre-qualified suppliers and to subsequently invite quotations for particular work packages from selected pre-qualified suppliers.

Successful Tenderers may be required to work with gravel, limestone, road base, bituminous products, asphalt, concrete and other construction materials used by the principle in the construction of roads, drainage and reserves and other assets.

The City of Mount Isa is a local government area in north west Queensland. The City covers the urban locality of Mount Isa, the administrative center, and surrounding area, sharing a boundary with the Northern Territory to the west.

Mount Isa is a reasonably affluent district. The largest industry in the City is the Mount Isa Mines, a source of lead, copper, silver and zinc. Cattle grazing and tourism are other industries of note.

title: Bairnsdale Aerodrome Runway 04/22 Upgrade - Design and Construct
description: Council requires the Bairnsdale Aerodrome Runway 04/22 to be designed and constructed as a CASA Part 139 (Aerodromes) MOS-compliant Code 3 runway that safely accommodates the confirmed design aircraft and forecast operations. publicQuestions.question:
Ref B1 Runway CMP.PDF:

Is stockpile of material proposed to be re-used permitted in the “Restricted Zone” Drg 2466/6002, and are construction vehicles permitted with the “Restricted Zone”, as it is likely to be traversed during construction, if not does EGSC have a nominated parcel of lane allocated with the Aerodrome boundary for the purpose of stockpiling of materials for re-use.
publicQuestions.answer: Stockpile of material and construction vehicles are permitted in the sections of the “Restricted Zone” Drg 2466/6002 that do not have native vegetation, and in the sections of the “Restricted Zone” Drg 2466/6002 that are part of the “Vegetation proposed for removal” (Figure 3.2 of Appendix D3_Flora and Fauna assessment). The words “Restricted zone” in Drg 2466/6002 should read “Proposed Limit of Contractor’s work zone”. Drawing 2466/6002 is for information only, it is not the approved Contractor's Construction Management Plan under contract CON2027 1810.

publicQuestions.question:
Temporary Site Accommodation/Facilities-Site Office

Does EGSC have a nominated parcel of land within the Aerodrome boundary for the establishment of temporary site facilities; Office, Lunchroom, WC facilities, etc, and a nominated access point for construction activities, eg. Aerodrome Road or Main Entrance via Bengworden Road (SOW – Contractor (D&C) Section 3.3
publicQuestions.answer: Council does not have a nominated parcel of land for the establishment of temporary site facilities. Tenderers will propose the most suitable location for temporary site facilities in line with their methodology and the site constraints. Access points are nominated in Part 3 Scope of works Section 3.3. Tenderers are encouraged to attend the onsite tender briefing to assess site constraints and opportunities.

publicQuestions.question:
Fencing – PPR

Can EGSC provide a Standard Drawing associated with Site Fencing, Section 5, #11 Perimeter Fencing – High Security, and Drawing No. B3-Proposed Fencing.PDF.
publicQuestions.answer: Part 3 Scope of works and Part 3 Appendix A PPR contain relevant fencing details. Fencing design is part of the Contractor's scope of works under contract CON2027 1810.

publicQuestions.question:
Good afternoon,

1. Can Council provide the aircraft traffic mix to be adopted for pavement design? The project documentation currently nominates the total annual aircraft movements but does not appear to provide a breakdown by aircraft type.
publicQuestions.answer:
Based on current activity, the following forecast aircraft traffic mix can be adopted for the pavement design of Runway 04-22:

- Beechcraft King Air 260/360 and Turbo Commander 690A: 2,200 annual departures

- Air Tractor AT802 and PZL-M18 Dromader: 1,500 annual departures

- RAAus: 1,500 annual departures

- General Aviation mix (including PA31 and C172): 850 annual departures

- PC-12 and Beechcraft 1900: 150 annual departures

- Heavy helicopters (AW139/Blackhawk): up to 300 annual departures

- Q400 (not currently using the aerodrome): 260 annual departures

publicQuestions.question:
Good afternoon,

Can Council confirm if the preference is for a spray seal or asphalt wearing surface for the runway works?
publicQuestions.answer: Council's preference is for a two-coat spray seal wearing course.

publicQuestions.question:
B1 Runway CMP

It is noted that Drg 2466/6003 shows areas of Protected Vegetation (Blue Scatter/Hatching); however based on the Reference Design Cross Section, these areas are subject to filling to bring existing surface levels to finished surface levels; as the new Runway FSL are higher the Runway ESL. The area of Protected Vegetation would need to be stripped, fill constructed and FSL topsoiled and seeding. Is this operation permitted within the Protected Vegetation Zone.?
publicQuestions.answer:
Drg 2466/6003 - the Blue colour shows some of the native vegetation currently protected under the EPBC Act. Some of this native vegetation will be impacted by the works under the permits that Council is currently seeking. Contractors should not rely on the part-complete CMP for native vegetation matters due to lack of clarity. CAD files have been provided as follows:

The EcoFeatures CAD file provided in Appendix D provides the extent of the native vegetation at the aerodrome (layer "Habitat Zone_EVC" and "Scattered trees"). Most of the native vegetation is currently protected under the EPBC Act (layer "EPBC").

The VegetationRemoval CAD file provided in Appendix D provides the extent of the native vegetation that Council and its Contractors will be able to remove once the three permits have been granted to Council (permit under the EPBC Act, FFG permit and Planning permit for the removal of native vegetation). Native vegetation that is not shown in the VegetationRemoval CAD file cannot be impacted by the Works.

Note: The VegetationRemoval CAD file does not show several scattered trees that will need to be lopped/removed for OLS purpose, however it is anticipated that the planning permit (once issued) will allow for those trees needed to be lopped or removed.

publicQuestions.question:
Stormwater Drainage

Can EGSC please confirm, consistent with Notes on Detail Layout Plan, that the existing stormwater infrastructure is abandoned, left in place, not excavated, removed and backfill, but rather pits and pipes left in situ but not able to allow ingress of water/run-off.?
publicQuestions.answer: Any existing stormwater infrastructure within future runway pavement areas and 10 metres either side of the future runway pavement areas needs to be removed and disposed off as part of the scope of works under this Contract. For existing stormwater infrastructure outside of the future runway pavement areas and 10 metres either side, the Contractor can consider alternative decommissioning options.

publicQuestions.question:
Airport Traffic:

Can EGSC please confirm the below with regards to air traffic use of the runway and taxiway:

1.	Daily schedule for RPT and

2.	Number of movements of GA aircraft
publicQuestions.answer:
1. There is no current daily schedule for RPT at Bairnsdale Aerodrome.

2. The current number of GA aircarft is not recorded, however there is an estimated 3500 annual departure in 2025 for Bairnsdale Aerodrome with activity progressively increasing each year.

Forecast traffic mix are different from the information provided above.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi

Respectfully we would like to request an extension to the closing date.

Given the complexities of this project and the requirements for design we would like to request a 3-week extension.

Thanks
publicQuestions.answer: Thank you for your request. Unfortunately, we are unable to grant an extension to the closing date due to our project timelines. We appreciate your understanding and look forward to receiving your submission.

publicQuestions.question: Please confirm whether the Principal requires the Contractor to provide a dedicated Work Safety Officers (WSO) for the duration of the works.
publicQuestions.answer: The Principal will provide a dedicated Work Safety Officers (WSO) for the duration of the works. However, Tenderers are welcome to include provision for a Work Safety Officer in the “Dayworks Rates”.

publicQuestions.question:
The tender documentation indicates new airside security fencing as part of the works.

The tenderer has assumed the required fencing standard is 2.1 m high chainmesh fencing incorporating three strands of barbed wire and cranked (cogged) tops (total height 2.4m), consistent with typical regional airport airside security fencing requirements.

Please confirm the required fencing specification, including fence height, security topping arrangement, gate requirements and any applicable airport security standards.
publicQuestions.answer:
The following requirements apply:

- 2.1m high chainmesh fencing

- three strands of barbed wire

- total height 2.4m

- three vehicle access gates are required. One on each end (04 end & 22 end), one at the end of RWY 31.

publicQuestions.question:
The tender documents nominate two new windsocks to satisfy the Part 139 MOS requirements for an instrument runway.

Based on the required placement location and the OLS setback requirements, the Runway 22 windsock appears to be positioned within an area identified as native vegetation that cannot be impacted by the works.

Please confirm whether environmental approvals for the windsock installation and associated works (electrical cabling) have been considered and included within the environmental approvals
publicQuestions.answer:
Council requires the design to meet the requirements of CASA Part 139 (Aerodromes) Manual of Standards 2019. For information, Bairnsdale Airport has an Illuminated Wind Directional Indicator (primary), and secondary unlit wind indicator, and an Aerodrome Weather Information Service unit (AWIS) which is a Bureau of Meteorology approved weather observing system which provides meteorological weather information broadcast.

The native vegetation that can be impacted by the Works once the permits are granted is shown on Appendix D5.

title: Design and Construction (D&C) of New Social Housing – Palm Island
description:
Palm Island Aboriginal Shire Council (Council) is seeking to engage one or more suitably qualified and experienced Contractors to undertake the Design and Construction (D&C) of 22 new social housing dwellings across multiple sites on Palm Island, Queensland, together with an optional additional Package comprising two (2) dwellings.

The core Works are divided into five (5) Packages, comprising 22 dwellings and 86 bedrooms. An additional Optional Package 6 comprises two (2) dwellings and eight (8) bedrooms. Tenderers may submit a Tender Response for one, several or all Packages, subject to their demonstrated capacity to deliver the Packages tendered.

The Contract is intended to provide Council with a turnkey delivery solution, under which the Contractor is responsible for all investigations, design development, engineering, certification, building approvals, procurement, manufacture where applicable, transportation, mobilisation, construction, site and infrastructure works, utility connections, testing, commissioning, statutory certification, documentation and handover necessary to provide completed, compliant and fully operational dwellings ready for occupation and handover to the Department of Housing and Public Works (DHPW), except for matters expressly identified as Council responsibilities.

Council's objective is for all dwellings to achieve Practical Completion and be ready for handover to DHPW by 31 December 2027.

Council will provide Reference Designs establishing the design intent and minimum functional and performance requirements. The Contractor will be responsible for developing and completing the design and may propose design optimisation, including prefabricated, modular, panelised or other off-site construction methodologies, subject to satisfying the requirements of this Specification, the Principal's Requirements and DHPW requirements.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
Palm Island Aboriginal Shire Council is delivering a program of new social housing on Palm Island in collaboration with the Queensland Department of Housing and Public Works (DHPW).

This procurement comprises the design and construction of 22 new social housing dwellings, providing a total of 86 bedrooms across five (5) Packages and multiple sites on Palm Island.

Package 6 (2 new social housing) is optional. Council may, in its absolute discretion, elect whether or not to proceed with and award Package 6.

Palm Island, also known as Great Palm Island, or by the Aboriginal name Bwgcolman, is the largest of twelve tropical Islands in the Palm Island Group. The settlement is named variously Palm Island, the Mission, Palm Island Settlement or Palm Community.

The group of Islands is less than 20 kilometres from the nearest point on the mainland (Lucinda) and is 65 kilometres north of Townsville over sea. The Islands are serviced by a 20 minute plane ride or one and a half hour ferry ride from Townsville and a one hour barge trip from Lucinda.

Palm Island consists of small bays, sandy beaches, fringing reefs, beautiful freshwater streams and steep forested mountains rising to the highest peak of 548 metres at Bentley Ridge. Other islands in the chain, such as Orpheus and North Palm have globally renowned resorts and marine research stations. Situated in the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park, the surrounding reefs are as good as any on the outer reef, presenting wonderful fishing and diving opportunities and are used extensively by locals for hunting and gathering and other cultural purposes.

Palm Island is the largest discreet Indigenous community in Australia with approximately 4,000 people residing on Palm Island. There is high mobility between Palm Island and the mainland, and the population can increase to over 5,000 people during festivals and events. There are seven suburbs on the Island, running from Butler Bay in the south to Wallaby Point in the north, with the main, central settlement area, The Mission having the mall, shops, service centres, police station, motel, hospital and health service and Council chambers. Critical services infrastructure, including the Council’s works depots, waste and recycling facility, (Ergon) power station, water and sewer treatment plants, and two water supply reservoirs are at The Farm area, Solomon and Wallaby Point.

title: Coaching and Development Panel
description:
Queensland Rail invites suitably qualified and experienced suppliers to submit a tender for inclusion on a Coaching & Development Panel.

The panel will support Queensland Rail's commitment to developing leadership capability and workforce effectiveness across both operational and corporate environments. Successful suppliers will partner with Queensland Rail to deliver high-quality coaching and professional development services that build organisational capability, support career progression, and enhance leadership effectiveness across the business.

The panel arrangement will be established for an initial period of two (2) years, with options to extend at Queensland Rail's discretion.

Suppliers may submit proposals for one or both of the following service categories:

Category 1: Coaching Services

Provision of individual and group coaching services designed to support employees and leaders at various organisational levels, including leadership development, performance improvement, career progression, and succession readiness.

Category 2: Professional Development Workshops

Design and delivery of engaging, practical and innovative professional development workshops aligned to Queensland Rail's capability and leadership development objectives.

Suppliers should clearly articulate their methodologies, experience, and areas of specialisation, including how their services align with Queensland Rail's Capability and Level of Work Frameworks.

title: Statewide Waste and Recycling Infrastructure Roadmap
description:
The Queensland government Less Landfill, More Recycling 2035: Queensland Waste Strategy identifies investing in modern infrastructure as a priority. The new Waste Strategy is backed by investment of $487 million over five years through the Waste Reduction and Recycling Activation Fund. However, investment in infrastructure requires not just State government investment, but local, federal and private sector investment as well.

A key action of the Waste Strategy is to develop a statewide waste and recycling infrastructure plan that identifies current and future material flows, infrastructure capacity and gaps, facility locations, supply chain options, land use planning considerations and priority investment opportunities.

In collaboration with the Department, the supplier will produce two complementary outputs: a Statewide Waste and Recycling Infrastructure Roadmap and a supporting Investment Prospectus. Together, these outputs will provide a contemporary, evidence-based framework to guide decision-making on priority waste streams, recycling and resource recovery infrastructure to 2035 and beyond and help identify key infrastructure needs and costed pathways to progress towards the targets in the Waste Strategy.

title: Canungra Work Base Design and Construction
description:
The Department of the Environment, Tourism, Science and Innovation, Queensland Parks and Wildlife Service (QPWS) invite suitably qualified suppliers to submit an offer for the P264127 - Canungra Work Base Design and Construction project.

This procurement seeks a suitably qualified and experienced Principal Contractor to deliver design and construction of a new work base at Canungra, consisting of one shed (24m x 12m) with cantilevered awning (4m), and one new office (16m x 8m), accommodating 13 desk spaces, kitchen, bathroom, and meeting room. This project includes all service connections, driveways, car parks, fencing, and soft scaping.

This is a Prequalification (PQC) System project. Tenderers must be on the relevant PQC list by the Tender Closing Date and Time. The PQC criteria are:

o	Procurement system contract category: Design and Construct – Single Stage

o	Service category: New Construction Work / Addition

o	Project type: Low rise - up to and including three storeys

o	Areas of operation: Moreton South/Gold Coast

o	Required office location: Brisbane, Moreton South/Gold Coast

o	Service activities: General Building: Low - conventional design incorporating commonly used trades (eg a school building)

**Important Dates**

Last date for Supplier Clarifications: 5:00pm Queensland Time on Monday, 2 November 2026

Tender Closing Date: 5:00pm Queensland Time on Friday, 6 November 2026

Minimum eligibility requirements are as follows:

• QBCC Licensing, registration and accreditation

• Copy of Certificate of Currency of required insurance policies

• Attendance at the mandatory site meeting

• Registration on the relevant Prequalification System (PQC) eligible list by the tender closing date and time.

Tenderers are advised that the following may apply to the project:

• Building Industry Fairness (Security of Payment) Act 2017 Project Trust Accounts

• Occupational Health and Safety Audits for Queensland Government building projects

Mandatory Site Visit

This Request for Tender has a mandatory site visit on Tuesday, 13 October 2026

Please register for the site visit via email no later than 5:00pm on Friday, 9 October 2026.

Registration details required are company name, name of attendee/s, contact number and email of attendee/s. Each company is restricted to two representatives.

title: Pedestrian Operated Signals – Swan Hill
description:
Swan Hill Rural City Council (Council) is undertaking pedestrian safety improvements within the Swan Hill CBD through the installation of raised pedestrian operated signals at three key locations.

The project forms part of Council’s program of infrastructure works and is intended to provide compliant pedestrian crossing infrastructure within busy urban areas. The works will be undertaken on existing road networks where maintaining safe access and minimising disruption to pedestrians, businesses, residents and road users will be important throughout construction.

Due to the specialised nature of the works, delivery requires a suitably experienced and Department of Transport and Planning (DTP) accredited contractor, with all works to comply with relevant DTP/TAC standards and requirements.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription: Swan Hill Rural City Council, "The Heart of the Murray" is a bustling provincial centre just three and a half hours from Melbourne and five and a half hours from Adelaide.The region is renowned for its world class produce, spectacular landscapes and close proximity to the Murray River. Our region runs adjacent to the Murray River for nearly 200 kilometres and encompasses 6,000 square kilometres and home to 20,000 people.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
Council is seeking a suitably qualified and experienced contractor to undertake pedestrian operated signal (POS) works at three locations within the Swan Hill CBD:

•	Site 1: Beveridge Street – adjacent to Coles (Package 1)

•	Site 2: Campbell Street – near the Commercial Hotel (Package 2)

•	Site 3: Campbell Street – near Arc Expresso (Package 7)

Works are to be appropriately staged to minimise disruption to traffic movements within Swan Hill and to ensure that all affected areas are not restricted simultaneously.

Council’s preference is for works at Site 1 and Site 2 to be undertaken concurrently using separate resources, followed by the works at Site 7.
